The read-back once, on 700, deriving from 383 and 1,789 and not from 423 and 1,989. The count of the three columns of the page of routes once, on 700. The volume's question once, on 700, answered by nobody. The document under a seal read out once, on 696, the name under the seal in no mouth. The Crown Keel seen once, on 699, not understood, no figure, nobody going to look.**

**THE LONGEST COMMON CONTIGUOUS RUN ACROSS THE TEN IS 170 WORDS, BETWEEN 693 AND 695, AND IT IS THE HEAD OF THE LOCK-REQUIRED MONEY ARITHMETIC. It is ruled for the owner of the form at `reviews/volume-13/volume-13-close.md` § 23 and was not cut.**

### THE TEN CHAPTERS

**691, Saturday the eleventh day of June, day 41, 424 / 1,994, the hearing on its hundred and eighty-ninth day.** The boat of about thirty tons comes back alongside the third lay at about eight with her own gear still aboard her and nobody asks where she has been. All five of the people who went down off that mole on the eighth are back in their own communities by about ten and five towns go down on that page with no name against any of them, and not one of the five is asked what it was like. The coil the woman of about thirty-three hung on its own nail comes off it at about half past ten and nobody saw her take it and nobody asked her. **The man of about thirty-two sleeps from about ten on Friday night until about five, the first sleep in three nights, finishes two cups of water, says the aftertaste has not lifted and that the knee is not worse, and no figure of money stands against any hour of it.** The woman of thirty of no office asks whether a page of days may be read out on those boards in front of people who cannot read it. Slip 579 words.

**692, Sunday the twelfth day of June, day 42, 425 / 1,999, the hearing on its hundred and ninetieth day.** **A wipe, the hundred and tenth, 27/14/27 = 68, from about ten past ten to about eighteen minutes past eleven.** That is seven Sundays of those figures and nobody has said why it is getting slower. A man of about thirty-one of the second lay stops at the bottom of that lane, says he has noticed, says he is not saying anything about it, and is written down as having noticed and not as being right. The biggest gap on the sheet of fourteen is three thousand six hundred pence bigger than it was a week ago and that is a gap getting bigger. The page of hands is not on the end stall and has not been since the first of May. The man of about thirty-two walks down to the end stall at about ten past three, stands at it about four minutes, reads nothing because there is nothing new on it, and goes back by the rail. Slip 612 words.

**693, Monday the thirteenth day of June, day 43, 426 / 2,004, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-first day.** **A rota day carrying no charge, the fifteenth of the fifteen, being down to the stones in the bottom of it at about eight, four buckets filled out of what was left and put back, the covers going on at about nine.** At about eleven the man who keeps the leaf takes the leaf off its nail with the shed empty, reads the four columns straight down, puts his thumb on the third column, and writes nothing, rubs nothing out, appoints nobody and closes nothing. The man of about thirty-two is given the leaf for as long as he wants it, looks at the fourth column for about six minutes, says one sentence, being that it is still standing open at one hundred and twenty-five and that nobody has shut it and nobody has struck it, and says nothing at all about the third. The man who hires hands leaves four names on the bench and says one of the four men is not coming back this week and is telling them and not asking them. Slip 556 words.

**694, Tuesday the fourteenth day of June, day 44, 427 / 2,009, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-second day.** **The eighty-sixth wage Tuesday.** The lid is read out at about ten in four minutes and does not move, the chest with the twenty envelopes stands shut from ten until four, and the eighty-sixth week stands fallen due at the close of the day behind the eighty-fifth. **A clerk out of the office on the west basin leaves a register copy of ten days, Monday the fourth of June through Wednesday the thirteenth, a hundred and sixty-eight pence on each of them including both Sundays, and it is the first time anybody has shown that yard where the figure it says out loud every day comes from.** The keeper asks whether the office keeps a column of what it owes and the clerk says that it does not. The register copy goes into the hands of the woman of thirty of no office because it is a municipal paper and this yard is not putting one on a page of days. A man of about fifty-six who lands fish asks whether the eighty-sixth week is bigger than the eighty-fifth and is told that the lid does not carry it. Slip 628 words.

**695, Wednesday the fifteenth day of June, day 45, 428 / 2,014, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-third day.** The page of the twenty-eighth of May has carried six lines for the eighteen days it has been up with nothing underneath any of them. **The man of about thirty-two and the woman of thirty of no office are both in that shed at about eleven in about nine people, neither sent for the other, and neither speaks to the other between eleven and four.** Four people ask the keeper separately between two and three whether it is settled and get the same answer four times, and all four of them ask what it would take and are told that nobody knows. **At about half past three a seventh line goes on that page under the woman of about twenty-seven's own line and under neither of the first two, and it says she has read the two lines above hers again and does not know which is right and is not changing hers and is still not going to be the one who decides.** Nothing came off any of the six lines. Slip 590 words.

**696, Thursday the sixteenth day of June, day 46, 429 / 2,019, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-fourth day.** **A rota day and the hundred and fifty-eighth charge, in eleven trips by hand between about eight and about eleven.** At about one a paper with a seal on it comes ashore off a boat out of the west basin and lies face down on that bench for an hour and a half. **At about half past two it is read out once on the boards at the back of that market by a man of about thirty-three who hires hands, in front of about twenty people of whom about eleven cannot read it, and it is not read out a second time.** It requires a named living custodian on every line carrying a testimony out of that harbor, named in writing and kept at the port, with a boat's account of what it carried and when kept and produced, and it is sealed at the bottom and is to be complied with from the first day of the following month. **It is correct and it costs a person and nobody in that market said it was wrong.** **The name under the seal is on the paper and is in no mouth on any day of the fifty.** Slip 644 words.

**697, Friday the seventeenth day of June, day 47, 430 / 2,024, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-fifth day.** At about eleven a man who hires hands says in about twenty words that there is a boat standing off the point that is not one of the nine, that she is lying still, and that he is not going to describe her, and asks for it on that page. **The yard does not go and does not send anybody and writes on the page that it will not go tomorrow either and does not know how it will not go the day after.** Four people ask what it is going to do about it and are told it is not going to do anything about it, and one of them asks whether it is not interested and is told that it is not uninterested and that it is not going, and that those are two different things. The page of routes is not counted on this day. A coil comes back onto its own nail at about half past two and nothing is said. Slip 603 words.

**698, Saturday the eighteenth day of June, day 48, 431 / 2,029, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-sixth day.** **At about eleven the wooden tally slate that has lain flat on that bench stone since the first of May is turned over where it lies, with four fingers on its edge and without being lifted, and four groups of strokes cut into the other side, older than this yard, with no name and no day against any of them.** Nothing is rubbed out and nothing is written on it and it is turned back the same way at about one and nobody asks what the strokes mean. At about two four people look at that wall from the floor: two lines and about eleven inches of empty plaster between them, empty since the twentieth of May, and nothing on it is counted. **At about half past three the page of hands is on the bench stone in front of about four people and stands at fifteen, and the four names that came off it in May are off it, with the day and the hour of the fall on the face of the page and the old figures still legible underneath.** Slip 687 words.

**699, Sunday the nineteenth day of June, day 49, 432 / 2,034, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-seventh day.** **A wipe, the hundred and eleventh, 28/15/28 = 71, from about ten past ten to about twenty-one minutes past eleven.** A boat goes out off that mole at about half past eleven with about nine people on her deck and at about half past one they see, for about two minutes, **a hull of a size that is not in this harbor's water, going slowly, not one of the nine, seen from the side and from a little abaft her beam, with nobody going below her and nobody going above her and nobody getting a line out.** Two of the four men who come past the yard are asked one question each on their own way up the lane and both say they did not know. **No figure of money and no figure of time is set against her, nobody puts a figure on what it would cost, and the yard writes on that page that it did not go and did not send anybody and did not go up the coast road to ask.** Slip 689 words.

**700, Monday the twentieth day of June, day 50, 433 / 2,039, the hearing on its hundred and ninety-eighth day. A rota day and the hundred and fifty-ninth charge.** **At about two in the afternoon the man who keeps the leaf reads that leaf out loud in the open at the flat of that bench stone, all four columns including the empty third, twice, in about nine people of whom about five cannot read a column, with both definitions in the same words and the same mouth as every other read-back and with its own derivation printed on the face of the reading.** The base of that derivation is three hundred and eighty-three and one thousand seven hundred and eighty-nine at the close of the first of May and not the figures of the tenth of June, and the keeper says out loud that he did not take them off last Friday's figures. **The count at the hour of that reading is four hundred and thirty-two and two thousand and thirty-seven and none and one hundred and twenty-five, and at the close of the day it is four hundred and thirty-three and two thousand and thirty-nine and none and one hundred and twenty-five.** At about half past three **the count of the three columns of the page of routes is written down for the second of twice**, one held, four restricted and four dormant over nine names with the held one the Saltmarch Weatherway alone, and it is not said out loud and is not in the slip. **At about half past four a woman of about forty-four with a chandler's counter asks, once, at the end stall of that market, in about eleven people, naming no person, when the last connection cannot be cut safely can a man stay connected on his own terms without putting one person's testimony back in the middle of the world, and nobody answers her, and it goes into that market's book as asked with the hour against it and no name against it.** The closing block carries the four columns, the fitting-out sheet with its two lines, the proof still in its case, the restricted remainder still sealed and the claim neither exercised nor released, the two lines and the empty plaster, four names gone off the page of hands, the hole in the Tuesday still a hole, and the bag with twenty-eight pence in it. Slip 966 words.

### 1. THE BATCH, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

**Sunday the twenty-second of May to Tuesday the thirty-first, ten consecutive days, one day to a chapter, no day missing and no day in two chapters. Two wipes, being the hundred and seventh at twenty-four off and eleven bare and twenty-four back, fifty-nine the whole of it, and the hundred and eighth at twenty-five and twelve and twenty-five, sixty-two the whole of it, and the wall behind a reeve's bench is now a minute slower than it was a fortnight ago and this yard has stopped asking the two men who do it. Two wage Tuesdays, the eighty-third and the eighty-fourth, the column at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks and unmoved on both, the chest with the twenty envelopes in it shut from ten until four on both, and the eighty-fourth week fallen due at the close of the last day. A new sheet went up on that wall on the Monday, the page of that week, with seven days down the side of it, and it carried ten lines by the close of the ten days and was read out every evening whatever was on it. A man of about fifty of the Lowfen Reed's own third lay said at a stall that his route was one man short on Wednesday night and would not ask anybody in that yard; he asked a woman of about forty of the Cinder Bell's own community himself, in nine people, and she said yes, with four clauses about non-ownership in her own mouth before anybody had written a word, and four of her own people were on the water for about seven hours under the Reed's own orders, and that yard asked nobody, sent for nobody, hired nobody, paid nobody and went with nobody. A man of about fifty-three put eleven words he wrote a long time ago on the Friday line of that page beside the Thursday line, and nobody answered them and no figure is set against them and he was not told he was wrong. Two people who are married each wrote one line in the middle of the Saturday line of that page, neither named in the other's line, and four other people wrote one line each under them, and it is not settled. A count of nights carried was taken off a second sheet of days at about three on the Tuesday afternoon in front of four people who came on their own account, and it was not said out loud and it is not in any slip. The bag is at twenty-eight pence, the fitting-out sheet is at one hundred and eleven thousand eight hundred and seventy-six pence out against ten thousand six hundred and forty in, and it carries one line and no second, and no line went onto it.**

### 2. THE TEN CHAPTER SUMMARIES

**671 — Sunday the twenty-second day of May, day twenty-one, a wipe, the hundred and seventh, 24/11/24 = 59.** Two men took the wall behind a reeve's bench off its holders at about ten past ten and it was bare by about half past ten and back at about nine minutes past eleven, at the angle it has carried since the twelfth of January, and it did not go up whole. A minute longer each way and a minute longer bare than the Sunday before, and nobody in the harbor has said why and this yard has stopped asking the two men who do it. At about two a man of about fifty of the Lowfen Reed's own third lay stood at that end stall in about nine people and said out loud that his route is one man short on Wednesday night and that he is not going to ask anybody in this yard, and he did not say who he was going to ask and he was not asked. The man of about thirty-two was in those nine and said nothing at all and was not asked to say anything, and this yard wrote that down and wrote down not one word about what he said nothing to. The slip, in five hundred and two words, gives the three numbers of the wall and not their sum, and says that the first thing this harbor does with a gap is send a man, and that a man who is sent is a man who was not asked. Four columns at four hundred and four and one thousand eight hundred and ninety-four, the third none and the fourth one hundred and twenty-five, the hearing at one hundred and sixty-ninth days, the bag at twenty-eight pence.

**672 — Monday the twenty-third, day twenty-two, a rota day, the hundred and fifty-second charge.** Eleven trips by hand between about eight and about eleven, walked on by none of it, the covers lying on it from about eleven until about four. At about ten the man of the Lowfen Reed was not in that yard; he had gone up that lane on his own account at about nine, and nobody sent for him and nobody knew where he had gone and the keeper did not ask. At about two a sheet went up on that wall beside the two lines, on two tacks out of the keeper's own pocket, with the seven days of that week down the side and nothing against any of the seven, and the keeper read it out in about nine people and named the page of hands, the page of routes and the money sheet separately and out loud before it went up. It is the page of that week; a thing that happens on a day goes on the line of that day; no name goes against a day and no state of any route goes against a day; anybody may read it and anybody may write a line on it. About four people in that nine cannot read a column and the sheet was read to them and nobody asked whether they had understood it and nobody read it twice. At about half past three a woman of about forty of the Cinder Bell's own community stood at the end of that shed for about a minute and a half and looked at the wall, and nobody asked her anything. Slip in four hundred and seventy-seven words.

**673 — Tuesday the twenty-fourth, day twenty-three, the eighty-third wage Tuesday.** The lid on that step was read out at about ten in four minutes by a man of about thirty-one of the second lay and stood at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks and did not move, and the chest with the twenty envelopes in it stood shut from ten until four, and the eighty-third week stands fallen due behind the eighty-second. At about eleven the first entry went onto the page of that week against the Monday and carries no name, and it was read out before it was written. At about half past two the man of the Lowfen Reed stood in about nine people and said out loud, on purpose and so that nobody could say afterwards that the yard had put a night on a page of its own, that whatever is paid for Wednesday night will stand on another route's own page and not in this yard's book, and the keeper wrote no figure at all, because the figure is not his and he did not hear it. Slip in four hundred and seventy-six words.

**674 — Wednesday the twenty-fifth, day twenty-four. THE FIRST BEAT.** At about ten, at that end stall, in about nine people, the man of about fifty of the Lowfen Reed's own third lay asked the woman of about forty of the Cinder Bell's own community for one night of work on the Reed's own line, and this yard did not send for anybody and was not asked whether he might. She said she would ask her own people and came back at about eleven and said that four of them will come on their own time and under their own order, and that the Bell runs nothing and has run nothing for a long time, and that she was speaking for four people who were going to be at home. She said, before anybody had written a word, that the Reed's page does not take the Bell's name as a custodian, that the Bell's page does not take the Reed's, that four people on the water for one night does not make them the Reed's and does not make the Reed theirs, and that if either of those routes ever wants to say otherwise it can come to that shed and say it in front of nine people. The man of about thirty-two asked one question, being whether this yard had sent for anybody, and both of them said it had not, and he asked nothing else. The Wednesday line carries no figure and no name and neither route's name, and under it the keeper wrote that the night's work will not put a name against anybody's written limits and that the page of hands will not be touched on the strength of four people being on the water. Slip in five hundred and fourteen words.

**675 — Thursday the twenty-sixth, day twenty-five, a rota day, the hundred and fifty-third charge.** Four of the Cinder Bell's own community were on the water on the Lowfen Reed's line from about seven in the evening until about two in the morning, on the Reed's own boat, under the Reed's own orders, and when they came in at about two they went up the lane and not into that market and nobody met them at either end of that mole. Nobody from that harbor went with them; that yard hired nobody and paid nobody. The man of about thirty-two was not on the water and was not asked to be and nobody sent for him, and the only fact about him is that a man of about thirty-three who hires hands asked him in passing whether he had heard and he said that he had. At about half past two the woman of thirty of no office asked two questions, being whether the night was on the page of that week and whether it was on the page of hands, and was told that it was on the first and never will be on the second, and was then told about the second sheet of days with the nine names down the side of it and that it had not been added up this month and was not going to be this week. Slip in five hundred words.

**676 — Friday the twenty-seventh, day twenty-six. THE SECOND BEAT.** A man of about fifty-three with a boat of about fourteen tons came in at about eleven with a slip of paper folded in four, a copy in his own hand of eleven words he wrote a long time ago and has never had answered. He said he was not asking for it to be answered and was not saying anybody was wrong, and that he had not come about Wednesday night, and asked for it on the Friday line of the page of that week beside the Thursday line. It was read out twice and written down with the day and the hour against it, and no figure is set against it and no figure on the other side of it, and the keeper wrote on the face of the sheet that no figure is set against it and that that is on the face of the sheet on purpose. *This coast can be cut in one place at a time.* Nobody answered it. A woman of about forty-four with a chandler's counter opened her mouth at about half past eleven and shut it again, and nine people saw her do it and nobody spoke for her and this yard wrote nothing about it. The man of about thirty-two looked at the two lines and said nothing. He said he is not taking it off again, that he would like to be told if a figure is ever set against it, and that he is sixty in the spring and would like something to be on a page before that. Slip in five hundred and thirty-nine words.

**677 — Saturday the twenty-eighth, day twenty-seven. THE THIRD BEAT, PAID AND NOT SETTLED.** Both of them were in that shed at about eleven in about nine people and nobody had sent for either and neither had come to fetch the other. The keeper left a space in the middle of the Saturday line and wrote two lines in it, one under the other, in their own words, neither carrying a name and neither of the two of them named in the other's line: his, that a line which records who did not agree keeps a man's yes at ten in the morning and loses his no at four in the afternoon; hers, that a line which records nobody's disagreement is a line that whoever reads it first can write, and that in nine months somebody would come along and read somebody's one line as a fact. He did not take his objection off the page and she did not take her third line off the page and neither gave up anything belonging to their own work. He then asked that nine whether anybody else wanted to write one line under the two, and four did, in their own hands, being a woman of about forty-four with a chandler's counter, a man of about thirty-one of the second lay, a man of about fifty-six of the third lay who lands fish and a woman of about twenty-seven with a burn scar across one forearm, and none of the four agreed with either of the first two. Nobody said the disagreement was settled and nobody said it was not, and those two did not speak to each other about any of it between eleven and four, and the keeper wrote that they did not and wrote no word about why. At about four she asked him what time that market shuts on a Sunday and he told her and she put it in her own pocket. **THEY ARE STILL MARRIED AND IT IS NOT SETTLED AND NO PAGE OF THIS HARBOR CARRIES A RESOLUTION OF IT.** Slip in five hundred and twenty-nine words.

**678 — Sunday the twenty-ninth, day twenty-eight, a wipe, the hundred and eighth, 25/12/25 = 62.** The wall came down at about ten past ten and was back at about twelve minutes past eleven and did not go up whole, and it is a minute longer each way and a minute longer bare again, and two Sundays now this yard has stopped asking and is not going to guess. At about half past two about four people in that shed were asked, one at a time and by nobody in particular, whether two people in that harbor are still speaking; three said yes and one said she did not know and had not seen them together; the keeper wrote all four answers with the hour against them and no name against any of them and not one word about the two. At about four both of them were in that shed for about ten minutes and were not in the same conversation and were not avoiding each other. A woman of about forty-four came down at about half past four and asked whether the Sunday line is read out like the rest of the week, and was told that it is, whatever is on it, that there are nine lines on it and he was not going to leave any of them off, and that she could stand at the end of that shed at half past five and that was all the invitation there is. Slip in four hundred and eighty words.

**679 — Monday the thirtieth, day twenty-nine, a rota day, the hundred and fifty-fourth charge.** Eleven trips by hand, the covers from about eleven until about four, and the name at the head of that rota board still off it. At about ten, in about nine people, the man of the Lowfen Reed asked the woman of the Cinder Bell whether she would do it again next week, and she said in about forty-three words that she will not say until she is asked and until her own people have talked, and that a route that has said yes once has not said yes twice, and he did not ask her a second time. **NOBODY IN THAT SHED SAID YES AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED SAID NO.** At about two the keeper took the second sheet of days off its nail, looked at it for about a minute and put it back, and told nine people he would add it up tomorrow and not today and would not say why in a room, and that whoever wanted to watch could stand at that bench stone at about three tomorrow; four said they would and five said nothing. Slip in five hundred and forty-six words.

**680 — Tuesday the thirty-first, day thirty, the eighty-fourth wage Tuesday, and Movement 3 CLOSES ON THE COUNT OF NIGHTS CARRIED.** The lid was read out in four minutes at about ten and did not move, the chest stood shut from ten until four, and the eighty-fourth week stands fallen due behind the eighty-third. At about three, in front of four people who came on their own account, the keeper took down the second sheet of days, with the nine route names down the side in the order they are always read in, and wrote one figure against one of the nine names and nothing against the other eight, and the sum of the nine underneath, and the day and the hour against it. **The figure is one and the sum is one, and it was not said out loud in that shed and it is not in the slip.** He said four things to those four people and none of them was the figure: that it is a count of nights and not of persons, boats or favours, and that the four people on the water last Wednesday are four persons and the number on that sheet is not four; **that a night carried by a route is not a night that route owns and no route owns a night because it was kept busy**, and that the name with a figure against it is the community whose people were on the water on somebody else's line, and it has it because they did the work and not because the Bell has gained a line or a crew or a page; that the same night is entered on the page of that week against the Wednesday line, so a stranger can get from one sheet to the other in about four seconds and back again, and it is one night and not two; and that the page of hands has not been touched and will not be added up this month. A woman of about forty-four added the nine figures herself with a pencil in about a minute, got the same figure, wrote it in the margin of her own price list, gave the sheet back and went to work, and was not asked what she had got. At about four the keeper wrote under the Tuesday line that the man of about thirty-two and the woman of thirty of no office are still married, that neither name is on any page of that harbor, and that the form is in the inside of a coat and is on no sheet. Slip in six hundred and seventy words, and it is the only slip in the batch that gives a whole day away to a summary of the ten days and it does not say the figure in it.

The cost is a season's work and a hull on about six men, finished being finished by about four in the afternoon, on no sheet. A man of about thirty-two goes out to two hundred yards, says thirty-seven words at the bench stone, and does not go into the water again in this movement. A helmsman of about thirty-one says two hundred and twenty-two words in nine people and is not thanked and is not told he was wrong. **622, Sunday the third of April, day 22** — a wipe, the hundredth time, seventeen off, four standing bare, seventeen back, thirty-eight minutes from about a quarter past ten to about ten to eleven, unrepaired and not whole; the boy of twenty-two is on the stool; the sheet of days is read to four people and the columns stand at four, one and four. **625, Wednesday the sixth of April, day 25** — a woman of about forty-one who crews out of Ashtide says in three hundred and thirty-four words that the Ashtide Run is restricted from that day; **WHAT MOVEMENT 1 IS, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** A sheet of days came into that harbor in the night under a stone and carries four columns headed opened, refused, restricted and withdrawn, and it says on its own face that it did not ask any community anything, that it does not name a person, that it does not carry a figure of persons, and that it does not say who set it out. It is the first Crown instrument in thirteen volumes that says what it did not do. Nobody has a name for whoever puts it out. A community was asked on Wednesday the sixteenth which of the four positions it is in, in about nine people, in four words, and answered opened. On Friday the eighteenth the same community said out loud, unasked, that it is in a different position, being restricted, and the position was taken back off the day it was written, the old figure left readable under a stroke and the new one written against Friday in a different column, and nothing was rubbed out and neither day moved. On Tuesday the twenty-second the count of positions was taken off that page, twice, and the two ways give three, and it was not said in a room and not said in the slip, and the man who keeps the leaf says in that slip why he is not going to say it. A man who came off a Crown list in the winter came up that coast road on foot over four days with a canvas bag and put it on a bench stone and nobody asked him what was in it. A route crew that had never been asked was asked to hold one mark for one night and said no, and said something else instead. **AND THE ARGUMENT OF THE MOVEMENT IS THAT THE SMOOTH PAGE IN THIS VOLUME IS NOT CHALK ON A WALL. IT IS A CALENDAR.**

### What the ten chapters did, one line each

1. **561.** A woman of thirty goes to the eleven people of that harbor who cannot read, one at a time, and comes back with what they said, in about two hundred and seventy-five words: about half of them said before she had finished asking that they did not want to say it in a slip; one of them said seven is the number he has believed since he was a boy; one of them said he has been in a boat that came in with her gear in the bottom and her man not on her and that he was twelve; **six of them wanted to know what a return is and not one of them had ever seen one**; and about four of them said the sixth of the six lines is the only one that has anybody in it. A man of about thirty-three who hires hands said a man cannot hire anybody out of eleven answers, and a man of about thirty-five of the first lay said there are two men in that market who cannot read a wall and that neither of them has ever asked for one. **SHE DECLINED OUT LOUD TO ANSWER HER OWN QUESTION AND SAID THAT WHOEVER ANSWERS IT WILL HAVE TO HAVE BEEN IN THAT ROOM ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH AND BE ABLE TO SAY WHAT THE ANSWER COSTS.**
2. **562.** A man of about twenty-seven of the second lay writes the six lines on the wall of the room over that market in a large hand, **stops at the seal, and writes no name under it**, having been asked by nobody. About twenty people go up and about eleven cannot read it. A man of about fifty-three who owns a boat of about fourteen tons goes at the six lines one at a time for about an hour and a half and takes none of them down, and stands in front of the fifth for about ten minutes. **HE SAYS OUT LOUD THAT HE STOPPED BECAUSE OF A WOMAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE WHO STOOD UP IN THAT ROOM ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF JANUARY AND SAID SHE HAD NOT BEEN ON THE WATER AND DID NOT KNOW, AND THAT HE DOES NOT KNOW WHY SHE SAID IT AND IS NOT GOING TO BE THE ONE WHO ASKS.** A man of about thirty-four, who cannot read, asks in about forty-six words to be told what he cannot read on that wall, and is not asked to have it read out and is not thanked.
3. **563.** A rota day and the hundred and twenty-second charge. A woman of about thirty-one of the first lay stands at the end of that slip and says out loud, in about two hundred and four words, what she was asked to say in that room on the twenty-fourth and what she said instead, naming nobody, and **says out loud that she does hold a particular and has had it since she was told about the two boats and has not put it on a wall and is not putting it on a wall, and that the sixth of those six lines does not require her to.** A man of about thirty-three says she is only saying it because a man of about fifty-three said it yesterday, and is answered in about twenty-four words and is not right and is not wrong. Nobody asked her what the particular is.
4. **564.** A fourth paper goes onto the board at the head of that mole at about eleven, in four lines, asking for the returns of that port and the harbour returns of the vessels engaged in that line, with about nine names on the foot of it by the middle of the day. **Four people spend the afternoon finding out that neither of those two things has ever been in that harbor.** A man of about fifty-three says a demand nailed to a board in this harbor goes to nobody, and that a cart takes four days each way and a boat takes a day and a night, and that he is not against the demand. A woman of thirty says out loud, in about fifty-six words, that a sheet of paper on a wall cannot be asked where its own figures came from. The paper went into a boat's basket at four o'clock.
5. **565.** The man of about thirty-two asks the man of about thirty-four of the second lay, out loud, in the open, in front of the same nine people, whether he will hold one of three channels and whether he says yes or no, exactly as he said on the twenty-ninth that he would. **The answer is no, in one word, and nobody argues him out of it, and the man who asked said nothing back and said out loud that he was not going to ask again.** A man of about forty-six writes the asking and the answer out on a page in a hand that is not the man's; that page is not a page of hours, carries no hour, and does not go on the bench stone. The man of about thirty-four says, unasked, in about two hundred and twenty-six words, why, and is not asked why before or after. **THE ONE LINE OF THE BATCH GOES ON THE SHEET AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE PENCE IN THE THIRD DATING FORM, AND THE PERSON WHOSE YARD IT IS SAYS BOTH DAYS OUT LOUD BEFORE THE FIGURE.**
6. **566.** A wipe and the ninety-second time. The wall comes down bare at about half past ten, eleven people go past it, and one of them shifts a basket about a yard short of it. **A SECOND SEALED SHEET COMES ASHORE AT ABOUT TWO IN THE AFTERNOON AND GOES ONTO THAT BOARD, AND IT IS ALSO TRUE.** Its six lines are printed in full and they are about the night of Friday the twenty-first, and its fifth line says in its own words that it does not state what was sounded on that coast on that night. **THE THIRD OF THE SIX LINES OF THE FIRST SHEET CARRIES NO SUCH THING AND THE FIFTH OF THIS ONE DOES, AND THE GAP OF FORTY-SEVEN SECONDS IS ON NEITHER SHEET.** A woman of thirty says so out loud, in about fifty-seven words, on the stones. A man of about thirty-three says in about ninety-seven words that reading a document aloud for people who cannot read it is the oldest job in that harbor. 9. **569.** A room over that market, about nine people, the six lines on the wall. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE WHO HIRES HANDS SAYS WHAT HE WANTS FIRST, BEING FOUR MORE HANDS ON HIS BOOKS BEFORE THE SPRING TIDES, AND THEN SAYS, OUT LOUD, IN ABOUT TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY WORDS, IN FRONT OF THOSE SIX LINES, THAT HE HAS BEEN WRONG SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF JANUARY, BY THE ADMISSION THAT IF ONE MAN IN THAT PORT HAD HELD THE WHOLE OF THAT RECORD IN ONE BOOK THEN TWO BOATS WOULD NOT BE ON THE GROUND OFF THAT WATER WITH THEIR GEAR IN THE BOTTOM AND NOBODY STANDING ON EITHER OF THEM, AND THAT HE IS NOT SAYING THAT THE PAGE IS RIGHT AND IS SAYING THAT IT WOULD HAVE WORKED.** Nobody answered. Nobody made a speech. A man of about fifty-three was in that room for the whole of it and said nothing. A woman of about thirty-one was in that room for the whole of it and said nothing. A man of about thirty-four who cannot read was in that room and said nothing. Nobody was thanked. **THE ADMISSION WENT INTO THE SECOND COLUMN OF THAT LEAF AND NOT INTO THE FIRST, BECAUSE THE FIRST COLUMN TAKES THE DAY.**
10. **570.** A rota day and the hundred and twenty-fourth charge. In the room over that market, at about two, in about nine people, **A CLERK OF THAT HARBOR AUTHORITY WHO READ THE FIRST SEALED SHEET ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF JANUARY AND WAS IN THAT ROOM ANSWERS THE QUESTION A WOMAN OF THIRTY ASKED THERE, OUT LOUD, ONCE, IN ABOUT TWO HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SIX WORDS: THIS HARBOR ACCEPTS THAT PAPER AS ITS ACCOUNT OF THE FOURTEENTH — AND HE SAYS WHAT THAT COSTS BEFORE HE SAYS THE ANSWER, BEING THE WALL AT THE TOP OF FISH STREET AND THE SIXTH OF THOSE SIX LINES.** Nobody answered him and nobody thanked him. At about half past four, in a second room four hundred yards away at the top of Fish Street, in about nine people, with the man of about thirty-five of the first lay standing there, **A WOMAN OF THIRTY SAYS, IN THIRTY WORDS AND EXACTLY THIRTY WORDS, THAT THE PRICE OF THAT IS PAID BY PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT IN THE ROOM, AND THEY CANNOT BE TOLD WHAT THEY ARE PAYING, AND IT GOES ON ALL THE SAME.** Nobody answered it. ### The figures, re-derived by adding and not by looking

The fitting-out sheet stands at one hundred and six thousand six hundred and forty-six pence out on the twenty-second and moves once, on the twenty-seventh, by four hundred and forty-eight pence, being air for one man for one descent at two hundred and eighty and a shackle and a link of chain and three fathoms of line at one hundred and sixty-eight. **106,646 + 448 = 107,094 out, being six hundred and sixty-nine marks, four shillings and sixpence, against 10,640 in, being sixty-six marks, six shillings and eightpence, and 107,094 - 10,640 = 96,454 short, being six hundred and two marks, eleven shillings and twopence.** The bag is twenty-eight pence on all ten days, and 28 + 1,680 - 1,680 = 28, and one thousand six hundred and eighty pence each way is ten marks, six shillings and eightpence. The leaf is at 293 and one thousand three hundred and thirty-nine and none and one hundred and twenty-five at the close of the movement, being 283 + 10 and 1,289 + 50, and it is not read back aloud on any of the ten days. The nine day-counters run from 248 / 250 / 588 / 354 / 172 / 127 / 142 / 159 / 190 and every one of the ninety printed values is its own base plus its own day, the ninth of the nine landing on two hundred on the thirty-first. The hearing of the man of about twenty-nine is forty-nine days on the twenty-second and fifty-eight on the thirty-first and no figure is set against it.

### The voice of the ten, for a writer of 561 to 570

**The batch opens on a sound and the sound is never explained. It is a pair of flat notes off the water with a countable gap in it and the countable gap is the only thing about it that a stranger can check, and that is the whole argument of the volume in one figure.** The account arrives as a thing with a seal on it and six true lines and a name nobody reads out, and the batch's best sentences are the ones that refuse it: *a man who is asked for a thing in a room with about eleven people in it and who thanks her for it has told those eleven people he was owed something*, which is Volume 11's own and is not repeated here; the batch's own is *a sheet with a line and a space for a hand is neither an account nor an answer and is a third thing*, and *a sheet which is correct about what it covers and silent about the rest is the hardest kind of paper there is to argue with in the open*, and *a man who lists the costs of ten days in the order of what he can put a figure on has written a bill and not a cost*, and *I have been handed a smooth page and I have had one a year, and there is a way to be handed a smooth page without ever being asked anything, and I have found it, and it is standing still*, and *a man who has counted one gap and can count the second one has found out that the sound is a repeating thing and not a pair of things, and neither of them wanted to know that at about half past ten at night on a Saturday in January with four people listening and no light in that shed but a lamp on a bench stone*.

**The house form held: the bold figures block, the nine-counter standing paragraph, the scene in paragraphs of two to six sentences separated by rules, the bold closing block, two rules, and then the first column in the yard's own mouth and the second column in the yard's own mouth with an hour against each. The required fact is carried in six noun phrases and seven verb frames in the ten scene bodies, which is what the Volume 11 audit asked a later batch to do, and in its own words in the apparatus on every day. No two scene paragraphs are byte-identical and no two five o'clock openings are byte-identical.**

### The one thing a writer of 561 to 570 must not soften

**The account is not false. Six of its six lines are particulars a stranger can check, and the man who refuses to sign it says out loud that he does not think it is a lie and that he has read it twice and there is not one line of it he could argue with. The pressure of this volume is not that anybody is lying to that coast. The pressure is that a technically accurate account with a seal on it cannot be argued with in a room, that a paper cannot be asked where its own figures came from, that its sixth line is an offer, and that the people who argue with it are made to look like people who want a coast where children are frightened by what they cannot verify. NOBODY ON THESE TEN PAGES HAS SAID THAT SENTENCE AND A LATER CHAPTER MAY NOT PUT IT INTO A MOUTH EITHER; IT IS PAID ON PAGES, IN A REFUSAL WITH A MAN'S OWN HAND AT THE FOOT OF IT, IN THREE YESES AND AN UNANSWERED QUESTION, AND IN A MAN ASKING TO BE ASKED.**

## Volume 11, Batch 0005 (Chapters 541–550), Movement 5, *three points in one night, a coast that moves without a Crown hull, and a question about a single voice* — as written, 30 September 2026. **THE CLIMAX MOVEMENT IS PAID AND THE VOLUME IS WRITTEN TO CHAPTER 550. TWO BOATS WERE LOST TO THE WATER ON THAT NIGHT, NOBODY WAS KILLED, NO BODY IS NAMED, NO CASUALTY FIGURE IS PRINTED, BOTH CREWS WERE ASHORE BY SIX IN THE MORNING, AND BOTH LOSSES ARE ON THE SHEET IN PENCE AS TWO BILLS ON TWO DIFFERENT DAYS. THE RECONSTRUCTION IS PAID A SECOND TIME AT FIVE THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-TWO PENCE, WHICH IS NOT FIFTEEN THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY PENCE.
