### Chapter 531 — *Sunday the Second Day of January, a Wipe, the Eighty-Seventh Time, the Wall Down Bare and Up Unrepaired, the Party on the Coast Road About Nine Miles Out at Eight in the Morning and the Wagons Turned About at Ten and That Quay at About Half Past Four, Bread and Salt for Nine Men for Three Days at Seven Hundred and Twenty and One Day of Air at a Cannery at Three Hundred and Twenty, Both With the Second of January Against Them, the Berth-Fund Day Paid and Its Reason Given in New Words and Said Out Loud Once, the Shortfall Said Out Loud at Forty-Eight Thousand Eight Hundred and Ninety-Eight*

****THE PARTY IS ON THAT COAST ROAD.** At about eight in the morning, about nine miles out, two wagons and a handcart stand at a gate where that road crosses a burn and nine people stand about them, none of them asked to be there and all of them having come. A man of about fifty who owns a boat of about twenty-two tons wants to go on, because he has been paid for going before, and the man of about thirty-two answers him in about thirty words and says the rest of it once: **there is nothing at the end of that road today that wants nine men, a party that is not on the water is a party standing about being paid a day a day, and I would rather turn two wagons about on a Sunday than pay nine men a Sunday for standing in a field.** The wagons are turned about at about ten and are on that quay at about half past four, **AND THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF DID NOT GO DOWN THAT ROAD AT ALL AND IS ON THAT QUAY ALL DAY, WHICH IS WHY THAT SHEET IS SETTLED EVERY DAY OF THIS MOVEMENT.** At about half past ten, four hundred yards and nine miles back, the wall behind a reeve's bench comes down bare for the eighty-seventh time and goes up at the angle it has been at since the twelfth, and five people walk past and none of them puts a bucket under it. **BREAD AND SALT FOR NINE MEN FOR THREE DAYS GOES ON THAT SHEET AT 720, BEING FOUR MARKS, SIX SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, BEING TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE A DAY, WHICH IS THE FIGURE A BOAT ALONGSIDE THAT WEST QUAY IS SELLING IT AT AND NOT THE FIGURE THE BOARD AT THAT END STALL CARRIED, AND ONE DAY OF AIR FOR A COMPRESSOR RUN IN A YARD AT A CANNERY ON THAT ROAD GOES ON AT 320, BEING TWO MARKS EXACTLY; BOTH CARRY THE SECOND OF JANUARY, BOTH ARE SAID OUT LOUD BEFORE A FIGURE IS WRITTEN AGAINST EITHER, AND BOTH ARE IN THE TOTAL THAT AFTERNOON.** The man who keeps the leaf says out loud once, in words that are neither of the last two Sundays, why that fund pays a Sunday: **once a fund is asked to account for itself to a market it has stopped being a fund and become an office with a slate in it, and this yard has said nothing to anybody about that book for sixteen weeks.** A handcart hired off the west basin comes up that road at about four in the afternoon with a boat upright on it in a cradle of loose shingles, and that boat goes into that shipyard at about six, **AND THAT BOAT IS THE ONLY THING THAT WAS EVER IN THAT YARD THAT SOMEBODY CAN POINT AT, AND IT IS THE REASON A WEEK LATER THAT A FIRE TAKES A BUILDING AND NOT A BOAT.** Nobody was thanked for anything. Shortfall 48,898, being 305 marks, 8 shillings and 2 pence. Columns 263 / 1,192 / none / 125 at the hour and 264 / 1,194 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 532 — *Monday the Third Day of January, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Thirteenth Charge in Eleven Trips by Hand and Walked on by None of It, a Man of About Thirty-Three Who Hires Hands Saying Out Loud at Half Past Nine That This Harbor Has Nine Men on It and No Work and Being Told That a Shed With Nothing in It to Mend Is Not a Week of Work and Then Being Refused Two Men to Carry Water by a Slater of About Forty in About Four Words, Coal for Four Days at Nine Hundred and Sixty With the Third of January Against It, the Shortfall Said Out Loud at Forty-Nine Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty-Eight*

****THE CISTERN IS CHARGED FOR THE HUNDRED AND THIRTEENTH TIME AT ABOUT EIGHT IN ELEVEN TRIPS BY HAND BECAUSE THE HOSE IS DEAD UNTIL THE SPRING, AND THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THAT ROTA BOARD IS STILL OFF IT.** At about half past nine, about nine minutes after nine men came back up a coast road with two wagons and nothing at the end of it, a man of about thirty-three who hires hands stands at the head of that third lay asking whether anybody wants a pair of hands for a week, and four people say no to him in about two minutes before he asks the ninth man. **He then puts it to the man who keeps the leaf directly, in front of about nine people, and is told in about six words that four of those nine are his own men paid a day a day at the figure in chalk whether he wants them or not, and that a shed with nothing in it to mend is the ninth week of it and nothing new was heard in it this morning.** He asks a slater of about forty for two men to carry water and is refused in about four words with the reason the slater gives himself: a board that turns on a Monday and a Thursday is not a place to ask anybody anything, moving a man up it once moves a man off it who has been on it nine years, and ask again in a fortnight and on a Thursday. **COAL FOR FOUR DAYS GOES ON AT 960, BEING SIX MARKS EXACTLY, AT TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE A DAY, THE FIGURE A BOAT ALONGSIDE THAT WEST QUAY IS SELLING IT AT AND WHICH WENT UP IN DECEMBER, AND THE FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE AT THAT END STALL IS A LAMP OIL FIGURE AND IS NOT ON THAT SHEET AND NEVER GOES ON THE SAME LINE AS A COAL FIGURE.** At half past five the shortfall is said out loud and a man who says there is nothing to do is told that the only number that moved in that harbor between ten and four was one hundred and sixty-eight pence going out for four men, and **none of the standing list moved and nothing was bettered and nothing was asked for.** Nobody was thanked. Shortfall 49,858, being 311 marks, 8 shillings and 2 pence. Columns 264 / 1,197 / none / 125 at the hour and 265 / 1,199 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 533 — *Tuesday the Fourth Day of January, the Sixty-Third Wage Tuesday, the Column at Twenty-Six Lines and One Hundred and Four Marks Read Out on the Step at Ten o'Clock and Not Moving and the Sixty-Third Week Fallen Due, a Shipyard on That Quay Priced in Hours and Material at About Half Past Eleven at Fifteen Thousand Three Hundred and Twenty Pence, Being Ninety-Five Marks and Ten Shillings, and Nobody Agreeing to Any Part of It and Nothing Going onto That Sheet, a Man of About Forty-Six Who Sells Ice Asking Out Loud Whether the Column Has Moved Since November, the Shortfall Said Out Loud Unmoved at Forty-Nine Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty-Eight*

****THE COLUMN IS READ OUT AND DOES NOT MOVE AND NOBODY IS PAID A PENNY OUT OF THE CHEST AND THE SIXTY-THIRD WEEK STANDS FALLEN DUE, AND A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX WHO SELLS ICE OUT OF A BARROW ASKS THE CLERK OUT LOUD IN FRONT OF FORTY PEOPLE WHETHER THE COLUMN HAS MOVED SINCE NOVEMBER AND IS TOLD THAT IT HAS NOT AND SAYS NOVEMBER TWICE IN THE SAME TONE AND GOES BACK TO HIS BARROW.** The day's work is at about half past eleven in the shipyard two hundred yards from the bench stone. **FOUR MEN ASK NESSA PIKE, OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE, WHAT A NEW ROOF ON THAT SHED WOULD COME TO — NO: OF ABOUT TWENTY-SEVEN — AND SHE PRICES IT IN HOURS AND MATERIAL ON THE BACK OF A SLATE AND SAYS EVERY FIGURE AS SHE WRITES IT: forty fathoms of three-inch fir at two hundred and forty pence a fathom being nine thousand six hundred, being sixty marks exactly; three days of one man's hours on a bench at one hundred and sixty-eight pence a day being five hundred and four, being three marks and two shillings; sixteen fathoms of two-inch for that yard's own stock at two hundred pence a fathom being three thousand two hundred, being twenty marks exactly; and three days apiece in advance to the same four men at the figure in chalk being two thousand and sixteen, being twelve marks and eight shillings, those four men being on no sheet and not counted on it. The sum is FIFTEEN THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY PENCE, BEING NINETY-FIVE MARKS AND TEN SHILLINGS, with no contingency on it.** A man of about thirty-three who hires hands, listening at the door, asks who is paying that, and is told in about ten words that nobody is, and that a figure for a yard standing with a roof on it is not a bill, because a bill is money somebody has decided to spend and no one in that harbor has decided to spend anything that morning. She then says, once, that if it is ever a bill it goes on that sheet with the day the work was done against it and into the total at the foot of that sheet on the day it is settled, and that the day somebody agrees to it is the day the slate comes off that bench. **NOBODY AGREED TO IT, NOBODY PUT A HAND ON THE SLATE, NOTHING WENT ON THAT SHEET IN ANY HAND, AND NOBODY WAS THANKED FOR ANY PART OF THE HOUR.** At half past five the shortfall is said out loud unmoved and the man who keeps the leaf says out loud that a number said out loud in a shipyard is not a cost and that if the work is not done the correct place for that figure is the back of that shed. Shortfall unmoved at 49,858, being 311 marks, 8 shillings and 2 pence. Columns 265 / 1,202 / none / 125 at the hour and 266 / 1,204 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 534 — *Wednesday the Fifth Day of January, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, a Shipyard on That Quay Destroyed in About an Hour Between About Ten and About Half Past Eleven and Nobody in It at Any Hour and Nobody Hurt, a Woman of About Fifty-Two at a Fish Stall the First to See It Saying the Shape of It and Not What She Thought It Was, About Two Hundred Yards of It Standing Open to the Sky, a Man of About Thirty-Three Asking Twice Who Did It and Not Being Answered Either Time, the Man of About Thirty-Two Saying Out Loud Once That He Is Not Going to Look, Four Men Paid at About Four in the Afternoon at the Figure in Chalk, the Shortfall Said Out Loud Unmoved at Forty-Nine Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty-Eight*

****NOBODY DIES, NO BODY IS NAMED, NO CASUALTY FIGURE IS PRINTED, NOBODY IS HURT, NOBODY HAS BEEN NAMED A CASUALTY, AND A BUILDING'S LOSS IS NOT A PERSON'S LOSS AND IS NOT WRITTEN AS ONE.** A woman of about fifty-two who keeps a fish stall at the head of that quay sees it from her own step at about ten and says the shape of it and not what she thought it was: smoke off the west end and not the east, the east end being the end the flue runs in and the west end the end the bench is in, and that it went along the west wall toward the door and did not go out through the roof, and she wants that in whatever anybody is going to write, because every one of them will be back down there in a week telling her it went up through the rafters. She puts the tray down, picks it up, goes back to selling fish, is not asked a second question and is not thanked. **About twenty people stand on that quay at about eleven at a distance the slater afterwards said was about the right distance and did not say why, and what is left standing is the wall the flue runs in at the east end, the door frame and about nine feet of the north wall, and the iron in the bench frames did not go.** Nessa Pike gives her account in about forty words and says in the same breath that she is giving it in that order on purpose: **a roof, a bench, a stock of sawn fir and a set of hours, and that is the whole of it.** She then says the one thing that matters: there was a boat in that building on Monday morning and there is not one in it now, because she hired a cart off the west basin on Saturday and paid for it out of her own pocket and it is not on that sheet and is not going to be, and that boat is at the north quay with her bilge blocks under her. **A man of about thirty-three who hires hands asks who did it at about a quarter past eleven and again at about half past and is answered neither time, gives himself one reason twenty minutes later — that two hulls came in past the west quay on Monday night and went out on the top of it and he was awake and has not written it down because nobody asked him and he is not going to start a list — and says that he has not got a name and is not going to get one by asking a woman with a tray of fish in her hand. NO NAME OF ANY MAN IS SAID OUT LOUD ON THAT QUAY THAT DAY, AND NO ORDER AND NO MOTIVE AND NO FIGURE IS SET AGAINST ANYBODY.** At about a quarter to twelve the man who keeps the leaf says one thing out loud on that quay, once: **he is not going to walk up that coast road and ask anybody anything, because he has four men on a wage and a bench to make and a sheet anybody with a leaf and a pencil can check, and a man who goes looking is a man who is not making the bench, and a question is going to be under nobody's feet at all** — and that the slate with fifteen thousand three hundred and twenty pence on it is still on that bench stone and is not going into the back of that shed until the work is done or not at all. **THE FOUR MEN ARE PAID AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON AT THE FIGURE IN CHALK, ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE APIECE, BEFORE ANYBODY HAS FINISHED LOOKING AT WHAT IS IN IT, AND A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WHO SAYS IT IS NOT RIGHT TO PAY FOUR MEN FOR A DAY WITH NOTHING TO MEND IS TOLD THAT A DAY'S WORK IS A DAY THAT A MAN WORKED AND THAT THE FIGURE HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE FIRST OF DECEMBER.** Nobody was thanked. Shortfall unmoved at 49,858, being 311 marks, 8 shillings and 2 pence. Columns 266 / 1,207 / none / 125 at the hour and 267 / 1,209 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 535 — *Thursday the Sixth Day of January, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Fourteenth Charge in Eleven Trips by Hand and Walked on by None of It, the Person Whose Yard It Is Saying Out Loud in Eleven Words That It Is a Bill and Not a Wound and Refusing a Second Reading in Nine Words, Three Days Apiece in Advance to the Same Four Men at Two Thousand and Sixteen With the Sixth of January Against It and the Days of That Roof Said Out Loud in the Open, the Shortfall Said Out Loud at Fifty-One Thousand Eight Hundred and Seventy-Four*

****THE CISTERN IS CHARGED FOR THE HUNDRED AND FOURTEENTH TIME IN ELEVEN TRIPS BY HAND AND THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THAT ROTA BOARD IS STILL OFF IT.** At about ten in the morning, with about fourteen people in about two hundred yards of it, **the person whose yard it is says eleven words out loud and once: IT IS A BILL AND NOT A WOUND. SAY IT THAT WAY ROUND. NOBODY IS GOING TO FEEL BETTER AND I AM NOT ASKING ANYBODY TO FEEL BETTER.** A man of about thirty-three who hires hands asks her, in front of about fourteen people, to say it again louder for the people at the end of that quay, **and she refuses in about nine words: you were not standing here at ten o'clock yesterday and neither was anybody at the end of that quay, a thing said twice for the people who were not there is not said louder, it is said to the people who were, and I have got fourteen of them here and I am not going to perform it at the far end.** He says that was fair and does not ask a second time. **She then gives the whole of Tuesday's figure off a second slate and says it has not changed by a penny, and then she gives the DAYS in the open because they are the part that is going to be wrong: two men on that roof is a fortnight and three men is five days and she has three, because two of the four went off on Wednesday night to a cannery at the end of that coast road and came back that morning and she did not ask them why and they did not tell her; so the roof goes up on the sixth, the seventh and the eighth, and if the weather turns on the ninth she will stand in that yard and be wrong out loud, and she is not going to buy a fourth day and pretend this week had one in it. The bench goes in on the eighth, because a bench made under a roof that is not on yet gets wet for nine months first, and the man whose hours those three days are is not one of the three on the roof. The stock comes off a cart on the eighth from the mill that goes off the coast road before the burn.** A man of about fifty-one who crews four out of the first lay asks how she knows and is told, in about six words, that he has watched her be wrong about a figure three times in eleven years and that this is the fourth time and he may write it on whatever he likes. **THE FOUR MEN ARE HIRED AT ABOUT TEN IN THE MORNING AT ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE A DAY APIECE FOR THREE DAYS IN ADVANCE, BEING TWO THOUSAND AND SIXTEEN PENCE, BEING TWELVE MARKS AND EIGHT SHILLINGS, THE SIXTH OF JANUARY AGAINST IT, IN THE TOTAL THAT AFTERNOON, THOSE FOUR MEN BEING ON NO SHEET AND NOT COUNTED ON IT.** Nobody was thanked, nobody was asked for a penny, and at half past five the man who keeps the leaf says out loud that the roof is not on that sheet and will be on it on the day the last board goes on, and that nobody in that harbor is a penny better off and the third lay is still a berth short and the lamp oil is still at four hundred and fifty pence. Shortfall 51,874, being 324 marks, 2 shillings and 10 pence. Columns 267 / 1,212 / none / 125 at the hour and 268 / 1,214 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 536 — *Friday the Seventh Day of January, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, Ternwatch Entered for the First Time, a Hut of Tarred Board About Nine Feet by Eleven on a Low Shoulder Above the Water With a Bell Under a Board on Four Sticks and No Board on Any Post, a Man of About Fifty-Two Who Ran That Station for Nineteen Years Standing in the Doorway Once and Saying That a Station With One Man in It Is a Man Sitting in a Box and Going Down Again, a Man of About Twenty-Nine Sitting in It From Dusk Until About Three in the Morning on Two Nights and Hearing Three Things and Saying He Cannot Tell a Pump From the Water in a Pipe, a Week's Hire of a Room Over a Store at Six Hundred and Seventy-Two Agreed in a Cart on the Coast Road on the Fourth, the Shortfall Said Out Loud at Fifty-Two Thousand Five Hundred and Forty-Six*

****TERNWATCH IS ENTERED HERE AND NOWHERE BEFORE IT, AND IT IS A LISTENING STATION ON A COAST THAT IS BEING CLOSED, AND THE FISHER COMMONWEALTH THAT BROUGHT ITS CONDITION IS NOT AT TERNWATCH AND IS NOT NAMED ON ANY PAGE OF THIS MOVEMENT.** The room: **A WEEK OF A ROOM OVER A STORE GOES ON THAT SHEET AT SIX HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-TWO PENCE, BEING FOUR MARKS, TWO SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, BEING FIVE SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE A DAY FOR SEVEN DAYS, QUOTED BY THE WOMAN WHO KEEPS THAT STORE IN A CART ON THAT COAST ROAD ON TUESDAY AND NOT ARGUED WITH, SLIPPED UP THAT ROAD IN AN ENVELOPE ON WEDNESDAY, WITH THE SEVENTH OF JANUARY AGAINST IT AND IN THE TOTAL THAT AFTERNOON** — and nobody in this harbor was asked for that figure and a room is not a favour. The station: a hut of tarred board about nine feet by eleven with a chimney out of it and a bench inside and a bell under a board on four sticks on a shoulder about three quarters of a mile above a street of about forty houses where nobody has been out on the water since the autumn, standing nineteen years with the post-board taken down in the autumn and not gone back up. **A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-TWO WHO RAN IT FOR NINETEEN YEARS WITH A SECOND MAN BESIDE HIM COMES UP THAT SHOULDER ON THE THURSDAY AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON, STANDS IN THE DOORWAY, DOES NOT GO IN, AND SAYS ABOUT FORTY WORDS: I TOOK NINETEEN YEARS IN THAT HUT AND I HAD A MAN BESIDE ME THE WHOLE OF IT AND THAT IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS WORTH ANYTHING, AND THERE IS ONE MAN IN THERE NOW AND THAT IS NOT A LISTENING STATION, IT IS A MAN SITTING IN A BOX; A MAN WHO WRITES DOWN WHAT HE THINKS HE HEARD WILL BE TWO MEN AND ONE OF THEM IS NOT THERE; YOU HAVE GOT NO BOOK AND NO SECOND PAIR OF EARS AND NOBODY TO SAY NO TO YOU AT THREE IN THE MORNING. HE GOES DOWN THE SHOULDER AND IS NOT ARGUED WITH, IS NOT ASKED TO COME BACK AND IS NOT THANKED.** The man of about twenty-nine sat in that hut from about eight in the evening until about three in the morning on the Thursday and the Friday and wrote down what he could hear on the back of a sheet out of a book, and gave his account of it in about sixty words: a pump at the third house up that road that goes at about eleven and stops at about twelve and that he has never walked up to look at; a bell about two in the morning out over the water to the south that he knows is a bell and not a gun and whose owner he cannot name and will not walk out to find; **and himself, which is that he can hear himself breathing on that side more clearly than he can hear a man standing in a doorway, and he does not know what that is and has not written it down.** He is asked one question, being whether he can tell a pump from the water in a pipe, and answers no in three words, and that is the end of it. **NOBODY THANKED HIM, NO FIGURE WAS SET AGAINST HIM, HE WAS NOT MADE A MEMBER OF ANYTHING, NOBODY REMARKED ON ANYTHING HE SAID IN A WAY THAT MADE HIM MORE, HE DID NOT ASK ANYBODY FOR ANYTHING, AND HE WAS TOLD TO PUT HOURS ON HIS THREE LINES AND NOT HIS NAME AT THE HEAD OF IT.** At half past five the shortfall is said out loud at fifty-two thousand five hundred and forty-six, being three hundred and twenty-eight marks, five shillings and sixpence, and it is said that a man is sitting five nights in a hut hearing three things and one of the three is himself and there is not one person in this harbor who has any more food this week than they had last week. Nobody was thanked. Columns 268 / 1,217 / none / 125 at the hour and 269 / 1,219 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 537 — *Saturday the Eighth Day of January, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, a Roof Going Up in Three Days on the Sixth, the Seventh and the Eighth With Two Days on the Face of One Line and the Last Board on at About Four in the Afternoon, Three Lines Going Onto That Sheet at About Ten in the Morning at Thirteen Thousand Three Hundred and Four in All, a Man of About Fifty Offering a Fortnight at Two Hundred and Forty a Day and Being Refused in Nine Words Because This Sheet Is Not Made to Balance by Asking This Harbor for the Difference, a Slate Carrying Tuesday's Figure Going Into the Drawer Under That Bench Stone, the Shortfall Said Out Loud at Sixty-Five Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty*

****THE ROOF GOES UP ON THAT QUAY IN THREE DAYS, THE SIXTH, THE SEVENTH AND THE EIGHTH, WITH TWO DAYS ON THE FACE OF ONE LINE, AND THE LAST BOARD GOES ON AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON.** Three lines go onto that sheet at about ten in the morning, the roof not on yet and not to be until four: **a roof at nine thousand six hundred, being sixty marks exactly, being forty fathoms of three-inch at two hundred and forty a fathom and the boarding dressed to it, with the sixth and the seventh both on the face of that line; a bench at five hundred and four, being three marks and two shillings, being three days of one man's hours at one hundred and sixty-eight a day, with the eighth against it; and a new stock of sawn fir at three thousand two hundred, being twenty marks exactly, being sixteen fathoms of two-inch at two hundred a fathom off a cart from the mill, with the eighth against it. Thirteen thousand three hundred and four pence in all, being eighty-three marks and two shillings. A man with a leaf and a pencil can take three days off those three lines and find they are the sixth, the seventh and the eighth.** And the sentence the man who keeps the leaf says about it is the heart of the movement: **forty fathoms is a number that a man can count with a stick and three days is a number that cannot be counted with a stick at all, and the three days is the part that cost the most and I have put it on that sheet in hours at a figure anyway, because that is the only way a man who was not in that yard on Friday can see any of it.** **AT ABOUT A QUARTER TO ELEVEN A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WHO OWNS A BOAT OF ABOUT TWENTY-TWO TONS PUTS HIS HAND FLAT ON THAT BENCH STONE AND OFFERED THAT YARD A FORTNIGHT'S WORK WITH HIS OWN BOAT AND TWO MEN AT TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE A DAY IN FRONT OF ABOUT NINE PEOPLE, AND WAS REFUSED IN NINE WORDS — THIS SHEET IS NOT MADE TO BALANCE BY ASKING THIS HARBOR FOR THE DIFFERENCE AND IT IS NEVER GOING TO BE — AND WAS NOT ARGUED WITH AND WAS NOT THANKED AND HAS NOT BEEN ASKED ABOUT IT SINCE.** The rest of it once: two hundred and forty pence a day would come on that sheet as a figure and there would not be one line on that sheet this winter a man could take a pencil to, **I WOULD RATHER BE SHORT BY SIXTY-FIVE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE AND BE RIGHT ABOUT EVERY ONE OF THEM THAN BE FOUR THOUSAND PENCE BETTER OFF AND HAVE NOBODY ABLE TO SAY WHAT THE FORTNIGHT WAS FOR.** He tells the man to find a day at the figure in chalk out of his own book and come back and put his hand to the bench, which is free; a man of about thirty-three says a sheet nobody can check is a diary with a bad head on it and says it once and is neither agreed with nor disagreed with. **AT ABOUT TWO IN THE AFTERNOON A SLATE CARRYING FIFTEEN THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY PENCE COMES OFF THAT BENCH STONE AND GOES INTO THE DRAWER UNDER IT, AND THE FIGURE ON THE SLATE AND THE FIGURE ON THAT SHEET ARE THE SAME FIGURE, AND THAT DRAWER HAS NEVER BEEN LOCKED IN THAT YARD.** Nobody was thanked for the roof and nobody was thanked for the choice. Shortfall 65,850, being 411 marks, 7 shillings and 6 pence. Columns 269 / 1,222 / none / 125 at the hour and 270 / 1,224 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 538 — *Sunday the Ninth Day of January, a Wipe, the Eighty-Eighth Time, the Wall Down Bare and Up Unrepaired and Six People Walking Past and None of Them With a Bucket, the Berth-Fund Day Paid and Its Reason Given in New Words and Said Out Loud Once, a Slater of About Forty Saying Out Loud at About Eleven That There Is Not One Sill Under That Roof and That He Is Not Going to Be the Man Who Puts a Slate on It, a Man of About Thirty-Three Walking Out to the Mole Head at About Two and Giving One Reason, Nothing Going Out and Nothing Going In, the Shortfall Said Out Loud Unmoved at Sixty-Five Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty*

****THE WALL BEHIND THAT REEVE'S BENCH COMES DOWN BARE FOR THE EIGHTY-EIGHTH TIME AT ABOUT HALF PAST TEN AND GOES UP AT THE ANGLE IT HAS BEEN AT SINCE THE TWELFTH AND SIX PEOPLE WALK PAST IT AND NONE OF THEM PUTS A BUCKET UNDER IT.** The berth-fund reason, said out loud once at the bench stone with the door open on the slip, in words that are neither of the last two wipes: **there was a roof on that shed on Wednesday morning and there is a roof on it now and this yard lost eleven years of shavings and a stock of fir and two benches in between, and a man standing on that slip has noticed that the berth fund paid a day yesterday for four men on a roof instead of on a boat, and he is right that it did and he is wrong about what it means. THAT FUND PAYS FOR A DAY OF WORK AND IT DOES NOT KNOW AND DOES NOT CARE WHAT A MAN DID WITH THE DAY, AND THE SECOND A DAY IS PAID FOR THE USING OF THE DAY THEN THIS YARD IS A HARBOR OFFICE WITH A SLATE IN IT, AND I WOULD RATHER BE A YARD WITH TWENTY-EIGHT PENCE IN A BAG THAN THAT.** A man cut that roof up on Saturday with his own hands because he was hired in advance on Thursday, and he would have been paid the same and been exactly as glad if the man had gone out on the water instead. **AT ABOUT ELEVEN THE SLATER OF ABOUT FORTY COMES BACK AND STANDS IN THE GAP OF THAT DOORWAY FOR ABOUT TEN MINUTES AND LOOKS UP AT A ROOF FINISHED ABOUT SIX HOURS AGO, AND SAYS WHAT HE CAME TO SAY: YOU PUT A ROOF ON IN THREE DAYS ON A TUESDAY SLATE AND IT IS A GOOD ROOF AND I AM NOT SAYING IT IS NOT; THERE IS NOT ONE SILL UNDER ANY OF IT; I AM NOT GOING TO BE THE MAN WHO PUTS A SLATE ON THAT ROOF IN THE SPRING, AND I WANT THAT SAID OUT LOUD IN THAT YARD TODAY SO THAT NOBODY IN THIS HARBOR SPENDS THE WINTER THINKING A MAN HAS BEEN FOUND TO DO IT; THERE ARE ABOUT A YARD OF OLD STONE AT THE EAST END AND NOTHING AT THE WEST, AND I WILL COME AND LOOK AT IT IN THE SPRING.** Nobody asked him what it would cost, nobody offered him anything and he was not thanked. **AT ABOUT TWO A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE WHO HIRES HANDS WALKS OUT TO THE HEAD OF THAT MOLE AND STANDS AT THE RAIL FOR ABOUT TEN MINUTES AND COMES BACK AND SAYS ONE THING: A LINE IS A LINE AND THERE ARE NINE OF THEM AND THEY WERE NINE OF THEM ON SATURDAY AND THEY ARE NINE OF THEM NOW; I WENT OUT AND LOOKED BECAUSE MY BOAT IS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THAT AND THAT IS THE ONLY REASON I HAVE GOT, AND I AM NOT DRESSING IT UP AS ANYTHING ELSE, BECAUSE IT IS A THING THAT TAKES BREAD OFF NINE FAMILIES IN THIS MARKET AND NOT A THING THAT ANYBODY SHOULD MAKE A SPEECH ABOUT.** He says it once and does not say it again. At half past five the shortfall is said out loud unmoved and a man's remark about four sills goes on the slip and not on that sheet, **and it is a Sunday, and the eighty-eighth time is the number this harbor has moved in seven days and not the number anybody will hear about.** Nobody was thanked. Shortfall unmoved at 65,850, being 411 marks, 7 shillings and 6 pence. Columns 270 / 1,227 / none / 125 at the hour and 271 / 1,229 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 539 — *Monday the Tenth Day of January, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Fifteenth Charge in Eleven Trips by Hand and Walked on by None of It, a Man of About Thirty-Three Asking at About Eleven for Two More Days in Advance to the Same Four Men and Being Refused Out Loud in About Twenty Words and Going and Finding a Man Himself, a Man of About Twenty-Nine Asking for a Day Asked for by Name at About One and Being Given One at the Figure in Chalk and Sitting in That Shed From One Until Four Saying Nothing and Being Said Nothing To, Nothing Going Out and Nothing Going In, the Shortfall Said Out Loud Unmoved at Sixty-Five Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty*

****THE CISTERN IS CHARGED FOR THE HUNDRED AND FIFTEENTH TIME IN ELEVEN TRIPS BY HAND AND THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THAT ROTA BOARD IS STILL OFF IT AND THE NEXT OF THOSE IS THURSDAY.** At about eleven, in front of about nine people, **a man of about thirty-three who hires hands asks for two more days in advance to the same four men — six hundred and seventy-two pence — gives his reason in about ten words (there are three instead of four in that yard and the bench is going in today and will go crooked if a man stands and watches it instead of holding it) and says he is not asking this harbor for it but the man who keeps the leaf, and IS REFUSED OUT LOUD IN ABOUT TWENTY WORDS: THAT SHEET IS A THING A STRANGER CAN CHECK BECAUSE EVERYTHING ON IT WAS DECIDED BEFORE ANYBODY WAS TIRED, AND ADDING MEN TO A BILL BECAUSE THE WORK IS GOING BADLY IS HOW A BILL STOPS BEING A BILL; and is told to find a man at the figure in chalk out of his own book and pay him himself and come back and put his hand to the bench, which is free. He says that is not a good offer and he will take it anyway, and he goes and finds a man.** At about one in the afternoon **a man of about twenty-nine asks for a day asked for by name and gives his name and is given one at one hundred and sixty-eight pence and is paid at four with the other three, and sits on a bench in that shed from about one until about four with his forearms on his knees, saying nothing, and nobody in that shed says anything to him, and nobody asks him about the crate of salt cod in a store on the second lay or about the week of a room four days down that coast or about the hut on that shoulder, and nobody asks him about his left side, and no figure in that harbor or on that sheet is set against him and he was not thanked.** The only words said to him in that shed between one and four are a man of about fifty-one who crews four out of the first lay telling him to mind that end of the bench because it has a nail in it, and he said all right. At half past five the shortfall is said out loud unmoved and the six hundred and seventy-two pence refused is called the smallest figure anybody in that harbor has put in front of that shed that month, and it is said that a man sat on that bench for three hours and was paid the same as the three men he sat with and that there is no figure in this yard or on that sheet or in this harbor set against one ear of that man's head and there is not going to be one. Nobody was thanked, including the man who asked and was refused. Shortfall unmoved at 65,850, being 411 marks, 7 shillings and 6 pence. Columns 271 / 1,232 / none / 125 at the hour and 272 / 1,234 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 540 — *Tuesday the Eleventh Day of January, the Sixty-Fourth Wage Tuesday, the Column Read Out on the Step at Ten o'Clock and Not Moving and the Sixty-Fourth Week Fallen Due and Twenty Envelopes Shut in a Chest, a Sheet of Paper Carrying a Date and a Place and Five Lines of Rule and a Seal at the Foot of It and a Name Under That Seal Nailed to the Board at the Head of That Mole at About a Quarter Past Eleven Under a Light That Is Out and Not Opened and Not Copied, a Room over That Fish Market Let Out at About Two With About Twenty People and About Eleven of Them Who Cannot Read, Isel Marn of About Fifty-Six Reading It Out Word for Word Once and Stopping at the Seal and Not Reading the Name and Putting Her Own Name and the Hour Under Her Own Reading, a Man of About Fifty Asking Out Loud Whether His Boat May Leave on Thursday and a Man of About Thirty-Three Asking for the Name to Be Read So He Could Put It on a Slate and Both Refused, the Four Heads Not Changed and No Fifth Head Added on Account of a Declaration, the Shortfall Said Out Loud Unmoved at Sixty-Five Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty*

****THE COLUMN IS READ OUT ON THE STEP BY A CLERK WITH HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR AT THE FOOT OF IT IN FRONT OF ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE OF WHOM ABOUT TWENTY CANNOT READ THE COLUMN ON THE LID, AND IT DOES NOT MOVE AND THE CHEST STOOD SHUT BEHIND THAT DOOR FROM TEN UNTIL FOUR AND NOBODY ASKED TO HAVE IT OPENED AND THE SIXTY-FOURTH WEEK STANDS FALLEN DUE.** At about a quarter past eleven a boat's boat comes up inside that mole with a man in it, a bag and a maul, **and that man nails a sheet of paper to the board at the head of that mole and does not put the maul down while he does it and says nothing to anybody while he does it, under a light that is out and has been out since the seventh of May.** There is a date at the head of it and a place at the head of it, five lines of rule, a seal at the foot and a name written under that seal, and no figure of any kind on the whole of it. The man who keeps the leaf reads it standing up with his hands behind his back about four times, does not take it off that board, puts no line against it on any sheet in that yard, and says two things out loud of which neither is what it means: **that paper is answerable to any man in that harbor who walks up and reads it in the dark, which is the only reason it was nailed up in the dark** — and **THAT NAME IS THE ONLY THING ON THAT PAPER THAT WOULD LET ANYBODY PUT A HAND ON A PERSON, AND IT IS WRITTEN AND NOT SPOKEN, AND A NAME THAT IS WRITTEN IS A FACT AND A NAME THAT IS SAID OUT LOUD IN A ROOM IS A RUMOUR WITH A COAT ON.** At about two a room over that fish market is let out, about twenty people go up those stairs and about eleven of them cannot read what is put in front of them, **and Isel Marn, of about fifty-six, who keeps a chandler's counter at the head of that quay and is not on anything and is a head of nothing, reads that paper out word for word once, in five numbered lines, and stops with her finger about an inch above the seal and does not read the name under it and says out loud why: THERE IS A NAME UNDER THAT SEAL AND I AM NOT GOING TO READ IT; I HAVE READ PAPERS IN THIS ROOM THREE TIMES THIS YEAR AND THE NAMES AT THE BOTTOM OF THEM ARE NEVER THE PART ANYBODY CAN ACT ON, AND THE MINUTE A NAME IS IN A ROOM IT IS IN ABOUT FORTY MOUTHS BY THE MIDDLE OF THE NIGHT; IT IS WRITTEN AND IT STAYS WRITTEN AND I WILL READ THE DAY AND THE PLACE AND THE FIVE LINES AND THE SEAL, AND THAT IS ALL OF THAT PAPER THERE IS; MY OWN NAME AND THE HOUR GO UNDER MINE AND I WILL READ THOSE OUT AT THE END, BECAUSE THOSE TWO ARE MINE AND I KNOW WHAT THEY ARE FOR.** Nobody stopped her at any word and she read it once and not twice. **THE FIVE LINES ARE: that from the hour set down at the head of the paper every stretch of that sea set down at the head of the paper is under martial custody; that no boat of any size shall go past a mark, into or out of that sea, without a permit signed at a coast office, and a permit is not a thing a coast office has agreed to give anybody; that victual, coal, timber, oil, glass and tin may be landed only at the places set down in the second column of a schedule that is not fastened to the paper and is held at a coast office; that no person shall leave that coast while the paper is in force without a permit, and a permit is not given twice to the same person in one month; and that the paper may be read aloud in any room on any coast and nobody shall be charged any figure for hearing it read.** A man of about fifty who owns a boat of about twenty-two tons asks out loud, in front of about twenty people, whether his boat may leave on Thursday, **and is answered out of the second and the fourth of those five lines and not out of anybody's own head: I CAN TELL YOU WHAT THAT PAPER SAYS; I CANNOT TELL YOU WHAT WILL HAPPEN ON THURSDAY AND NEITHER CAN ANYBODY STANDING IN THIS ROOM, AND ANYBODY WHO STANDS UP HERE AND TELLS YOU THAT YOU MAY OR MAY NOT IS NOT READING A PAPER, HE IS MAKING ONE UP IN FRONT OF TWENTY PEOPLE.** A man of about thirty-three who hires hands then asks her to read the name at the foot of it so that he can put it on a slate and take it up the coast to about eleven people in a room four days down that coast, **and is refused in about twenty words: NO; YOU HAVE NOT TOLD ME WHAT THE SLATE IS FOR AND I AM NOT GOING TO PUT A MAN'S NAME IN THIS ROOM'S MOUTH SO THAT IT CAN BE CARRIED UP A COAST ROAD IN SOMEBODY'S COAT; IF IT IS ABOUT A PERMIT THEN THE TWO LINES ON PERMITS CAN BE COPIED OFF WITH A PENCIL, AND IF IT IS ABOUT ANYTHING ELSE THEN PUT IT TO ME WITHOUT A NAME ON IT AND I WILL READ THAT OUT FOR YOU IN FRONT OF THESE TWENTY PEOPLE. He says that was fair and does not put it to her again.** **THE FOUR HEADS ON THAT WALL DID NOT CHANGE AND NO FIFTH HEAD WENT ON IT AND THERE IS NO HEAD OF ANYTHING ON THAT WALL, AND ABOUT NINE PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM SAID ONE THING OUT LOUD, ONE AT A TIME AND IN ABOUT SIX WORDS EACH, THAT THEY WERE GOING TO DO ABOUT IT, AND NOT ONE OF THE NINE SAID THEY WOULD COMPLY WITH IT AND NOT ONE OF THE NINE SAID THEY WOULD NOT.** The man who keeps the leaf names the fitting-out sheet and the four heads separately and out loud in that room and says that a declared sea is not a bill and that this sheet is a bill. At half past five the shortfall is said out loud unmoved and it is said that a sea was declared in that room and it did not move a penny on that sheet, and that the paper from the third of December is still on that board and was not opened, and that there is still no lamp oil at any figure and no flour and no cheaper anything and there are still nine hulls about two sea miles off that mole. **The first column of that leaf has taken one entry against each of the ten days since the first of January and not one of them has gone without an entry; the second has taken five against each, three before the hour and two after; the third took none and nobody has been put in it and the boy's hand is at the head of it and it is still there; the fourth took none and stands at one hundred and twenty-five and is neither shut nor struck; and the read-back is not due until the last page of the fifty.** Nobody was thanked for the reading and nobody was thanked for the reader. Columns 272 / 1,237 / none / 125 at the hour and 273 / 1,239 / none / 125 at the close.**

### Chapter 521 — *Thursday the Twenty-Third, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Tenth Charge Walked on by None of It, Bread and Salt Beef at Two Thousand Four Hundred and a Day Apiece in Advance at Six Hundred and Seventy-Two, Two Wagons Down the Coast Road and Not to Sea, the Man of About Fifty-One Out of a Coast Town Four Days Down Not in That Cart and Not Sent For, the Shortfall at Thirty-Nine Thousand Nine Hundred and Seventy*

**The hundred and tenth cistern is charged at about eight and walked on by none of it, the name at the head of that rota board is still off it, and the figure of that hundred is not said out loud a second time.** Bread and salt beef for nine men for ten days goes on the sheet at 2,400, being fifteen marks, **at the figure a supply boat alongside the west quay is selling it at, which the man who keeps the leaf says out loud is eight hundred pence more than the same article came to on the third of December and one hundred and sixty pence more than the two thousand two hundred and forty chalked on the step at that end stall on the fourteenth, and that he is paying the boat and not the chalk.** A day apiece in advance to the same four men at 672, being four marks, two shillings and eightpence. **TWO WAGONS AND A HANDCART GO DOWN THAT COAST ROAD IN THE MORNING WITH THAT YARD'S GEAR IN THEM AND COME BACK UP IT EMPTY BEFORE DARK, AND THAT GEAR IS LEFT AT THE END OF THAT ROAD UNDER A TARP AULIN WITH A CHAIN AND A PADLOCK ON IT AND NOBODY STANDING OVER IT, AND THE REST OF THAT GEAR GOES DOWN ON THE LAST DAY OF THAT MONTH, WHICH IS THE ONLY DAY ON WHICH THE PARTY LEAVES; THE BOAT DOES NOT GO TO SEA, BECAUSE THE TRENCH IS TWO DAYS' SAIL AWAY AND THE ROAD GOES TO A HARD AND A CANNERY AND A WORKING PLACE WHERE NOBODY IN THIS HARBOR HAS EVER BEEN ASKED ANYTHING; AND HE SAYS HE WILL BE IN THAT HARBOR ON THE FRIDAY AND THE SATURDAY AND WILL BE IN THAT ROOM WHENEVER IT IS LET OUT, BECAUSE A CONDITION IS EITHER ANSWERED IN A ROOM WHERE ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE CANNOT READ IT OR IT IS NOT ANSWERED.** And a man of about fifty-one out of a coast town four days down is in that harbor and is not in that cart and was not sent for and nobody has asked whether he will come, and the man who keeps the leaf says out loud he is not going to be asked either. ### Chapter 522 — *Friday the Twenty-Fourth, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, a Man of About Thirty-Four Up the Coast Road in a Cart With a Chest of Tools, a Room over a Fish Market Let Out at About Two o'Clock With About Twenty People and About Eleven of Them Who Cannot Read, One Condition Stated Out Loud in About Four Sentences and Not Said Twice, Coal for a Pump for Ten Days at Two Thousand Four Hundred, the Four Heads Not Changed and No Fifth Head Going On It, the Shortfall at Forty-Two Thousand Three Hundred and Seventy*

**A man of about thirty-four of a fisher commonwealth at a port four days down that coast, who works and crews and is not a name on a wall or a list or a sheet of anybody's, comes up that coast road in a cart with a chest of lashed tools and a bag of rope, is at the head of that third lay at about eleven o'clock, refuses to say his business on that slip, and is in a room over that market at about two o'clock with about twenty people up those stairs and about eleven of them who cannot read.** He states ONE CONDITION in about four sentences and does not say it twice: the crews of that port will take victual and coal off that coast the way they have always taken it and will put a mark on that coast and name it and keep it and answer for it, **AND A PERSON FROM OUTSIDE THAT COMMONWEALTH DOES NOT HOLD A BUOY AND DOES NOT GO OUT TO IT.** He says in the same breath that he has not come up to be thanked and is not going to be thanked. **NOBODY THANKED HIM. A woman at the back of that room asks out loud whether a person from outside that commonwealth is a person and he says yes, and that the condition is a statement about who goes out to a float in the water in the dark on a tide, and that his own crew put it to him.** Somebody puts the seven and the four of the tenth of December to him and he says those fifteen crews are in this harbor and not in that commonwealth and that the four that wrote no name are not less than the seven that did and that if they want their names on a page at that port they can put them there themselves and no one of them will be asked twice. **A man of about thirty-three who hires hands says out loud that the four heads on that wall cannot send anybody anywhere and that whatever this party decides will not be decided by anybody standing in front of that wall, and the man of about thirty-four says he will be in that room on the Saturday and will not read it again, because a condition that has to be read twice is a doubt.** Coal for that pump for ten days at 2,400, being fifteen marks, with the whole of the line said out loud first including the yard's own rule about a line and the day it is written. **THE FOUR HEADS DID NOT CHANGE AND NO FIFTH HEAD WENT ON IT AND THE SHEET THAT CARRIES THE MONEY IS ON NO WALL IN THAT ROOM.** Shortfall 42,370, being 264 marks, 10 shillings and 10pence. ### Chapter 523 — *Saturday the Twenty-Fifth, a Room over a Fish Market Let Out at About Two o'Clock With About Twenty People and About Eleven of Them Who Cannot Read, Eleven Words Said Out Loud in That Room in Front of All of Them and Not a Speech and Not a Thank-You and Not a Restoration, Four Lines With His Own Name and an Hour Under Each Going Onto the Face of the Record That Room Keeps and Read Out Twice, Two Buoys, Two Bells and About Sixty Fathoms of Line at One Thousand One Hundred and Twenty, the Shortfall at Forty-Three Thousand Four Hundred and Ninety*

**TWO FLOATS OF TARRED FIR, TWO CAST BELLS AND ABOUT SIXTY FATHOMS OF TWO-INCH STUFF GO OUT OF THAT YARD ON A BARROW AND ALONG THAT QUAY TO A BOAT, AND THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF PUTS ONE LINE ON THE SHEET AND SAYS OUT LOUD FIRST THAT HE IS NOT PUTTING WHAT THOSE BUOYS ARE FOR INTO ANY BOOK UNTIL THE WORDS OF IT HAVE BEEN SAID IN A ROOM WHERE ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE CANNOT READ THEM.** At about two o'clock the room is let out, about twenty people go up those stairs and about eleven cannot read what is put in front of them, and the man of about thirty-four is standing at the side of that room and is not asked to say anything. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO STANDS UP, SAYS HE IS GOING TO ANSWER THE CONDITION, SAYS IT ONCE, SAYS NOBODY IS GOING TO BE ASKED WHETHER THEY AGREE WITH IT, AND WHEN A MAN AT THE BACK SAYS THAT A MAN WHO SAYS IN FRONT OF A ROOM THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO BE THANKED IS SAYING IT TO BE THANKED, HE SAYS NO IN FOUR WORDS AND DOES NOT SAY IT AGAIN. THEN HE SAYS THE ELEVEN WORDS AND THEY ARE ALL OF IT: "We don't set the buoys, don't go out, and aren't told." A woman at the back asks what a person does on that coast and he says a person does whatever the crews of that port tell him to do, and that he will be one of the men carrying victual and coal for a port four days down that coast, and that is the whole of it. HE WAS NOT THANKED AND WAS NOT RESTORED BY IT.** At about half past two four lines go onto the face of the record that room keeps in his own hand, each with his own name and an hour under it: that this party does not set a buoy on that coast and does not hold one and does not go out to one; that it has given the naming, the keeping and the answering for of every mark there to the crews of that port and will not ask for any of it back; that it is not told what a route there is doing and will not ask to be told this winter; and **that this party is one body among the bodies on that coast and is not the body that decides, and a buoy is a thing on a quay and not a desk.** **Hobb Lee, of about forty-six, who mends nets on the third lay, reads them out twice, word for word, at about half past two and again at about ten to three, with his own name and the hour of each reading at the foot, and nobody stopped him at any word in either.** The man of about thirty-four reads them over himself and says they are a fair copy of what he heard and that he is not signing anything and that the third of them will be true in a month and not on that Saturday. And at about ten past three he is asked whether the crews of that port will come up and put marks here, and says: **"You will get the condition and you will not get a man. ### Chapter 524 — *Sunday the Twenty-Sixth, a Wipe, the Eighty-Sixth Time, the Wall Behind a Reeve's Bench Down Bare and Up Unrepaired and Nobody With a Bucket, a Day of the Berth Fund Paid and Its Reason Given in New Words and Said Out Loud Once, a Page Up on the Boards of That Market at About Half Past One With Four Local Names at the Head of It and Five Marks and His Name Nowhere on It, the Four Heads Not Changed and the Fitting-Out Sheet on No Wall in That Room, the Shortfall Unmoved at Forty-Three Thousand Four Hundred and Ninety*

**THE WALL BEHIND THAT REEVE'S BENCH COMES DOWN BARE FOR THE EIGHTY-SIXTH TIME AT ABOUT HALF PAST TEN IN THE MORNING, GOES UP WHOLE AT THE ANGLE IT HAS BEEN AT SINCE THE TWELFTH, AND FIVE PEOPLE WALK PAST IT AND NOT ONE OF THEM PUTS A BUCKET UNDER IT. A DAY OF THE BERTH FUND IS PAID AT TEN AND A DAY IS PAID AT FOUR AND THE FIGURE IN CHALK DOES NOT MOVE AND THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF SAYS OUT LOUD ONCE, IN NEW WORDS, THAT A FUND PAYS THE DAY THE WORK WAS DONE AND A MAN WHO PUT A WALL UP ON A SUNDAY IS OWED THAT SUNDAY BY WHOEVER HE PUT IT UP FOR, AND THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO BE TOLD BY HIM THAT HIS SUNDAY DEPENDS ON A DAY OF THE WEEK.** At about half past one a page goes up on a wall of the floor of that market on four tacks: **THE BUOYS LIST, WITH FOUR NAMES AT THE HEAD OF IT AND THE MARKS EACH ANSWERS FOR AGAINST EACH NAME, BEING JORY ANSE OF THE OSYRA, NINE MEN, THE FIRST MARK; BEL HESK OF THE CORDLE, SIX MEN, THE SECOND MARK; TAM RIEVE OF THE SENNET, FOUR MEN, THE THIRD MARK, WHICH IS A BELL AND NOT A FLOAT; AND THE CREWS OF THAT PORT TOGETHER, FIVE MARKS BETWEEN THEM AND THE PUTTING OF ANY OF THEM.** **THE NAME OF THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO IS NOT ON THAT PAGE AND IS NOT UNDER IT AND IS NOT ON THE BACK OF IT EITHER, AND HE DID NOT ASK TO HAVE IT ON IT, AND NOBODY IN THAT MARKET SUGGESTED THAT IT OUGHT TO BE, AND NOBODY WAS THANKED FOR THE PAGE GOING UP.** Hobb Lee puts it up and says out loud that a list of who answers for what is a list of what people have agreed to answer for and that anybody who had not agreed to answer for anything is not on it and is not going to be put on it. A woman with an end stall asks whether a person from this harbor could put a name on it, and he says she could do it tomorrow morning and the list would be tacked up again with a fifth line and nobody in that market could stop her, and that what would happen to her is that the crews of that port would find out, because that page goes down that coast in a cart on Monday and does not come back. **The man who keeps the leaf then stands in the room over that market and says out loud that the sheet that carries the money is not in that room and is not on any wall in it, and that the four heads on that wall are the four heads on that wall, and that a buoys list with four names on it went up on the boards an hour ago and is a different thing, and that the two are named separately so that nobody could go away thinking that a name under the four heads is the same as a name under a mark, and they are not.** Nobody in that room asked for either. Shortfall unmoved at 43,490, being 271 marks, 10 shillings and 10pence. Columns 257 / 1,159 / none / 125.

### Chapter 525 — *Monday the Twenty-Seventh, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Eleventh Charge Walked on by None of It, Line, Glass, Tin and Gaskets for a Second Pressure Case at One Thousand Two Hundred and Eighty and a Day Apiece in Advance to the Same Four Men at Six Hundred and Seventy-Two, Eleven Words Said Out Loud at the Bench Stone at About Half Past Eleven in Front of About Nine Men, the Shortfall at Forty-Five Thousand Four Hundred and Forty-Two*

**THE CISTERN IS CHARGED FOR THE HUNDRED AND ELEVENTH TIME AND IS WALKED ON BY NONE OF IT AND THE NAME AT THE HEAD OF THAT ROTA BOARD IS STILL OFF IT.** A second pressure case goes onto the sheet at 1,280, being eight marks, with the whole line said out loud first, being thirty feet of two-inch stuff, a pane about the size of two hands laid flat, a ring of tin and four gaskets, **and that a pane that a glove goes over every time a man gets into it stops being a thing you can see through and a scratched pane at four fathoms gets worse and not better.** A day apiece in advance to the same four men at 672. The four men ask whether that pressure case is for going out to the buoys and the man who keeps the leaf says that a pressure case is for a man going into water and that whether that man is going to a buoy of that port or to a stone on this quay is not a line on this sheet and is not going to be. **AND AT ABOUT HALF PAST ELEVEN IN THE MORNING THE WHOLE OF THAT WORKING PARTY'S OWN BOOK ON THE DAY OF THE THREE IS ELEVEN WORDS AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO SAYS THEM OUT LOUD AT THE BENCH STONE IN FRONT OF ABOUT NINE MEN: "We are not going to be on that water at all on the day of the three."** A man asks what he means, since a party of nine with two pressure cases is not a thing that stays off a quay, and he says he means that the day of the three is not this yard's day and not this yard's water and not this yard's mark, and that the mark on that water belongs to two crews of this harbor who took a channel each on the twenty-first and held the two ends of that line between them and struck a bell once, and that if the day of the three is done it will be done by three men asked in the same words at the same rate and this yard will carry a slate and pull a cutoff and hold a boat. **A man of about thirty-three who hires hands says out loud that that sounds like a party giving up the only water it has ever been any good at, and he says that it is not giving anything up, it is that this party put a mark in four fathoms on the twenty-first with two ends of a line and not three and crossed on four boats and not five, and that a thing that stops when one of three stops is not a thing anybody gets to keep, and that two local crews in this harbor know that better than he does because they were two of the three that were asked.** A man of about thirty-eight who works the compressor asks at about one o'clock whether three men in about four fathoms with a line between them is the same as three men with a line between them and somebody going to a float on it afterward, and is told no, and that this party is not going to be one of the three on that water on that day and said so out loud in front of nine men at about half past eleven, **and that the man of about thirty-eight was the only person in that shed who had understood it the first time and that was not a thing anybody was going to make anything of.** Shortfall 45,442, being 284 marks and twopence. ### Chapter 526 — *Tuesday the Twenty-Eighth, the Sixty-Second Wage Tuesday, the Column at Twenty-Six Lines and One Hundred and Four Marks With Twenty Envelopes in a Chest and Not Moving and a Further Week Fallen Due, a Twelfth Week of That Winter in the Column and Nobody Says a Word About It, Three Days of Air at Nine Hundred and Sixty With the Whole of the Line Said Out Loud and the Man Who Keeps the Leaf Saying That Line Is Not for the Three and the Three Are Not Going on It, the Shortfall at Forty-Six Thousand Four Hundred and Two*

**A CLERK OF THAT HARBOR AUTHORITY READS THE COLUMN OUT ON THE STEP AT THE BACK OF THAT MARKET AT TEN O'CLOCK IN FRONT OF ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE AND ABOUT TWENTY OF THEM CANNOT READ THE COLUMN ON THE LID AND PUTS HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR AT THE FOOT OF THE READING, AND THE COLUMN DOES NOT MOVE AND NOBODY IS PAID A PENNY OUT OF THAT CHEST AND THE SIXTY-SECOND WEEK STANDS FALLEN DUE.** **THE COLUMN HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF NOVEMBER, WHEN THE TWENTY-SIXTH LINE AND THE LAST FOUR MARKS WENT ONTO IT, AND IT HAD BEEN TWENTY-FIVE LINES AND ONE HUNDRED MARKS THE WEEK BEFORE, AND NOTHING HAS GONE ON IT SINCE.** A man at the back of that step says out loud, in front of about forty people, that there is a twelfth week of this winter in there somewhere, and somebody else says the twelfth, and he says the twelfth week, and a woman at the front of that step asks the twelfth of what, and nobody answers her, and the clerk goes on reading the next line and nobody stopped him and the twelfth week of that winter went back into the column without a word. **Three days of air go onto the sheet at 960, being six marks, with the twenty-eighth of December against it, and the man who keeps the leaf says the whole line out loud before he writes a figure against it AND SAYS OUT LOUD THAT THAT LINE IS NOT FOR THE THREE AND THE THREE ARE NOT GOING ON IT, BEING THREE DAYS OF AIR FOR A COMPRESSOR AND NOT FOR A PERSON, AND THAT AIR IS BOUGHT IN ADVANCE OR NOT AT ALL.** A man of about thirty-three who hires hands says everything on that sheet this month is for the three and is told no in about four words. At about two o'clock a room over that market is let out with about twenty people up those stairs and about eleven who cannot read, **and nothing is read out in that room on that Tuesday**: a man of about fifty who owns a boat of about twenty-two tons stands at the back for half an hour and says nothing, a ropemaker of about sixty-one comes up those stairs for the first time in a month, stands by the door, says nothing, leaves before three o'clock and puts nothing in, and the four heads did not change. At about half past five the man who keeps the leaf says the shortfall out loud and says the wage column thing once, out loud, in that yard's own mouth, **being that a wage Tuesday is a harbor finding out what it owes and the finding out is not a payment, and that this yard writes its own out at half past five because this yard is answerable for what it spends and is not answerable for what a council four hundred yards from here has not voted.** Shortfall 46,402, being 290 marks and twopence. Columns 259 / 1,169 / none / 125.

### Chapter 527 — *Wednesday the Twenty-Ninth, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, a Day's Hire of a Boat and Two Men to Run the Buoys at Three Hundred and Thirty-Six With the Whole of the Line Said Out Loud Including That Those Two Men Are Not on That Sheet and Are Not Counted on It, Five Sentences Written at the Head of a Page at About Half Past Eight in the Morning Before Anybody Was Asked Anything, Three Men Asked Out Loud One at a Time and Not in Front of the Other Two Whether They Will Each Hold One Channel of the Same Stretch of About Four Fathoms Off That Third Lay, Each One Told Before He Was Asked That He May Stop It and That Nobody Will Ask Him Which Channel It Was, the Shortfall at Forty-Six Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty-Eight*

**A day's hire of a boat and two men to run the buoys goes onto the sheet at 336, being two marks, one shilling and fourpence, off a boat that is not the berth fund's and not this yard's, with the whole of the line said out loud first INCLUDING THAT THOSE TWO MEN ARE NOT ON THAT SHEET AND ARE NOT COUNTED ON IT, THAT THEIR NAMES ARE IN THE BOOK THE DAYS ARE PAID OUT OF, AND THAT THAT SHEET CARRIES NO COUNT OF PERSONS AND HAS NEVER CARRIED ONE.** **FIVE SENTENCES GO ONTO THE HEAD OF A PAGE ON THAT BENCH STONE AT ABOUT HALF PAST EIGHT IN THE MORNING, BEFORE ANYBODY HAD BEEN ASKED ANYTHING, AND ARE NOT ALTERED AFTER THAT HOUR ON THAT DAY BY ANYBODY, AND THEY SAY IN THE HOUSE'S OWN WORDS THAT THE STRETCH IS ABOUT FOUR FATHOMS OFF THAT THIRD LAY AND ABOUT TWO HUNDRED YARDS LONG WITH THE FLOAT IN IT, THAT THERE ARE THREE OF THEM ASKED AND THREE THINGS TO HOLD AND NO NAME ON ANY OF THEM, THAT NOBODY IS GOING TO BE ASKED WHY OR WHETHER HE IS SURE AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE TOLD WHICH ONE HE TOOK, THAT A MAN ASKED MAY STOP IT AT ANY HOUR AND WILL NOT BE ASKED WHEN OR WHY AND IT WILL BE RECORDED THAT WAY AND NOT ANY OTHER WAY, AND THAT NOBODY IS PAID FOR IT AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM CAN SEND ANYBODY ANYWHERE.** **Three men are asked one at a time and not in front of the other two, and the five are read out word for word to each before each is asked anything else, and the two other men are not in that shed at the hour either of them is asked.** A man of about fifty-one who crews four out of the first lay asks one question, which is whether the bell will be struck and by whom, is told the tender on the surface will strike it and will not be in the water at any hour, and says yes and asks nothing further. A man of about thirty-three who runs a lighter of about eleven tons on the west quay says yes in one word and then says out loud, on his own account and before anybody asked him, that if he stops it he will say so in the room and not on the water, and that he wanted that written down, and it was written down with the hour against it. **A man of about thirty-eight who works that compressor asks one question and gets one answer, being whether there will be three of them in the water at any hour, is told there will be one at a time and this yard's man will be on the surface in a dinghy with a cutoff and on the compressor and not in the water and is not one of the three and is not going to be, and then says yes.** **HE IS NOT THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO SAID NO ON THE TWENTY-FIRST OF DECEMBER ABOUT A CHANNEL; HE IS A DIFFERENT MAN ON THE SAME HARBOR, AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED CONNECTED THE TWO THINGS AND NOBODY WAS GOING TO, AND THE MAN WHO SAID NO HAS NOT BEEN ASKED ABOUT THAT NO SINCE HE SAID IT.** Shortfall 46,738, being 292 marks, 1 shilling and 6pence.
