### Chapter 528 — *Thursday the Thirtieth, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Twelfth Charge Walked on by None of It, Air for the Day of the Three at One Thousand One Hundred and Twenty With the Whole of the Line Said Out Loud and Every Descent of That Day on That Line and on No Other, Three Slates Written Before Anybody Was Off the Boat With a Reason in Each Man's Own Words and the Hour and a Figure of Twenty-Five Minutes, a Named Tender on the Surface and Not in the Water and an Independent Line and a Physical Anchor Seated on That Floor and a Cutoff He Could Pull Without Asking, One Man in the Water at a Time and Nobody in Twice and Nobody in at the Top of a Flood, a Consent Failure on the Page at About Half Past Twelve Wherein One of the Three Asks Out Loud for a Channel to Be Dropped and the Drop Is Made and Nobody Argues and Nobody Asks Him Which, the Held Water About a Hundred and Ten Yards of Two Hundred and the Other Ninety Yards Water Nobody Has Looked At, Three Accounts That Fit Together and Do Not Agree About One Thing, a Shared Aftertaste Paid in Three Mouths at Once at About Six o'Clock, a Man of About Thirty-Two Not Certain Which of the Three Accounts Is His Own, the Shortfall at Forty-Seven Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty-Eight*

**THE STAGE IS TAKEN HERE, ONCE, IN THIS CHAPTER, AND IS NOT TAKEN AGAIN.** Three slates are written at about half past eleven in the morning before anybody is off that slip, each with the reason in that man's own words and the hour against it and **a figure of twenty-five minutes**: a man of about fifty-one who crews four out of the first lay, because there is a setters mark under that float and nobody in this harbor knows what is under it and he would rather know before somebody goes out on it; **EACH OF THE THREE SLATES IS SIGNED WITH A LAY AND A DATE AND AN HOUR AND NOT WITH A NAME, BEING THE FIRST LAY, THE WEST QUAY AND THE SECOND LAY, ALL THREE OF THEM AGAINST THE TWENTY-NINTH OF DECEMBER AT ABOUT HALF PAST EIGHT, WHICH IS THE MORNING THE THREE SAID THE WORDS AND WERE ASKED IN THEM; AND THE THREE MEN OF THOSE LAYS ARE NOT THE THREE MASTERS OF THE OSYRA, THE CORDLE AND THE SENNET, WHOSE NAMES WENT UP ON THE BOARDS OF THAT MARKET ON THE SUNDAY, AND THOSE THREE ARE FOUR DAYS DOWN THAT COAST**; a man of about thirty-three of the west quay, because he has run a lighter of about eleven tons over that water in the dark twice a week for nineteen years and has never once been told what the bottom of it does; and a man of about thirty-eight who works that compressor, because that compressor has run for nineteen years and he has heard that float come up against its own board in the dark on a falling tide and has never had an answer about it and there is nobody to ask. **IVO SARK, OF ABOUT TWENTY-FOUR, IS THE NAMED TENDER ON THE SURFACE IN A DINGHY ABOUT NINE FEET OFF THAT SLIP WITH HIS OWN HAND ON THE CHAIN WEIGHT AND A CUTOFF HE COULD PULL WITHOUT ASKING ANYBODY'S LEAVE AND HE IS NOT IN THAT WATER AT ANY HOUR OF THAT DAY; NESSA PIKE, OF ABOUT TWENTY-SEVEN, IS ON THE COMPRESSOR; THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF SAT WITH THE BOOK AND THE SLATES AND THE HOURS AND WAS NOT THE TENDER AND SAID OUT LOUD THAT THE TENDER WAS NOT GOING TO BE HIM, BEING THAT A MAN WHO WRITES THE HOURS IS NOT THE MAN WITH THE CUTOFF.** **THE PLAN ON THE BENCH STONE IS TWO HUNDRED YARDS OF THAT WATER IN THREE CHANNELS, ONE TO A MAN, AND THEY ARE NOT EVEN LENGTHS AND NOBODY MEASURED THEM AGAINST EACH OTHER: THE NORTH ONE ABOUT NINETY YARDS, THE MIDDLE ONE ABOUT A HUNDRED YARDS, AND THE SOUTH ONE A SHORT PIECE NOBODY MEASURED.** **THE CONSENT FAILURE IS ON THE PAGE.** At about half past twelve, before anybody is off that slip, the man of about thirty-three of the west quay says, standing up, in about nine words: **give one of them up, take a channel off the table before anybody is off the slip and put the water that was on it back to being water nobody has looked at. The man who keeps the leaf rubs one of the three lines off the slate and writes the hour against the rubbing-out, and NOBODY ASKS HIM WHICH CHANNEL IT WAS AND NOBODY ARGUED WITH HIM ABOUT IT AND HE WAS NOT THANKED AND NO FIGURE IS SET AGAINST HIM. THE HELD WATER BECOMES ABOUT A HUNDRED AND TEN YARDS OUT OF TWO HUNDRED AND ABOUT NINETY YARDS AT THE NORTH END IS WATER NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS LOOKED AT, AND 110 + 90 = 200. THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE WAS ASKED FOR THE NORTH ONE AND THE NORTH ONE IS THE ONE THAT WENT, AND NOBODY WAS ASKED WHICH.** **THE THREE GO DOWN ONE AT A TIME ON A FALLING TIDE AND A MAKING: the first over the rail at about ten past one and out at about thirty-five minutes past one, being five minutes down, eighteen on the bottom and two up, which is twenty-five of his twenty-five, with the cutoff called at about thirty-three minutes past one because he had said nothing for two minutes and pulled without anybody asking and the word about four seconds later; the second over at about ten past two and out at about thirty-five minutes past two, twenty-five of his twenty-five, who did not ask to come up and was not pulled on and who asked, in the boat, for a cup of water and nothing else; the third over at about ten past three and out at about thirty-five minutes past three, twenty-five of his twenty-five, with the cutoff called at about thirty-three minutes past three and pulled without anybody asking. NOBODY WENT IN TWICE, NO TWO MEN WERE IN IT AT ONCE, NOBODY WENT IN AT THE TOP OF THAT FLOOD, AN ASCENT A MAN ASKED FOR WAS NOT ARGUED WITH, NOBODY WAS HURT, NOBODY HAS NAMED ANY OF THEM A CASUALTY, NO FIGURE IS SET AGAINST ANY OF THEM AND NONE OF THEM WAS THANKED.** **AT ABOUT HALF PAST FOUR THE THREE GIVE THREE ACCOUNTS AND THEY FIT TOGETHER AND ARE MORE THAN ANY ONE OF THEM HAD: about eleven fathoms of chain in a curve under that float curving away north and moving against the stone twice with about four seconds between; water coming over one man in one direction and going back in the other in the shape of that curve; and the chain not lying on the floor at all but down in something about a foot and a half wide and about a foot deep running north, into which a man put his whole forearm twice and it went in to the elbow. IT IS NOT A RECORDING AND NOT A VERDICT AND NOT A ROUTE AND IT CANNOT BE TAKEN OFF A PAGE WITH A PENCIL BECAUSE IT IS THREE MEN'S MOUTHS IN A SHED. AND THE THREE OF THEM DO NOT AGREE ABOUT ONE THING, BEING WHETHER THAT FLOAT WAS BEING HELD BY ITS LINE OR WAS LOOSE IN THAT WATER, AND THEY ARE KEPT DISAGREEING: one says the line held it, one says the line was slack and a line on a stone is not a hand, and one says he was watching the trough and is not going to make an account up. NOBODY SETTLED IT, IT WENT INTO THE SECOND COLUMN IN THE ORDER IT WAS SAID AND NOT INTO THE FIRST, AND THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF WAS ASKED FOR HIS OPINION AND SAID HE HAD NOT GOT ONE AND WAS NOT GOING TO GET ONE.** **AT ABOUT SIX O'CLOCK ALL THREE SAID OUT LOUD, IN THREE MOUTHS AT ONCE, THAT THEY HAD THE SAME THING: a sweetness at the back of the throat, a pressure behind the eyes that was not a headache, and a want to be quiet that lasted about ten minutes and went off of its own accord. IT WAS PAID IN THAT SHED, IT WAS NOT A LESSON AND IT WAS NOT A SPEECH, NOBODY WAS THANKED, NO FIGURE IS SET AGAINST IT AND NONE OF THE THREE IS A MEMBER OF ANYTHING. AND AT ABOUT TEN TO SEVEN THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-TWO, WHO KEPT THE BOOK AND THE SLATES AND THE HOURS AND WAS NOT THE TENDER AND WAS NOT IN THAT WATER AT ANY HOUR OF THAT AFTERNOON, SAID OUT LOUD TO ABOUT NINE MEN THAT HE WAS NOT CERTAIN WHICH OF THE THREE ACCOUNTS WAS HIS OWN, IN ABOUT TWENTY WORDS, AND DID NOT EXPLAIN IT AND NOBODY ASKED HIM TO.** Shortfall 47,858, being 299 marks, 1 shilling and 6pence. Columns 261 / 1,179 / none / 125.

### Chapter 529 — *Friday the Thirty-First, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, Nothing Going Out and Nothing Going In, the Man Who Keeps the Leaf Saying That What the Three Did on the Thirtieth Is Not on That Sheet and Never Is Going to Be and That the Air Is, Three Men Asked About the One Thing They Do Not Agree About, One at a Time and Separately and Not in Front of Each Other, at About Ten o'Clock, About Half Past Eleven and About One o'Clock, Three Accounts That Do Not Agree Entered in the Second Column in the Order They Were Said and Not Settled, a Woman of Thirty of No Office Saying That a Man Who Says He Does Not Know Is a Man Who Has Said Where His Knowledge Stops, a Man of About Thirty-Two Not Certain Which of the Three Accounts Is His Own and the Aftertaste Not Lifted, the Shortfall Unmoved at Forty-Seven Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty-Eight*

**Three questions go onto the head of a page at about half past eight in the morning about the one thing the three did not agree about, are not altered after that hour, and each of the three is asked them one at a time and separately and not in front of the other two at about ten o'clock, about half past eleven and about one o'clock.** Nobody was asked his reason, nobody was asked whether he was sure, nobody was told what either of the other two had said, and each of the three was told before he was asked anything that nobody would be asked to agree with anybody and that nobody would be asked to say it a second time. **The man of about fifty-one says the line held it and that the line was taut the whole time and that a thing that is loose goes where the water puts it and that thing did not. The man of about thirty-three says he will not agree with the other two and has not been told what they said and does not want to be told, that the float was loose in his water and the line was slack by the fifth minute and that a line on a stone is a line on a stone and is not a hand. The man of about thirty-eight says he was watching the trough and not the float, that he has not got an account of the float and is not going to make one up for that book on that bench stone, and that whoever of the two of them is right the trough is there, a foot and a half wide, going north, and he put his arm in it twice and it went in to the elbow, and that is his and is the only thing in that water he would put his name to.** They are not settled and nobody was asked to agree with anybody. **A woman of thirty of no office is asked, in that shed, in front of about nine people, whether three accounts that do not agree about one thing are a finding, and answers in about forty words that a man who says he does not know is not half of a finding, that he is a man who has said where his knowledge stops, and that that is the only part of the three of them anybody can lean on tomorrow, and that the other two have each got a thing they are sure of and are sure of different things and a page that says so can be read out loud. She was not thanked. The man who keeps the leaf says he had not asked for an opinion, she says he had asked her a question, and he then says out loud that he has not got an opinion and is not going to get one, and that anybody who wants his opinion on whether a float is held or loose can go down to four fathoms with a slate and find out, and that the slate would be thirty feet of three-inch on its own weight and a figure of twenty-five minutes and a man on a compressor and a cutoff, and that is what the sheet is for.** **The man of about thirty-two is not asked about his own uncertainty, because he said it once in front of nine people and that is what he owes that room, and asking again would have turned a thing he said into a thing he owes. THE AFTERTASTE FROM THE THIRTIETH HAD NOT LIFTED: all three still had it on the Friday in three separate places, and one of them said out loud that it was not getting better and was not getting worse and that he had stopped expecting it to, and nobody asked him what it was like and nobody wrote a figure against it and nobody in that harbor has made it lift and it is not a condition anybody there is going to fix.** Shortfall unmoved at 47,858, being 299 marks, 1 shilling and 6pence. Columns 262 / 1,184 / none / 125.

### Chapter 530 — *Saturday the First Day of January, Not a Rota Day and Not a Wage Tuesday and Not a Wipe, the Only Thing Anybody Says About the Day Being the First of a Month Being That It Is a Saturday and That a Day Asked for by Name Is Paid on a Saturday at the Figure in Chalk, a Page Carrying the Crossing of the Thirtieth and the Names of Three Men and the Refusal of One Channel With No Name Against It Read Out Once With the Reader's Own Name and the Hour Under It, a Man of About Thirty-Three Asking Out Loud Who Reads Out in That Room and Being Told That Nobody in That Room Decides Where a Boat Goes, the Four Heads Not Changed and the Four Standing Lines the Four Standing Lines, the Shortfall Said Out Loud at Forty-Seven Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty-Eight and Nobody Asked for the Rest of It, the Bag at Twenty-Eight Pence*

**A page carrying the crossing of the thirtieth and the names of three men on it and the refusal of one channel on it is read out once, word for word, at about two o'clock in the afternoon by Hobb Lee, of about forty-six, who mends nets on the third lay, with his own name and the hour under it, in front of about twenty people of whom about eleven cannot read it and hear all of it, and nobody stopped him at any word.** Its five lines say that three men went into about four fathoms off the head of the third lay one at a time and each held one channel, that they were asked in the same words before they were asked anything and each was told before he was asked that he might stop it and that nobody would ask him which channel it was; **that before any of the three went down one of the three asked out loud for one of the three channels to be dropped and the drop was made and nobody argued with him about it and nobody asked him which channel it was and he was not thanked and no figure is set against him**; that they said three accounts at about half past four and that they do not agree about one thing and were not settled and nobody was asked to agree with anybody; that the stretch now held is about a hundred and ten yards and about ninety yards at the north end is water nobody in this harbor has looked at; and that all three came up and all three said out loud in that shed on the evening of the thirtieth that they had the same thing in their mouths, that it was still there on the thirty-first, and that no figure has been set against any of it and none of the three is a member of anything. **THERE IS NO NAME AGAINST THE SECOND OF THOSE FIVE LINES AND NO REASON AGAINST IT EITHER, AND THE MAN WHO ASKED FOR THAT CHANNEL TO BE DROPPED IS NOT ON THAT PAGE IN ANY OTHER PLACE, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM ASKED ABOUT IT AFTER THE READING AND NOBODY HAS ASKED ABOUT IT SINCE.** A woman of about thirty-one asks out loud whether the man who gave up a channel is the man who was asked for a date by a Crown officer in a room on the west basin on the ninth of December, and Hobb Lee says he is not going to say. **A man of about thirty-three who hires hands then asks, out loud, in front of about twenty people of whom about eleven cannot read, who reads out in that room when a thing is on a page in that shed, and nobody answers for about five seconds, and Hobb Lee says the man who keeps the leaf reads out whatever that yard has on its own slip, and that the fitting-out sheet that carries the money is not on any wall in that room and was not read out in it on that day and is not going to be, and that the four heads on that wall are claims and refusals and restricted records and a public correction and that they are four and are not going to be five, and then: "Nobody in this room decides where a boat goes and that includes the man who keeps the leaf and it includes the man who was in that water on Thursday. No route and no account and nothing of that kind is on that wall for anybody who has not asked to be represented, and no man in this harbor has asked, and the man who gave up his buoys on the twenty-fifth of December has his name nowhere on that page and is not on any of the four lines and did not ask to be."** **The man of about thirty-two was not in that room and was not sent for and has not been asked to come.** At about half past five the man who keeps the leaf says the shortfall out loud with the door open on the slip and says that a figure of a hundred and ten yards of water is in three men's heads and is on that sheet nowhere, and that the only place it is written down is the second column of that leaf in three men's own words, and that is the correct order and he is not going to change it; and then he says the thing the movement ends on, once, in that yard's own mouth: **a commonwealth said yes to one condition and the condition has been kept and this yard is not thanked for it and is not thanked for anything and no part of that condition has put a shilling cheaper on a table in this harbor — the lamp oil is at four hundred and fifty pence and there is no flour in that market and no barley in it and no barrel of lamp oil since the twenty-ninth day of August and the mole head has been dark since the seventh of May and the hose will be dead until the spring and the tide gang is four men short and the third lay is a berth short and nineteen winters are on a page in an office on the west basin and the wage column is at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks with the sixty-third week fallen due on Tuesday; and this yard put a mark in four fathoms, asked three people to hold it, gave it up, and cannot be told what a route on that coast is doing. Nobody in that harbor has any cheaper food because of it and nobody has any dearer food because of it either and the two of those are the same thing.** Shortfall 47,858, being 299 marks, 1 shilling and 6pence. Columns 263 / 1,189 / none / 125.

## Volume 11, Batch 0002 (Chapters 511–520), Movement 2, *a supply boat at a figure, a commonwealth that will not sign, and a proof that a crew can refuse a channel and the route stays up* — as written, 29 September 2026. **THE MOVEMENT IS PAID. THE VOLUME IS TWENTY CHAPTERS OLD OF FIFTY. THE TEN DAYS RUN MONDAY THE THIRTEENTH DAY OF DECEMBER TO WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND, ONE DAY TO A CHAPTER, NO DAY MISSING AND NO DAY IN TWO CHAPTERS, AND NO CHAPTER STATES A YEAR. ### Chapter 511 — *Monday the Thirteenth, the Hundred and Seventh Charge Walked on by None of It, Bread and Salt Beef at One Thousand Nine Hundred and Twenty and a Day Apiece in Advance at Six Hundred and Seventy-Two, the Hard at Another Port Answered Out Loud by a Working Person of That Port of About Fifty With a Condition Attached, the Three Marks Not Going, the Shortfall at Thirty-One Thousand Nine Hundred and Seventy*

**A man of about fifty who fits boat bottoms, who has been in that harbor nine weeks with a chest of tools against a wall by a door and a bed above a chandler's on the second lay, and who owns no boat in that harbor and is not the man of the twenty-two tons, stands up in the middle of a room over that market at about half past one in the afternoon and says he is from that port, and gives the answer that has been standing at that hard since the ninth of November past, in about eleven words, on his own hook, with a condition attached to it: the boats at that hard will take victual off the outside at the top of the flood and carry it up to the cannery steps, and coal the same way, and nothing else off that hard, and the first of anything else that comes up it will be put back on the water where it was found and will not be opened by anybody at that port, and not one man of this harbor comes past the fish quay there. AND HE SAYS THE THREE MARKS ARE NOT HIS AND NOT THEIRS AND ARE ON THE NINTH OF NOVEMBER AND ARE GOING TO STAY ON THE NINTH OF NOVEMBER, AND THAT HE IS HERE ON HIS OWN HOOK AND NOT OFFERING IT TO A ROOM THAT CANNOT AGREE WITH HIM. NOBODY THANKED HIM, NO FIGURE WAS SET AGAINST HIM OR AGAINST THAT PARTY, THE ENTRY IS NOT SETTLED, THE THREE MARKS DID NOT GO, AND A CLAIM IS NOT A DEBT.** Bread and salt beef for nine men for ten days at 1,920, being twelve marks, at the figure the increase of the fourth of December set, and a day apiece in advance to the same four men at 672. ### Chapter 501 — *Friday the Third, Nine Hulls About Two Sea Miles Off the Mole Head Seen First at Ten Past Six and Told to Nobody Until Eight, Bread and Salt Beef at One Thousand Six Hundred and a Day Apiece in Advance to the Same Four Men at Six Hundred and Seventy-Two, a Paper With a Seal on It and No Figure on It Nailed to the Mole-Head Board at About a Quarter Past One and Not Opened and Not Copied, Two Accounts That Do Not Agree and Both Standing, the Shortfall at Twenty-Four Thousand One Hundred and Eighty-Two*

**A man of about fifty who owns a boat of about twenty-two tons is on the third lay at about ten past six on the Friday morning with his painter half in and a coil of light line over his forearm, and he sees it, and he stands there with his hand on a ring for three quarters of an hour and does not call out, and he says at about eight that the water was making at ten past six and that the woman with the end stall and the slate was on her own step at half past seven and there was nothing on it while she was on that step. So it came in the night and he did not see it come in and he says so.** Nine hulls, two of them with a gunwale a plank could be landed on and seven not, lying the same way, not swinging at the half past the ebb, about two sea miles off that mole head. **TWO PEOPLE GIVE TWO ACCOUNTS OF WHAT IT IS THAT DO NOT AGREE AND BOTH ARE STILL STANDING ON THE TWELFTH AND NEITHER WAS ASKED AGAIN: the woman with the end stall says in about one sentence, in the way she says a price, *that is what it looks like when two boats of a supply do not come in*; a man of about thirty-three who hires hands at that market says, and is not laughing, that a shortage arrives at your own gate by itself and does not need a mark, and that somebody has drawn a mark at about two sea miles and put boats on it.** **Bread and salt beef for nine men for ten days at one thousand six hundred pence, being ten marks, and a day apiece in advance to the same four men at six hundred and seventy-two pence, being four marks, two shillings and eightpence, go on the sheet at about ten in the morning, and the man who keeps the leaf says the whole of both out loud before he writes a figure, and nothing goes in and nobody is asked for anything. HE THEN SAYS THE ONE THING HE SAYS ON THAT DAY, TO THE FOUR MEN AND NOT TO FISH STREET: that the figure in chalk has not moved and is not going to move that week whatever is standing off that mole, and that a man who loses a day's work because of a thing he did not decide is still owed the hour he worked. One of them asks whether the figure will be the same on Monday and he says it will be the same on Monday and he is not going to say what it will be in a week.** **AT ABOUT A QUARTER PAST ONE A BOAT'S BOAT COMES UP INSIDE THAT MOLE AND A MAN GETS OUT WITH A BAG AND A MAUL AND NAILS A SHEET TO THE BOARD AT THE HEAD OF THAT MOLE AND SAYS NOTHING WHILE HE DOES IT.** It is about two feet by a foot and a half, a seal at the foot of it and no figure on it anywhere, a date and a place at the head, about seven things in the second line and about nine lines of rule under that. **It was not opened, it is not copied, there is no line of it on any sheet in that yard, there is no key to it in that harbor, and the light over that board is out and its lens has been out since the seventh of May, so about eleven people stood in front of it in the dark and about eleven of them could not read it.** The man who keeps the leaf reads it standing up about four times and does not take it off the board, and says two things out loud, and neither of them is about what it means. Nobody is thanked. The sheet is **twenty-four thousand one hundred and eighty-two pence short**.

### Chapter 502 — *Saturday the Fourth, the Last Supply Boat of That Kind Inside the Line, the Same Victual a Second Time at a Figure Up by a Fifth at Three Hundred and Twenty as a Line of Its Own, Coal at Two Thousand Six Hundred and Eighty-Eight, and a List of What May Not Come In Read Out Twice by Iven Sallow of About Forty-Four With Three Questions Answered in the Words That List Uses*

**A supply boat of about two hundred tons comes up past the end of the line of nine boats at about twenty to ten in the morning with a red lead down her port side and the two boats that should have been with her not with her and not seen since the first of December. Iven Sallow, of about forty-four, a close-sea officer, stands in a dinghy off that mole head with two men and a warrant in an oilskin case and waves her in with his own arm, and says to the man in the dinghy and not to the quay that she is the last one of that kind that comes in here and that he has three of them coming and not the water to bring them, and the man in the dinghy is not writing it down and nobody wrote it down.** The same victual, the same nine men and the same ten days, bought a second time at a figure up by a fifth, goes on as a line of its own at three hundred and twenty pence, being two marks, **and the man who keeps the leaf refuses out loud to carry the increase inside another line and gives his reason: a figure a stranger can take off a page is worth more than a figure that is correct and buried in another one, and in a month somebody is going to ask that yard what it paid for bread and salt beef in the first ten days of December and he is not going to be the man who cannot point at it.** Ten days of coal off her at two thousand six hundred and eighty-eight pence, being sixteen marks, ten shillings and eightpence, and he has not moved the price of coal in that yard in two years and the reason it is what it is is on the quay and not in the shed. **At about two o'clock the room over that fish market is let out and about twenty people go up and about eleven cannot read and the officer reads the list of what may not come in, standing up, with the sheet in his left hand and no table under it: a date and a place at the head, a seal and no figure on it, about seven things set down, no person's name anywhere on it, and four names of officers in the margin, and he is one of the four.** Three questions are asked and answered in the words the list uses: is my name on it; how do we know what any of it means by coming in; will that boat come in again. **HE READS IT A SECOND TIME AT ABOUT HALF PAST TWO, IN THE SAME WORDS AND AT THE SAME SPEED, TURNS THE SHEET ROUND AND HOLDS IT UP, AND WRITES HIS OWN NAME AND THE HOUR OF EACH OF THE TWO READINGS AT THE FOOT OF IT IN HIS OWN HAND. NOBODY STOPS HIM AT ANY WORD IN EITHER, AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE SAYS OUT LOUD THAT SHE GOT THE SAME TWENTY WORDS BOTH TIMES AND COULD NOT HAVE SAID WHICH WAS WHICH.** Nobody is thanked and no figure is set against him. The sheet is **twenty-seven thousand one hundred and ninety pence short** and the man who keeps the leaf names the day's movement as three thousand and eight pence. **A man of about twenty-nine got the use of the left side of his head back on that Saturday, nobody set a figure against it, nobody made it into a thing he is better at, he said nothing about it and nobody asked.**

### Chapter 503 — *Sunday the Fifth, a Wipe, the Eighty-Third Time, Four People Walking Past It and Nobody Putting a Bucket Under, the Berth Fund's Reason Entered in the Second Column in New Words, a Page Read Out Twice in a Room over That Market for the First Time Since the Twenty-Eighth of November, Nobody Stopping Him in Either Reading*

**The wall behind a reeve's bench comes down bare at about half past ten for the eighty-third time and goes up whole at the angle it has been at since the twelfth, and four people walk past it between then and the middle of the day and not one of them puts a bucket under it, and the man who keeps the leaf is in that shed with the door shut and says to the slate that he has written it in the same words eighty-three times and is not going to vary it now because a line of boats has come outside that mole and made the eighty-third into something that sounds like a reason.** One hundred and sixty-eight pence comes in at about ten and the same figure goes out at about four on a Sunday, and he says the reason out loud once in the yard's own mouth: **a berth fund pays a day for a day, and it does not care what is standing outside that mole, and it was not written by anybody in that room and does not know about a line of boats, and if it did it would pay the same.** One of the four says at the door that he had not asked, and he says that is why he said it. **At about two the room over that market is let out with a bowl on the step and about twenty go up in the half hour and about eleven cannot read, and it is the first time a page has been read out in that room since the twenty-eighth of November. The page is the account of the fourth, with the rule on its face that the reader's name goes under what he reads, the hour under his name, and anybody in the room may stop him at any word.** Hobb Lee, of about forty-six, who mends nets on the third lay, reads it out at two and at twenty-five past two, does not raise his voice for the second and does not go slower, and nobody stopped him in either. **At about half past three a woman of about thirty-one of no office asks whether the room is going to say that on Sundays now, and he says no, because the room is let out to anybody who comes up the stairs and the bowl is put on the step by a man with a key and a pail, and a thing being read out in here twice a day would want about nine of them to agree to it and he is not going to count anybody in a doorway.** She put nothing in, was not asked and is not on that sheet. The sheet is **twenty-seven thousand one hundred and ninety pence short** and has not moved since the Saturday.

### Chapter 504 — *Monday the Sixth, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Fifth Charge, a Second Pair of Hands at Three Hundred and Thirty-Six on the Sheet and Not in the Total, the First Half of the Rule About the Day a Line Carries and the Day It Goes Into the Total Said Out Loud for the First Time in Four Years, a Man of About Fifty-Eight Asked in Front of Nine People What a Man Is Owed When the Boats Cannot Go Out and Given the Same Answer and One More Sentence Written on the Face of the Sheet and Not in a Column*

**The cistern is charged for the hundred and fifth time at about eight by two men who did not stop walking, the hose in that harbor being dead until the spring and the water carried into it in eleven trips from the butt behind that market, and the name at the head of that rota board is still off it. The figure of that hundred was said out loud once on the eighteenth of November and is not said out loud a second time, and the man who keeps the leaf says he is not going to improve on it because a man came up on Saturday with a list in his hand and read it out in a room four hundred yards from that shed.** A second pair of hands for two days goes on the sheet at about twenty past nine at three hundred and thirty-six pence, being two marks, one shilling and fourpence, with the sixth against it, **and the total at the foot of the sheet does not move, and he says why, which is a thing he has never had to say in four years: a line goes onto that sheet with the day the work was done against it and the day it goes into the total at the foot of it is another day and not always the same one and both of them are on the face of the line, and those two men have not worked a day yet, and a stranger with a leaf and a pencil can take the day off the line and the day it goes into the total off the line and they are two different days and that is not a trick.** **At about half past eleven, in front of nine people, a man of about fifty-eight of the second lay with a boat of about nine tons and two men asks out loud what a man is owed when the boats cannot go out at all, and he is given the same answer in the same words he gave four men on Friday morning — that the figure in chalk has not moved and will not move this week whatever is standing off that mole, and that a man who is not on the water is not a man who has not been worked — and then one more sentence: if he is not asked for by name tomorrow he is not worked tomorrow, and that is a thing that harbor does and not this yard.** The whole of that answer, both sentences and the third, is written out in the yard's own hand on the face of the sheet with the hour against it, **not in the first column and not in the second**, and he reads it standing up with his thumb under the last sentence and reads that one twice and does not argue with it, and says it is the first time anybody in that harbor has written down a thing he can come back and look at, and that he is not thanking anybody and is not going to say anyone is right about tomorrow, and that he will send his two men down at seven and ask for them by name. Nobody is thanked. The sheet is **twenty-seven thousand one hundred and ninety pence short, unmoved since Saturday morning, with a line on it that is not in the total, and both of those facts are true and both of them are on the sheet.**

### Chapter 505 — *Tuesday the Seventh, the Fifty-Ninth Wage Tuesday, a Clerk Carries the Chest Out on a Step at Ten in Front of About Forty People and It Does Not Move and Nobody Is Paid a Penny Out of It, Three Days of Air at Five Hundred and Forty With the Fifth Against It and Every Descent From That Day on That Line and on Nothing Else*

**A clerk of the harbor authority carries the chest out onto a step at the back of that market at ten in the morning in front of about forty people and reads the column aloud: twenty-six lines, one hundred and four marks, twenty envelopes, and he is reading it and not paying anybody and it has not moved once since the twelfth of October. About twenty of the forty cannot read the column on the lid. When a woman asks where it is, he says the column is on a sheet in an office on the west basin and he has brought the chest and not the sheet, and that anybody can count the envelopes and nobody can check the sheet without a permit, and he has not got a permit and is not going to ask for one that morning.** At ten minutes past ten he reads the form the authority has used since the twelfth of October: **a wage Tuesday is the day a harbor finds out what it owes, fifty-eight weeks stood fallen due at the close of the last day of November, a further week stands fallen due at the close of this day and that is fifty-nine, and the finding out is not a payment and nobody should go home and tell anybody it was one.** The further week is a further week on the sheet and not in the chest, and there have been twenty envelopes in that chest since the twelfth of October. **At about ten past eleven the man who keeps the leaf puts one line on: three days of air hired off that same supply boat at five hundred and forty pence, being three marks and five shillings, with the fifth of December against it, being the day he agreed it and could not pay for it, and he says the whole of it out loud and then says the rest of it once, and nobody writes it down: every descent from that day is on that line and on nothing else, and if a man wants to go down on that air he goes down on that line or he does not go down, and there is no other air in this harbor the yard can open a line for this week.** The sheet is **twenty-seven thousand seven hundred and thirty pence short** and moved by five hundred and forty and nothing has gone into it in four days.

### Chapter 506 — *Wednesday the Eighth, a Buoy and a Bell and a Line Built in That Yard Between Seven and One for Six Hundred and Forty, the Bellwright Not Asked and His Chest Shut, One Descent in About Four Fathoms at Ten Past Two With a Slate and a Tender and a Cutoff, Out at Thirty-Five Minutes Past Two, and the Thing Said Once About What a Buoy Is*

**The yard builds a float of tarred fir about five feet across with a ring of old chain round its waist and a leaded stem, a cast bell about nine inches across the mouth under a board on four sticks of sawn fir, and about forty fathoms of two-inch stuff with a shackle and a sinker. It is not the bellwright's bell, that yard was not asked for a figure and did not give one, his chest is shut, and the eight marks and a day of a boat that stand against him are unargued. Nessa Pike puts water in it and not oil, because oil is a thing a bell can be got to do once and water is a thing a bell does to anything that is wet, and this harbor has had no barrel of oil in it since the twenty-ninth of August and is not going to be given one by anything standing outside that mole.** At about one the man who keeps the leaf says the whole line out loud before the figure and would not put his own hours on a thing he cannot pay himself out of this month. **AT ABOUT TEN PAST TWO ON THAT EBB, IN ABOUT FOUR FATHOMS OFF THE HEAD OF THAT THIRD LAY, ON THE AIR LINE OF THE FIFTH OF DECEMBER AND ON NO OTHER AIR: Calder Marr goes down with a slate written before anybody was off the boat carrying the reason in his own words and a figure of twenty-five minutes and a cutoff if he says nothing for two minutes; Ivo Sark of about twenty-four is the tender in a dinghy about nine feet off that slip and not in the water, the pump hand of about forty-four is on the compressor, and there is a second line on the surface that had nothing to do with the buoy. He is about six minutes in the water before he is on the bottom and about nineteen of his twenty-five on it. AT ABOUT HALF PAST TWO THE TENDER SAYS OUT LOVER THE WIRE THAT HE HAS SAID NOTHING FOR TWO MINUTES AND THE CUTOFF IS PULLED WITHOUT ANYBODY ASKING, the word comes about four seconds after it is called for and is not asked for twice, and he is out of that water at about thirty-five minutes past two, being twenty-five minutes and five seconds from the rail to the rail. Nobody went in twice on that day, no two men were in it at once, nobody went in at the top of a flood, and nobody was thanked.** The second pair of hands' two days go into the total that evening. At about half past five he says the shortfall — **twenty-eight thousand and sixty-six pence short** — and then he says the one thing he says that week about what a buoy is, once, in front of about nine people, and none of them repeat it: **a buoy is a thing that is in the wrong place until somebody stands on that quay and says it is in the right one, and that is a thing nine people can do, and that is also a thing nine people can stop doing.** The boy who carried the float down the slip is not on the water and his surname is on no page of that harbor.

### Chapter 507 — *Thursday the Ninth, a Rota Day, the Hundred and Sixth Charge Walked on by None of It, a Close-Sea Officer of About Forty-Four Asks a Man of About Fifty for a Date in a Room in the Harbor Authority's Office on the West Basin and Does Not Get One, Four Sentences in About Forty Seconds With a Condition in the Middle of Them, the Whole Room Into the Second Column at Half Past Four, Nobody Thanking Him and No Figure Being Set Against Him*

**The cistern is charged for the hundred and sixth time and is walked on by none of it. At about two o'clock in a room in the harbor authority's office on the west basin, with a table and a stove and a window over the basin and a clerk who comes in at a quarter past and goes out again, Iven Sallow opens his docket book and writes in it before he asks, and says he has four boats in that line and is required to have a date from every owner of a boat of over fifteen tons inside that harbor, and that he is not asking him to agree to anything and there is nothing in that room that can make him agree to anything.** The man of about fifty looks at the book and then at the window, and says four sentences in about forty seconds, in his own mouth, and says no fifth thing, and it is not a threat and it is not a speech: **he has got a boat of about twenty-two tons and there is a line of nine boats outside his mole and he is not going to give a day, because a day given away is a day somebody can come back and ask him for and say that he promised; he has not said no and is not going to say no, because a no is a thing that goes in a book and a thing in a book is a thing that can be used twice; and if you want a day out of him you are going to have to come out to that slip and stand on it with him and not send anybody.** **The officer does not argue, does not thank him, and does not write the word *refused* because the man did not use it; he writes *declined to give a date* and the hour, and the four reasons go in the book because the book is where reasons go, and he turns the book round and pushes it nine inches across the table, and the man of about fifty reads his own words and does not ask for a word of it to be changed. THE OFFICER SAYS OUT LOUD THAT IT WILL BE HELD, THAT IT IS A REGISTER COPY, THAT NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR WILL EVER BE SHOWN IT, AND THAT IN ABOUT A MONTH A MAN A LONG WAY OFF WILL HAVE A COPY AND HIS SLIP WILL BE ON A LIST WITH ABOUT ELEVEN OTHER SLIPS, AND THAT HE CANNOT STOP THAT AND HAS NO POWER TO STOP IT AND IS NOT GOING TO PRETEND OTHERWISE.** Nobody thanked him and no figure was set against him anywhere. **At about half past four at the head of that third lay the man of about fifty tells the whole of it to the man who keeps the leaf, the man who keeps the leaf asks him nothing about any part of it, and the whole of that room goes into the second column with the hour against it, the four sentences as they came out of him, the condition, both hours, and no name against any of it but the man's own.** The sheet is **twenty-eight thousand and sixty-six pence short** and unmoved since the Wednesday morning.

### Chapter 508 — *Friday the Tenth, About Eleven Local Crews Asked One at a Time Off Eleven Sentences Written Before Anybody Was Asked and Read Out Eleven Times, Seven Names and Four Not and No Reason Given and No List Kept and Nobody Asked Again, the Woman of Thirty of No Office Refused in Two Sentences, a Day Apiece in Advance at Six Hundred and Seventy-Two With the Ninth Against It and Not in the Total Until the Morrow*

**A page goes round that room with eleven sentences at the head of it, written before anybody was asked anything, and Hobb Lee reads them out word for word eleven times, one time for each crew, with a hand laid flat on the page between times, and about eleven people in the room hear all eleven and the eleventh is word for word the first.** The sentences set down that it is a line of local crews and not a company and has no head; that a crew that puts a name agrees to go out to the mark off that third lay once a month and answer for it by going out, looking at it and writing down what is wrong with it, and not in weather and not at night and not when the officer outside that mole says not to; that nobody in that room is paid by the page or for the day he loses coming up the stairs; that a crew may take the name off in front of anybody and needs to give no reason, and **that a crew that does not put a name is not asked again this month or any month after it**; that the name is the crew's and not the owner's; **that the page is not a list of anybody who has refused and no such list exists in that harbor**; that nobody's name goes on the four heads and that this page does not go on that wall; and that what goes into the book afterward is what the reader says out loud. **Seven names go on and four do not. None of the four gives a reason, none is asked for one, their names are on no page in that harbor, they are not counted with anybody, and nobody in that room and nobody in that yard has asked any of them anything since and is not going to.** At about half past two a man at the front says *so that is four of them against it*, and Hobb Lee refuses it in about two sentences — four men not writing a name is the whole of what happened, and writing *against* about four people makes a list, and the ninth sentence says there is not going to be one — and offers him the alternative of saying it about himself, and nobody takes him up on it. **At about ten past three the woman of thirty of no office asks to have the four refusals read into the record of that room, and he refuses in about two sentences and says the decision is his and he will say so every time, and she says that is a decision and he has not said whose it is, and he says it is his because he is the one with the book, and nobody wrote the four anywhere and there is not going to be any such list.** **At about eleven in the morning a day apiece in advance to the same four men goes on at six hundred and seventy-two pence, being four marks, two shillings and eightpence, with the ninth of December against it, being the day they worked, and it goes into the total on the day he writes it, which is the morrow, and nobody asked why those four men are the same four men as on the third.** The page goes home with the man who mends nets and is on no wall. The sheet is **twenty-eight thousand and sixty-six pence short**, unmoved since Wednesday morning.

### Chapter 509 — *Saturday the Eleventh, a Harvest Week and a Room That Is Not Let Out, a Working Man Puts Out Loud That a List of the People Who Put Nothing In Would Make the Line Easier to Run, a Ropemaker of About Sixty-One Refuses It in Four Words and Then Says Once That a Roster of Boats Is a List of Work and a Roll of People Is Not, the Buoy and the Day Apiece Both Going Into the Total at About Half Past Eleven and the Whole of the Rule Said Out Loud in One Piece for the First Time*

**The room over that market is let out Monday to Friday and is not let out on this Saturday, and this is a harvest week, and about a dozen people were in it anyway at about half past two and the man with the key and the pail was not there and had not been asked to be there.** A fair copy of a schedule of which boats may go out of that harbor and on which hour and on which tide came ashore on the Thursday with a seal at the head and no figure on it and no person's name anywhere on it, and the man who hires hands has the boat column of it in his coat and has read it out twice in that market. **At about half past two he puts the other thing out loud to everybody in the room and not to one person: a man he did not know and who would not give his name came to him on the Wednesday and asked him for a list of the people in that harbor who have put nothing into that sheet, said it was worth something, said a name that is on no paper can be come back to twice while a name on a paper can only be read, and said it would make the line outside that mole easier to run.** A ropemaker of about sixty-one, who is not in a room of her own on a Saturday and has not had one for eleven years, and who is not a member of anything and is not on a list of anything and whose name is on that sheet on no line, says four words from about nine feet back: **nobody is keeping that.** And then she says the rest of it once: **a schedule is a list of work — it says which boat, on which hour, on which tide, it does not say who does it, it is about seventy boats, it has no person's name on it and it could have been handed over in a morning by a man who owes nothing to anybody here — and a roll of people who put nothing in is a list of what a person has not got money for, which no office in the world can be given, because it has to be written by somebody here out of what he knows about his neighbours, and the only people who could write it are the people who did not put in, and they are the last people in this harbor going to write it.** She says she has said it in that room before and that the last time a man said *then somebody will be asked twice*, and yes, and she would rather somebody was asked twice by one man with a bad memory than that the whole harbor had a book about what it has not got. **Nobody wrote it down and nobody thanked her.** **At about ten past three at the head of that slip the man who keeps the leaf says the rule out loud for the in one piece for the first time, because the half of it was said on the sixth and the rest of it on the eighth and on both of those days the man who keeps the leaf was the one talking and nobody was asking: the buoy, the bell and the line at six hundred and forty with the seventh against it, being the day the two men started on it, and the day apiece in advance to the same four men at six hundred and seventy-two with the ninth against it, being the day they worked and not the day he paid them, and both are in the total since about half past eleven that morning, and **a line goes onto that sheet with the day the work was done against it and is not in the total at the foot of that sheet until the day this yard settles it, and both of those days are on the face of the line.**** At about half past five the sheet is **twenty-nine thousand three hundred and seventy-eight pence short**, having moved by one thousand three hundred and twelve at about half past eleven and not since, and nothing has gone into that sheet since the sixteenth day of October. Tobias Wren was on the crown of that mole from ten until four with eleven pieces of a boat behind him and nobody sent for him.

### Chapter 510 — *Sunday the Twelfth, a Wipe, the Eighty-Fourth Time, and at About Ten Past Five in the Evening in the Open the Leaf Read Back Twice With Its Own Arithmetic on Its Own Face at Two Hundred and Forty-Two and One Thousand and Eighty-Seven and at Two Hundred and Forty-Three and One Thousand and Eighty-Nine, the Money Read Back After That in Full, the Whole of What a Close-Sea Line Changes Said Out Loud Once, and at Twenty to Six One Thing Said in Nobody's Mouth But the Man Who Keeps the Leaf's*

**The wall comes down bare for the eighty-fourth time at about half past ten and five people walk past it and not one of them puts a bucket under it, and it goes up whole at the angle it has been at since the twelfth. THE LEAF IS READ BACK AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING IN THE OPEN AT THE HEAD OF THAT THIRD LAY, IN THE YARD'S OWN MOUTH, ALL FOUR COLUMNS INCLUDING THE EMPTY ONE, READ TWICE BECAUSE ABOUT FOUR MEN OF THAT PARTY CANNOT READ, both definitions in the same words and the same order as on the twenty-second of October and the first, eleventh and twenty-second of November and the second of December, and the reading prints its own arithmetic on its own face: **ten have gone in on the ten days from Friday the third of December to this day, one against each of them, and not one day in two of them has not got an entry against it, which is the first time in fifty-one days that those two things have been the same**; and **five have gone in on each of those same ten days, three before the hour of that day's reading and two after, so that of the fifty that have gone in, forty-five went in on the nine days before this one and three this morning, and fifty less two is forty-eight, and one thousand and thirty-nine and forty-eight is one thousand and eighty-seven.** The third column is empty and unappointed with a boy's hand at the head of it, that boy's surname is on no page of that harbor, and he is not on the water. **The fourth stands at one hundred and twenty-five and has taken no line in these ten days or the ten before them, has no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it, and is neither closed nor struck.** **THE SHEET THAT CARRIES THE MONEY IS READ BACK AFTER THAT IN FULL WITH THE DAY AGAINST EVERY LINE, CARRYING NO COUNT OF PERSONS, WITH THE THREE WHO SAID NO AT THE SIZE OF THE FIGURES, AND ON ITS FACE: ten thousand six hundred and forty in, forty thousand and eighteen out, twenty-nine thousand three hundred and seventy-eight short, being one hundred and eighty-three marks, eight shillings and twopence, and eight lines out on eight days being 1,600 and 672 on the third, 320 and 2,688 on the fourth, 540 on the fifth, 336 on the sixth, 640 on the seventh and 672 on the ninth, being seven thousand four hundred and sixty-eight pence, forty-six marks and nine shillings, and on four of the eight the day the work was done and the day it was written are not the same day.** One of the four men asked him to say the second number again and he said it again. **AND AT ABOUT TWENTY TO SIX IN THE EVENING, IN THE OPEN, IN THE YARD'S OWN MOUTH, HE SAYS ONE THING, ONCE: a route held by nine people is a route that stops when one of the nine stops.** And then the working of it: seven names are on that page in the room over the market and nine of them on this slip answer for that mark, two of them being the man of about thirty-four of the second lay and the man of about fifty who owns the boat of about twenty-two tons; the four that did not write a name are not in the nine and are not counted with anybody; a day's work comes in at one hundred and sixty-eight pence whatever is on the water, a day asked for by name is paid whether anybody is on the water or not, and a man can be asked for a date by somebody with an order and can decline and is not thanked and is not given a face — three things, all three said out loud in that yard in the last ten days — and **if the fourth is a man who stops going out, the mark goes over to the weather in a fortnight and the weather is not going to answer for it.** Nobody answered it. **IT WENT INTO THE SECOND COLUMN WITH THE HOUR AGAINST IT AND INTO NOBODY'S MOUTH BUT THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE LEAF'S, AND IT IS NOT SOLVED AND NOBODY HAS SOLVED IT AND NOBODY IS GOING TO SOLVE IT THIS MONTH.**
