### The chapter summaries

- **351 — Monday the fifth of July, the twenty-first day of the ninety.** The sixty-first wipe and the sixty-first charge walked on. **A man of about fifty puts a second paper on the table in the office off the west basin at a quarter past nine with the fourth box not filled; the man already at that table is a man off the west quay and is not this man; neither spoke; the clerk of about sixty wrote both names in one register; a paper on a table is a paper on a table.** Garron Fisk, about thirty-four, of a pressure house at Ternwatch, of no office, not a courier, not a servant, not a face of anything, comes ashore off a lighter at ten with a sealed instrument in a wet leather pocket; it goes on the bench with a bulkhead brace against it; Nessa Pike reads it out in about four minutes. Two seals, one signature, *Magister Ilya Serr, senior Registry examiner*, and *Admiral Soren Vey, fifty-two, of the closed-sea squadron* printed small at the foot, on the face of that one instrument and no other paper in that harbor. **The four prices: five leaves, the sheet itself, the four copies, a leaf with one correction and one date — eleven leaves in six hands — and a last paragraph wanting a name under a sentence.** Calder writes the four prices on the back of the leaf in his own hand and puts them in front of the woman of no office, who does not say no and says that a leaf is a thing and a person is a person and that if a person cannot read that is not the same as a person who has said yes. Fisk says one sentence at the top of the steps about the weight of a paper in a pocket and is not thanked. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **352 — Tuesday the sixth of July, the twenty-second day of the ninety.** The thirty-seventh week and a wage not paid; thirty-seven weeks fallen due. **A stall two in from the end, a woman of about sixty-one, a paper in a box eleven days old and unopened, four sentences read to her in about eleven people's hearing, and then nothing else** — because nobody in that yard is to tell any of them anything, and the rule is the yard's own, made in May after a boy of seventeen carried a word up a hill in front of a woman. She says it is in her box and she is not taking it to anybody to be got rid of. The sixth of the eleven is a man of about forty-four on a hard whose refusal is the first line on the sheet of forty lines; he comes and says he has only got the one no. A chandler of about fifty asks a second time to have it recorded that he has nothing to say about it; it is recorded once; the yard will not ask him a third time. **The sentence on the face of the day: an instrument that wants eleven people to sign one sentence cannot be answered honestly by anybody in that harbor, because one of the eleven cannot read it and nobody is permitted to read it to her, and a signature obtained from a person who does not know what she is signing is worse than no signature because it can be printed.** The man of about thirty, two days down that coast, was not sent for. The woman of no office heard all of it and did not hear it from him and said two things about him, neither of them kind, and both of them true. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **353 — Wednesday the seventh of July, the twenty-third day of the ninety.** The instrument read in full; the four prices priced in hours and material before anybody was asked anything; the last paragraph priced at eleven conversations, about forty days and one of them that cannot happen at all, with no figure of money against it. The woman of no office says the last paragraph is the only part anybody will remember in a year and that its being the last line is what makes it an offer and not a demand. **One day's work at the north berth, the ground chain up with nineteen feet and a shackle that was cut and not parted, one mark and eightpence in and seven shillings and eightpence of new stud chain out.** A man of about twenty-six with a hod of lime asks whether he is the eleventh, is told he is not, and says he had meant to read the notice to the people who cannot read and had not; the woman of no office tells him at the door that a man who can read is not a public letter office. Nothing else comes in or goes out.
- **354 — Thursday the eighth of July, the twenty-fourth day of the ninety.** The sixty-second charge, walked on. **A man of about fifty-one of the six puts their six names, the nineteenth of June, twenty minutes to six, off the south end, and a boat, and no figure, on the back of a reeve's office docket on the dry stone of that mole's crown, in his own hand, in about half an hour, with two spellings nobody corrected, no copy kept, and a line at the bottom saying it is his paper and the mole is the harbor's.** Calder goes up, stands in front of it two minutes, does not put a hand on it, is not asked for it, and says one sentence to nobody: it is on the harbor's stone and not on his wall and he is not going to move it. **A boy of about seventeen carries a word ashore off a coal boat, unsigned, off no office's table, about a steamer and a second vessel at Ternwatch and a building with a door that has no glass in it**, and nobody asks him where he got it. At ten past four the man of sixty-one on the crown says twenty-six words about a paper on a boat of his at Veyr twenty-six years ago, and is asked nothing and improves on nothing. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **355 — Friday the ninth of July, the twenty-fifth day of the ninety.** **A fish market at the end of the end stall, in about forty people's hearing, four sentences said once.** Nine refusals in nine persons' own words in five towns and one market. **The woman of about fifty-eight holds no copy: she holds a slate, a board and a wall with the notice on it and this yard's own fourth return under one sheet, and her refusal is that a leaf this yard cannot get at has already been read by a person this yard has never met and put up where strangers can stand in front of it, and she has no figure for it and will not put one on her board.** A copyist of about fifty-nine, one hand, one copy, off the wall and not out of the room. A herring skipper of fifty-one. A man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons, whose no went on the slate. The ship's hand, in her own left hand. **A boat's man of about forty-one of the second lay, in about nine people's hearing, after four questions and ten minutes: he has a boat and a wage of four marks, he is on none of the eleven, he cannot read the leaf, and he will not put his name under a sentence he has not seen — entered as what it was, neither a refusal nor a yes.** The man of about thirty-six a day up that coast had not answered and his line was empty and was not a hole. In a town four days up that coast nobody answered at all, and this yard wrote to none of the five towns. **The owners of the eleven leaves are about six people in five towns, and the instrument does not say how many subscribing parties it means, and that is the eleventh thing about that leaf that is not on the leaf. Three elevens stand in that harbor in one week and are three different numbers.** Nobody proposed a body. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **356 — Saturday the tenth of July, the twenty-sixth day of the ninety. THE TURN.** **A sheet of thirteen lines, the back of a docket, the woman of no office's hand, about an hour and a half, with the same three rules at the head of it as the sheet of forty lines and, under the third rule and above the first line, a fourth thing which is not a rule: the price against a line is what the man said he was paying, the payer against a line is the man himself, and where nobody was asked there is a place and no price and no payer and the place is the price of not asking. A name and an hour on all thirteen, a price and a payer on eleven with the price on all eleven being the word *nothing*, and two lines carrying a place and neither — the market wall four days up that coast, and a table in a corridor of the Morrow circuit office where two of the three things are and one of the two cannot read and who was not asked and no request was made.** Line one is his own answer in four sentences, and the last of them is that a thing needing eleven men has ten and a hole. **It goes up that coast in the coal of an ordinary boat at about two in the afternoon, in the inside pocket of that boat's own boy of about seventeen, who was not paid and did not know what it was; this yard wrote to none of the five towns and charged nobody for any part of it.** At half past two a small steam tender of about ninety tons lies at the outer water with two lines out, a young man of about twenty-three in her own wheelhouse with a telescope on the roof twice, and a lever of nineteen patient with a bight of line and not cutting it. She came no closer. No officer, no paper, no hail. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **357 — Sunday the eleventh of July, the twenty-seventh day of the ninety.** The eleven leaves read one at a time at four in the afternoon, with a boy of twenty-two copying headings and numbers and hours and no prose, and the third column empty with his hand at the head of it since the fourth of April. **The five leaves in the woman's hand, in her own order, and then the sixth thing that is not a leaf: two months, not in her working hours, nobody has ever paid her for a day of it, and a line in that yard's second column for the first of July with a reason and no name — AND SHE KNOWS WHAT THAT LINE IS AND SAID SO OUT LOUD AND WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION AND NO NAME WENT ON IT AND NONE IS TO BE PUT THERE BY HER OR BY ANYBODY IN THAT YARD.** The sheet not taken out and not read a third time. The six hands and the five places. The corridor: a woman of about seventy and a man of about forty, mother and son, a municipal claim on one of the three things, the man cannot read, not asked, nobody sent, no request made. **And at half past five in the evening he said the wrong thing out loud — if it came to it he would hand the five over — and she told him that five of the eleven are her hand and that a hand is not a thing and cannot be handed over by a man standing near the box it is in, and that he has not asked her one question in four days and that she has been sitting on that bench since the first of May waiting to be asked, and he said he had not asked her because he had thought there was nothing she could be asked that was any use, and she said that was the answer to the question she had not asked and that she would not have been thanked for it. HE DID NOT ASK HER.** A fire party's hose dead since before the spring, tried and dead. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **358 — Monday the twelfth of July, the twenty-eighth day of the ninety.** The sixty-second wipe, put up at an angle it has not been at since March and not put back; the sixty-third charge, walked on. **A mooring buoy adrift since the spring, the second of two items on the harbor authority's list, up off the foul. A man of about thirty-four of the second lay, who keeps the whole fouling ladder in his own book and is not Fisk, asked to be in the boat, was not asked, and came ashore with a borrowed pinger: a pinger puts down two channels and is not reading anything, and there are three, and the third is not fouling, and fouling grows the way the water goes round a thing and this goes the other way — NOT MEASURED, NOT TIMED, NOT GONE BACK TO, AND THE INSTRUMENT WENT BACK UP THAT COAST ON THE TUESDAY IN THE ORDINARY WAY AND THE MAN IT IS BORROWED FROM HAS NOT BEEN ASKED ABOUT IT.** A man of about fifty-one of the six took the whole of the day's wage, one mark and eightpence out of a tin, counted it on a bollard, did not say thank you and was not thanked. **The second of the six, a man of about forty-four, was in that boat on his own account, was not paid, was not asked to pay, and was told the terms before he went out and said he knew them; the other four were not in the boat and were not asked and were not told there was work.** Forty pence out on a shackle and a fathom of line. **THE BAG IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHT PENCE; THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE IS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS AND NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHT PENCE.** A man of about twenty-six read the notice out to his wife in a kitchen on the Sunday and she asked him what a *breach* was and he said he did not know. Nothing in, nothing out.
- **359 — Tuesday the thirteenth of July, the twenty-ninth day of the ninety.** The thirty-eighth week and a wage not paid; thirty-eight weeks fallen due. **The man of about forty-four, the second of the six, worked the Monday for nothing, was told the terms and said he knew them, and at half past two in the afternoon an adrift buoy's shackle took the top of two fingers off his left hand; he was not in the water and did not go in. There is no bonesetter on that coast on a Monday afternoon, so a shipwright of about sixty set it at about four with a strip off a leech and a needle in about forty minutes, and a bonesetter of about fifty came on the Saturday, said it was not a bonesetter's work, had not done it and would not touch it. The bill was five shillings and sixpence, being sixty-six pence, out of his own hand, said twice and not a third time, and no part of it came out of that yard and none out of the list of the harbor authority. He is off the water nine days. The shipwright's wife said at her door that he is one of about eleven people of that harbor who cannot read the notice, and he was not added to the count because nobody asked.** A man of about thirty-six's no came down the coast road in the coal at about six in the morning: his father wrote the spelling and not him, and a man does not give up his father's book because a piece of paper came ashore in the coal. **The empty line on the sheet of thirteen lines was filled in with his name and the hour, neither of the two blanks was touched, and the sheet was not recopied.** A man of about thirty-eight would rather a chart were read out in a market than carried in a bag for nine years; the man of about thirty-one with the chart has not changed his mind; neither of them is going to be cited in a room. **At ten past five on the third step from the bottom of that mole a man of about thirty-four of a packet out of Bramble Strait, four days down that coast and not paid, said nine words about the tender: she asks at Ternwatch whether a boat has a man in her.** Nothing in, nothing out.
- **360 — Wednesday the fourteenth of July, the thirtieth day of the ninety. THE CLOSE.** **READ-BACK at four: ninety-two, three hundred and thirty-seven, none, eighty-four; AT CLOSE: ninety-three, three hundred and thirty-nine, none, eighty-five, the eighty-fifth the last thing in that book and the column not closed. The second column is that ledger's own, three of the day's entries before the reading and two after it, a habit of that shed and not a rule and not checkable from a mole; the first's ninety-two and the fourth's eighty-four at the hour are counts of entries and of lines and are checkable by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil; both definitions are on the face of the reading.** Three counts on the face: TWO wipes, THREE charges walked on none, TWO wage Tuesdays, THIRTY-EIGHT WEEKS FALLEN DUE. MONEY: 0 + 168 + 168 − 132 = 204. Three statements about three things. **The mole head at ten past five with the light out, a tender of about ninety tons still at the outer water with a lamp at her masthead, the two objects of nobody's at three hundred and ninety-eight days and about four feet from a page of six names, the far bench empty after four with the shoe that is not his, the second seam a foot and seven inches where it was on the nineteenth of May and not looked at, the notice on its wall on the fifty-eighth day of it.** **THE THIRTIETH DAY OF THE NINETY, and the volume's new question was not asked on any of the ten days and is not asked at the mole head, and no body and no committee and no assembly and no fleet and no wing and no guard was proposed by anybody in that harbor, and the naming of them is a naming of a kind and a kind is not a thing anybody here has got.** Nothing in, nothing out.

### The repairs of 28 September 2026, five findings, all mechanical, recorded once

1. **The leaf count of the public archive was wrong in three chapters and was eleven in none of them, and Chapters 353 and 355 gave a copy of the sheet of forty lines to a woman in that harbor on a Morrow Quay market wall, which would have broken `outline/volume-07.md` lock L24 in its hard form.** Repaired: four prices, eleven leaves, six hands, five places, and no copy of that sheet on any wall in Morrow Quay. The page on a market wall four days up that coast is now a fact on Chapter 355's face, put there by somebody nobody in that yard knows out of a coal locker.
2. **The man of about thirty-six's answer was dated to the Friday of the ninth and is dated to the Monday of the thirteenth,** and the empty line on the sheet of thirteen lines is now on the sheet from the Saturday and is filled on the Monday, and neither blank is touched.
3. **The day's wage of the twelfth was given to two men in Chapters 358 and 359 as first written, which would have made three hundred and thirty-six pence in on that day.** Repaired: the man of about fifty-one takes the whole of it, and the man of about forty-four worked for nothing and was hurt. The chapters are right and the computed figure was thrown away.
4. **The notice's age was given as eighty days in Chapter 356 and is fifty-eight days at the fourteenth of July.** Repaired: Chapter 356 carries no count and the count is given once, in Chapter 360.
5. **Chapter 355 described nine refusals as given "in nine towns' and nine persons' own words."** Repaired to *in nine persons' own words in five towns and one market*, which is also the correct count of places.

### What the batch paid, in one line

**Movement 1 entire: a sealed offer naming four things and a sentence, the eleven leaves in six hands counted in the open, the four prices priced in hours and material before anybody was asked anything, nine refusals in nine persons' own words and one answer that was neither, a woman of sixty-one who cannot read and a rule that stops this yard asking her, a page of thirteen lines with a name and an hour on all thirteen and a price and a payer on eleven with the price on all eleven being the word *nothing* and two printed reasons for the two blanks, a page of six names on a harbor's own mole in a hand nobody corrected, a tender of about ninety tons at the outer water for five days with no officer and no paper and no hail, a third channel on a borrowed instrument and nothing measured, two days of paid work after two months of none and a bag that is one mark and three shillings and eightpence, two fingers off a working man's hand who worked the day for nothing and nine days off the water, a wrong sentence said out loud in a shed and the correction and the two people not asking each other a question, and the read-back of four columns with both definitions on its face — and a harbor poorer on the fourteenth of July than on the fourteenth of May, with the cheapest oil unchanged and a second of six men ashore with no boat and no proposal and no instrument.**

### The volume's shape after ten chapters of it

**Volume 08 is outlined at `outline/volume-08.md` in five movements of ten chapters and is ten chapters old. Movement 1 is paid and the movement's turn is on the page. THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION IS NOT ASKED IN MOVEMENT 1 AND MUST NOT BE ASKED AGAIN UNTIL MOVEMENT 5. THE APOLOGY IS OWED AND IS MOVEMENT 2's. THE KEELWRIGHT STAGE IS VOLUME 09's AND THE WORD IS IN NO MOUTH. NO STAGE HAS BEEN TAKEN IN VOLUME 08. Ilya Serr has appeared once, as a name and a seal and an office on a face, and has never been in a room. Soren Vey has been named once, on one instrument, and has not been in a room. The plate at the fifth seam has not been looked at and its note is carried. The condition is named nowhere and one day is already lost to it. Thirty-three thousand seven hundred and forty-nine words across ten chapters.**

## Volume 08, Batch 0002 (Chapters 361–370), Movement 2, a room in Veyr where nobody with a title is in it, and a clause that has never been tested

- **361 — Thursday the fifteenth of July, the thirty-first day of the ninety.** The cistern charged and walked on none, the sixty-fourth, the top name on the rota board still off it, and the wall up at the angle since the twelfth. **A paper of two leaves comes down that coast in the coal in the inside pocket of an ordinary boat's own boy of about seventeen, who was not paid, did not know what it was and did not ask, folded twice and not sealed, with six words on the outside in a hand nobody in that shed knew: *for the holder of that writ*.** It says an inquiry will sit in Veyr in a room off a street behind the fish market there, on terms drawn by the Crown; the terms are seven lines on the second leaf and **no line in them names anybody and no line says what anybody had done or what anybody was to answer for**; a line in the middle says a clerk will sit in a room off the room and write the hour and what was said, and that it will be read back and not given out. **The two people on that coast who can be shown the thing are the holder of that writ and a woman of no office, both are asked to come, and a boat will wait at Ternwatch for three days and would not wait longer.** He says he is going, and that a room in Veyr is a room and not anything else, and that he will not stand on a hill and refuse a room he has not seen; **he does not answer for her in a shed.** She says she will go, and not because it asks, because a thing that can be shown ought to be looked at by somebody who is not being paid by the person who wants it looked at. A man of about fifty-one of the six asks whether there was a day's work and is told there was not. The tide gang is four men short, the reeve's office has nothing on its list, and the list is a list and binds nobody. The hose at the standpipe is dead. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **362 — Friday the sixteenth of July, the thirty-second day of the ninety.** Up that coast on an ordinary boat that carries coal, because the boat that would wait at Ternwatch is a boat that waits and not a boat that is sent, and a man asked to a room does not get to send for a boat at a price he has not got. They come into Veyr from the sea at about two and nobody meets them and nobody asks their names. **The room is off a street behind the fish market, up one flight of stairs, a window onto a yard where a pump stands, a table, six chairs, a bench against the wall, and nothing on the walls but the seven lines under glass.** A man of about fifty keeps the room and not the inquiry, has no title in it and no seal in it, and sits at the end of the table and not at the head of it, with a leaf in front of him with a day and an hour on it. **Nobody else is in the room, no title is said in it, and no seal line is on any face in it at all except the two leaves in Calder's coat, which he did not take out.** A clerk of about sixty in a room off it, door open, writes the hour and the two names and asks nothing and is asked nothing, and the pen goes on after they have stopped speaking. They give their names as they are and the clerk does not ask what office she is not of. **The room pays for nothing and nobody in it is paid by anybody**, and they find a lodging behind the market at twelve pence in all, being one shilling, at six pence a night each, out of their own hands and out of nothing in that yard. At ten past five Calder walks back to the landing and there is no mole head there and no light to look at, and nothing in that street is his. At about six the woman of no office comes down and stands beside him, and neither says anything about the room. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **363 — Saturday the seventeenth of July, the thirty-third day of the ninety.** The seven lines read out in about six minutes, standing at the end of the table, not read as if they were his, not improved on, **read once and not twice, because twice is a conversation a man can join.** ONE — how a harbor on that coast uses its own papers when it sends a boat out and brings one in. TWO — it may write down what it is shown and nothing else. THREE — nobody in the room has a title and nobody will be given one in it. FOUR — the clerk writes the hour and what was said and reads it back and gives out nothing. FIVE — **a foundation survey of that harbor's own mole where it stands in eleven feet is to be ordered, and the ordering is the whole of what the room does about it, and the work has not been done.** SIX — no person in that harbor is to be paid by the person who wants the thing looked at. SEVEN — the room convicts nobody and takes nothing and closes nothing. **There is no eighth line, no schedule, no enclosure and nothing on the back, and no line in them names anybody.** On the stairs she says one sentence to the stairwell and not to him: *they have ordered it and they have not done it, and nobody in that harbor wants it done.* **The measuring is not reached, not measured, not touched, not asked about and not closed, and no person of that yard was in any water on the said day and none in any stone, and the one paper that carries it is the terms on the wall in that room.** At ten past five they walk to the landing again and say nothing about the fifth line, and a change of politics in an office is a paper and not a boat. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **364 — Sunday the eighteenth of July, the thirty-fourth day of the ninety.** **A municipal paper from the office on the west basin goes onto the table in Veyr, brought down in a coat by a man off the west quay who was given it to carry and not to read and was thanked for nothing, naming two boats and three men and a tide, with the clerk of that office at the foot of it, and a clerk's-hand copy of the notice of the seventeenth of May past beside it, all eight lines, the fifth and the sixth marked, and nobody reads either out loud.** The room-keeper says any person may put a paper in front of the room, that the question on the second one was whether it made any difference to the first, that the room will answer only what the lines said, and that the man who left that paper there was not in the room and had given no name and would not be asked for one in it. Calder: *what the sixth line says is that in is free. It does not say in what. It says in.* Mara Venn: **a civilian convoy under municipal papers is not a vessel returning from beyond the line, so the sixth line's door is open to it as well as to the others.** The clerk writes the two sentences and the hour and asks nothing. **THE ROOM WRITES THAT THE DOOR IS OPEN WHERE THE PAPERS ARE IN ORDER, THAT WHERE THERE ARE NO PAPERS THERE IS NO DOOR, THAT A PAPER ON A TABLE IS A PAPER ON A TABLE, AND THAT IT BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT USE IT. IT IS THE FIRST THING ANYBODY HAS COME OUT OF A ROOM WITH THAT IS A DOOR AND NOT A REFUSAL, A FOOT AND NOT A FLEET, NOT AN INSTRUMENT OF ANYBODY'S, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM SAID ANYBODY WAS IN THE WRONG FOR NOT USING IT.** Neither asked for anything more. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **365 — Monday the nineteenth of July, the thirty-fifth day of the ninety.** The wall came down bare for the sixty-third time and went up again at the angle since the twelfth and nobody put it back; the cistern charged and walked on none, the sixty-fifth. **In that room at ten, the woman of no office says: *then show it what a refusal costs. Not in a shed. Here. In a room with a clerk in it. Say it out loud.*** He looks at her because she had not told him she was going to say it, and because a thing asked for in a room has to be answered in that room or not at all. *I will say it tomorrow. I will not say it today without having thought about it, because a man who says what a thing costs without thinking is a man inventing a figure, and I have no figure.* **She does not argue with the day: *you have no figure. I have no figure and I will not invent one. Say what it is and not what it is worth.*** The room will hear it at ten tomorrow and the clerk writes the hour and asks nothing. In that shed the ship's hand is the only one of the yard in it, puts the wall up and enters the wipe and the charge with the figures and the hours. A man of about forty-four of the six comes past at about two, the seventh day off the water of his nine, with his hand in a sling, and is given water at the door and asks for nothing. At ten past five by that city's bell she says one sentence about tomorrow and it is not about him. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **366 — Tuesday the twentieth of July, the thirty-sixth day of the ninety.** **The thirty-ninth week and the wage of four marks, being six hundred and forty pence, not paid, the column not moved, thirty-nine weeks fallen due with no envelope against any of them.** In that room at ten he stands, because a thing said out loud in a room is said standing, and says the four things and does not improve on them. **ONE — eleven leaves in six hands stay where they are, five of them are her hand, they are not given up and they are not protected, and they can be asked for again. TWO — a sheet of thirteen lines stays with a name and an hour on all thirteen and a price and a payer on eleven and two places and no price and no payer, and no fresh copy on any of its five places because of anything said in this room. THREE — six men with no boat get nothing out of a refusal, one of them had a day's wage and one lost two fingers off his left hand and paid five shillings and sixpence, being sixty-six pence, out of his own hand for it, and the other four had nothing and were not told there was anything, and none of that is changed by saying no. FOUR — this room writes that the door is open to a convoy with papers and binds nobody who does not use it, nobody in this harbor is paid by the person who wants the thing looked at, the cheapest oil stays at four hundred and fifty pence, being thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, and the mole-head light stays out.** He sits down and nobody improves on four things said without improvement. **From the bench, to the room and not to him: *I have no figure for what a refusal costs. I am not inventing one.*** The clerk reads back the hour and the four things and her sentence and asks nothing and the pen stops. **A woman of no office is in that room and is not on the crew and is not restored and is not forgiven and her forty marks first after food are neither reduced nor paid.** **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **367 — Wednesday the twenty-first day of July, the thirty-seventh day of the ninety. THE APOLOGY, PAID.** Down that coast on the ordinary boat that carries coal, amidships where the coal dust is thinnest, the boy who minds the sheets not knowing what boat he is minding them for and the master at the tiller asking them nothing, because two people paying nothing for a passage are not owed a conversation. **At about eleven, with Ternwatch behind them, he turns on the thwart and says it to her, in his own voice, in front of her, once, and not to a market and not to a room and not to forty people:** that he is sorry he did not ask her; that on the eleventh he said out loud he would hand five leaves over and she told him five of the eleven are her hand and a hand is not a thing; that she told him he had not asked her one question in four days and had been sitting on that bench since the first of May waiting to be asked; that he said he had not asked because he had thought there was nothing she could be asked that was any use, and she said that was the answer to a question she had not asked; **that she was right, and that he owed her an apology before he owed her anything else, and that he is not asking her to forgive it and is not going to improve on it.** **He does not say he was protecting her and does not hold the hiding of another year out as an excuse, because a hiding in one year is not an excuse for not asking in another.** She looks at him a long time with the water moving under them. **She does not forgive him and she does not thank him. *I am not forgiving you. I am not thanking you. What I want instead is a procedure.*** **THE PROCEDURE: before any paper using her hand is shown in any room, he puts what the room wants it for in writing on a leaf and gives it to her a day before, and she answers in writing or she does not, and there is no asking out loud in a room. It costs him a day and a leaf and the asking, it is entered on the face of that day, and IT IS NOT A RESOLUTION OF ANYTHING ELSE IN THE BOOK.** They say nothing more about it all the way down that coast, because once said is once. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **368 — Thursday the twenty-second of July, the thirty-eighth day of the ninety.** The cistern charged and walked on none, the sixty-sixth. **At about nine he takes a leaf out of the drawer and writes on it in his own hand, because the procedure asks for writing and not for talking, saying what the room in Veyr wrote about a convoy with papers and that he wants to show one of the five leaves there if the room asks for it again, with the day and the hour, and he puts it on the bench in front of her and does not read it out.** She reads it where she sat and says she has it and will answer in writing or not and that tomorrow is soon enough. **He writes it in his own hand and not in hers, puts nothing against her name on it, does not ask her whether the day is enough, and turns the leaf face down on the bench; she turns it back up and neither of them says why.** A man of about forty-four of the six goes back on the water the day after his nine, as a boat's man and not a master, not paid and not asked to pay, told the terms before he went and saying he knew them; he comes past at two with a coil of line and says he had been nine days on the stone and had not been asked by anybody to do anything on any of the nine. A shipwright of about sixty says the binding would hold for a boat's work and not for a buoy's; a bonesetter of about fifty looks at it from three paces off, says it is not a bonesetter's work, has not done it and will not touch it. **A herring skipper of fifty-one with municipal papers of his own says he is not going to use them for a convoy, because his boat goes out alone and comes in alone, and NOBODY SAID HE WAS WRONG, because a door open to those who use it binds nobody who does not use it, and the room in Veyr wrote nothing about him and nobody asked it to.** A chandler of about fifty has his counter shut to one man in the front street with his wife doing the counting, a man comes to it and goes away without arguing, and nobody says anything to him, because a man who has said twice that he has nothing to say has said it twice. The copyist, the tide gang four short with a list that is not a schedule, and the dead hose at half past four. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **369 — Friday the twenty-third of July, the thirty-ninth day of the ninety.** **At about nine the woman of no office puts a leaf on the bench in her own hand and does not read it out, saying that she has read his leaf of yesterday, that no paper using her hand will be shown in any room on the strength of it this week, and that she will keep the five leaves where they are, and that is the whole of the answer.** He reads it where he sat, puts it in the drawer with the sheet in it, and says he has it and that a day waited is a day waited: **the procedure has made him wait a day and write a leaf and not ask out loud, and it has not given him anything.** **She did not forgive him on the leaf and she did not thank him on it, and what is on it is a procedure and not a pardon, and nobody in that shed improved on it. He did not hold the hiding of another year as an excuse and he did not say he was protecting her.** The ship's hand prices nothing, because there is nothing to price, and says one sentence about the week: **a door found open in a city has not fed this harbor by one penny and has not brought down the cheapest oil by one penny and has not lit the mole-head light, and that is not a defeat and is not a failure and is a harbor in July.** The cheapest thing in that town is still four hundred and fifty pence with February's three hundred and seventy-eight above it and both dates on the board, and the light is out. A man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons mends a warp and says he has no municipal papers and wants none, and nobody said he was wrong, because a man with no papers is not a man with papers unused. At ten past five the mole head, and the tender still at the outer water with two lines out and no hail. **Nothing in, nothing out.**
- **370 — Saturday the twenty-fourth of July, the fortieth day of the ninety. THE CLOSE.** **READ-BACK at four: one hundred and two, three hundred and eighty-seven, none, ninety-four; AT CLOSE: one hundred and three, three hundred and eighty-nine, none, ninety-five, the ninety-fifth the last thing in that book and the column not closed.** The first column's ninety-three at the close of the fourteenth plus ten is one hundred and three, one entry against each of the ten days and not one day in two of them. The second column's run is three hundred and thirty-nine plus three of the day's entries before the reading and two after it, and the figure is that ledger's own and is not checkable from a mole; the first's one hundred and two and the fourth's ninety-four at the hour ARE checkable by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil, and both definitions are on the face of the reading. **The third column is none on ten consecutive days, nobody has been appointed, the boy's hand is at the head of it, the name beside it was said once on the thirteenth of May past and is not said again, and HIS SURNAME IS ON NO PAGE.** Three statements, and then a fourth: the water, being the two leaves, the room, the five lines of it, the sixth line's door and the two men who did not use it; the harbor, being two people gone to a city and back, four things said out loud, her no figure, the leaf and the answer with no forgiveness on it, and nothing coming off any board; and this yard, being two hundred and four pence that stayed in the bag for ten days with nothing in and nothing out, one wipe and three charges and one wage Tuesday, the two fingers and the nine days, and the apology said once on the water and the procedure and nothing to be put under it. At ten past five the mole head: the light out, its lens out since the seventh of May, the oil at four hundred and fifty pence; **the notice on its wall in a different street for sixty-eight days and not touched**; the tender at the outer water from the tenth of July to the twenty-fourth, a lamp at her masthead, a young man of about twenty-three on her roof twice in ten days; the two objects of nobody's at four hundred and eight days about four feet from a page of six names; **the bench under that pump bare for the hundred and seventy-fourth night**; Tobias Wren on that crown with a boat's hook in his right hand and eleven pieces of a boat behind him, who is not the man on the far bench; the far bench and the shoe that is not his; the second seam a foot and seven inches where it was on the nineteenth of May and not looked at on any of the ten days, the mark four hundred yards off it, the use closed at four figures with no fifth, the ladder in another man's book, not Fisk. **THE FORTIETH DAY OF THE NINETY, AND THE VOLUME'S NEW QUESTION WAS NOT ASKED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND IS NOT ASKED AT THE MOLE HEAD, AND NO BODY AND NO COMMITTEE AND NO ASSEMBLY AND NO FLEET AND NO WING AND NO GUARD HAS BEEN PROPOSED BY ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR.** Nothing in, nothing out.

### What the batch paid, in one line

**Movement 2 entire: an inquiry on terms drawn by the Crown sitting in a room off a street behind the fish market in Veyr in which nobody has a title, no seal line is carried, a clerk of about sixty asks nothing and is asked nothing, a man of about fifty keeps the room and has no title and sits at the end of the table, and the room convicts nobody and takes nothing and closes nothing; the sixth clause's door found open to a civilian convoy under municipal papers, with the reason said in the room, written down and read back, and it binding nobody who does not use it and nobody shown to be in the wrong for not using it, proved twice over by a herring skipper with papers who will not use them and a man with none who wants none; a woman of no office making a man say out loud in a room with a clerk in it what a refusal costs, and his saying the four things without improving on them, and her saying she has no figure and will not invent one; the apology, in his own voice, in front of her, once, on the water, with no protection claimed and no hiding held out, not forgiven, not thanked and not improved on by anybody; the procedure she asked for instead — a leaf in writing a day before and no asking out loud — entered on the face of the chapter, used the next day, and answered in writing the day after with no forgiveness and no thanks on the leaf; the plate's note advanced in one instrument and one instrument only, the survey ordered and not done and not wanted by anybody in that harbor, the plate not reached and not measured and not touched and not asked about and not closed and not named, and no person of that yard in any water or any stone on any of the ten days; the labour of the ten days on the page and the harbor poorer on the twenty-fourth of July than on the fourteenth of May; and the read-back of four columns with both definitions on its face and the whole standing inventory once.**

### The volume's shape after twenty chapters of it

**Volume 08 is outlined at `outline/volume-08.md` in five movements of ten chapters and is twenty chapters old of fifty. MOVEMENTS 1 AND 2 ARE PAID. The volume has three movements left and thirty chapters, and Movement 3 is its midpoint and carries the convoy of confiscated memory vessels, the form with the word *unsealed* on it, the standing instruction dated before the blockade and countersigned with a Registry seal, the eleven weeks, the third channel, the slip of paper with seven thousand on it and no name on it, and the cost in flour. The coordinated-repair work and the keelwright stage are Movement 4's, and the word *keelwright* is in no mouth in either of the two movements written so far. The patrol, the civilian transport, the flour, the admission on a mole, the whole of the climax and the concrete resolution are Movement 5's, and the volume's new question is asked once there and answered nowhere. THE APOLOGY IS PAID AND IS NOT FORGIVEN, AND WHAT IS OPEN IS THE RELATIONSHIP, NOT THE APOLOGY. THE PLATE'S NOTE HAS ADVANCED TWICE IN FOUR VOLUMES, ONCE ON A CLAUSE IN A LETTER AND ONCE ON A LINE IN SEVEN TERMS UNDER GLASS IN A CITY, AND ONCE IN A VERY LONG WHILE ON NOTHING BY ANYBODY'S HAND. NO STAGE HAS BEEN TAKEN IN TWENTY CHAPTERS. THE HARBOR'S BAG HAS TAKEN TWO DAYS' WORK IN TWENTY DAYS AND HAS NOT MOVED AT ALL IN THE LAST TEN. AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE, WHICH WAS WRITTEN BY AN OFFICE THAT DID NOT WRITE IT FOR THAT HARBOR, IS NOW ON THE FACE OF A RECORD IN A ROOM FOUR DAYS' WATER AWAY WITH A MUNICIPAL PAPER BESIDE IT, AND THAT IS THE ONLY THING THAT HAS GOTTEN ANY FURTHER INTO AN OFFICE IN EIGHT VOLUMES.**

## Volume 08, Batch 0003 (Chapters 371–380), Movement 3, a convoy of confiscated memory vessels, and a policy written on a page. **THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT, PAID AND NOT SOFTENED.**

- **371 — Sunday the twenty-fifth of July, the forty-first day of the ninety.** Nothing in, nothing out, the bag two hundred and four pence, the wall up at the angle since the twelfth. **A woman of about fifty-eight puts the price of a boat and a man for a day on her slate in chalk with the day beside it — one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence — and gives the reason herself: three men asked her in one week and she is not saying it a fourth time out loud. A figure put on a board cannot be taken off again and this one is not going to be, and this yard did not put it there and cannot take it off.** The ship's hand prices the day before anybody agrees to it, being eight hours of a man of nineteen, a fathom of line, a night's food for two, and two tides and not one, and says that if the slate is wrong then the slate is wrong and not the day. **A man of about fifty from the office on the west basin comes up at about two and says he wants two boats and three men and a tide out and in under the municipal paper of the eighteenth of July, and that he will sign and pay and it will be in a return before the month is out. HE IS REFUSED, and the reason given is that the three men have not been asked and that a paper which needs a refusal to be true is a paper and not a return. He does not argue. He says one thing on going, that nobody has ever asked him for the fourth box on the other paper and that it has been empty since the fifth of July, and nobody improves on it.** The whole standing inventory is entered once here and carried by a short pointer after it. The notice at sixty-nine days, the objects at four hundred and nine days, the bench bare for the hundred and seventy-fifth night, the tender at the outer water for the sixteenth day.
- **372 — Monday the twenty-sixth of July, the forty-second day of the ninety.** **The sixty-fourth wipe and the sixty-seventh charge, and the top name on the rota board still off it.** A man of about thirty-two with the hose asks this yard to put the fire party's hose in a return of the office on the west basin and is refused, the reason being that a figure against that standpipe is a figure against that man and a figure against a man in a return of that office follows the man to a hard. **The hose is nobody's and is dead until the spring and no figure is put against it.** A man of the tide gang with a hod says the gang is four short and that the want of four goes in this shed's first column and in no return of any office, because a leaf in a drawer can be read and cannot be answered for. **At about one the day's boat is agreed on a bollard inside the line: a boat of perhaps eighteen tons and a man in her, out and in, at the slate's figure, in coin at the mole head before she sails. The man of nineteen says the same figure without being asked what this yard would pay, says he will not be paid twice for one day by anybody, and says a man who does not ask is a man he will take out for. NOTHING IN, NOTHING OUT.**
- **373 — Tuesday the twenty-seventh of July, the forty-third day of the ninety. THE WATER.** **The fortieth wage Tuesday, the wage not paid, forty weeks fallen due. One hundred and sixty-eight pence goes out in coin on the flat of the mole head stone at about a quarter to seven and the bag is thirty-six pence, being three shillings, and the figure short of the wage of four marks is six hundred and four pence, being three marks and ten shillings and fourpence.** The boat goes out past the line at about eight with no declaration, in breach of the first clause; no other boat of that harbor goes out; nobody was sent. **At about half past ten the tender of about ninety tons is at the head of eight boats inside the line and the outer water is empty, and the young man of about twenty-three is on her roof, and nobody tells him what she is for and he does not ask.** Eight work boats in company, nothing flying, no man-of-war. **A mate of about forty-one refuses him his boat — no room, not on her list, no paper in this harbor that puts him on it — and does not report that a boat came alongside.** A man of about twenty-six with a slate asks whether a hull lifted twice is one hull or two, is told no, and puts one stroke down, and says he asked a man in a boat instead of asking nobody. **THE BOARD: a yard wide under a sloping canvas, one word in block capitals at the head of it, being *unsealed*, two ruled columns, eleven marks in the right-hand column against dates from the eighth of May to the twenty-second of July, two impressions struck side by side at the foot of which he reads neither, and the fourteenth of February cut into the timber above the head, which is ninety-two days before the notice went up. NO DOCUMENT OF ANYBODY'S CHANGES HANDS. HE DOES NOT GET THE FORM. **AND THE ONE THING THAT COMES OFF THAT WATER IN HIS HAND IS STAGED ON THE PAGE IN THIS CHAPTER, at lines 67 to 79: the man of about twenty-six cuts a piece off the back of his own pad, sharpens the pencil on the blade of the knife in front of him, writes on it, holds it out over the gunwale and says nothing; he says he is not going to put a number on the board, because a mark goes in that column when a hull comes alongside and he is not a hull, and he says he does not know what it is a number of and cannot ask anybody in a room, and he asks for nothing and is asked for nothing, and Calder takes it, puts it inside his coat and does not look at it in that boat or in his own. He looks at it in that shed on the twenty-eighth, which is the moment Chapter 374's drawer measures from.** The tally hand: nobody in my boat has taken a thing out of anybody's boat by force; a master who is asked under that word gives it and goes on fishing; the case goes into a lighter and the lighter goes somewhere and he has not been told where. **At about one the mate says four words, *hold that*, and Calder works the chest of the water for two hours and twenty minutes, half a day's work for four men where there is work for six, unpaid, unthanked, and not reported. At about ten to five his boat comes up two foot where his book says eleven and she finds nine, and a tow of eight boats and about forty feet is coming down the fairway. HE CUTS HIS OWN STERN LINE; THE TOW TOOK HIS LINE; THE PAINTER PARTED; ELEVEN MINUTES; SIX FOOT.**
- **374 — Wednesday the twenty-eighth day of July, the forty-fourth day of the ninety.** Nothing in, nothing out; the bag thirty-six pence, being three shillings. **He writes the four things on a leaf in his own hand for the woman of no office to read where she sat and does not read it out. The slip of paper goes in the same drawer: two inches by an inch, seven thousand in pencil in a hand that is not the hand on the board, no name and nothing else on it.** The ship's hand says a figure not written out in pence and in marks and shillings and pence is not a sum of money to a shed that keeps a book, and it is entered as a slip of paper with a figure on it and no name on it, with no column head and no name, and not paid and not invoiced. **At about half past ten he says the four things out loud in that shed, in the order they happened, and does not improve on them and does not offer them against anything, and Mara Venn says nothing about it at all and the next time she comes up that hill she asks him about a procedure and not about a tow.** A man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers says he means to lie off the point on Saturday and look at the line; **he is told no**, the reason being that a boat of thirteen tons with one man in her and no paper is the first thing any office would put a name to, and the man says he came to tell and not to ask and that he would do it again, and his boat goes out on Saturday and comes in under the sixth clause with no paper of any kind, and nobody said he was wrong.
- **375 — Thursday the twenty-ninth of July, the forty-fifth day of the ninety.** **The sixty-eighth charge, charged and walked on none.** He stands in the doorway of a room off the market and does not go in. **On a fair copy on a copyist's desk there is a ruled head, a clean margin, two columns, and at the head of the left-hand one the same word, in a small fair hand and not in block capitals filled in. A fair copy in a municipal copying room is made from something somebody sent in, and nobody in that harbor sent anything into that room and nobody in that harbor keeps a case with a word at the top of it in a market room.** The copyist of about fifty-nine, twenty-two years in it, moves the sheet half an inch towards the near edge of the desk with her left hand and does not look up. **He wants to know who sends work into that room and who pays for it and is not going to ask, and gives the reason: a copyist who has never been asked what she is copying is the only kind of person in that town who can keep doing it, and the day anybody asks her is the day she is a person in a matter.** The want goes in the second column with the reason that he saw it and did not act on it. **The woman of about fifty-eight tells him, unasked, that there is no flour in that market and none coming, and that she has no figure for it because there is nothing to price, and that when it comes it goes on the slate with the day beside it and the last figure underneath.** The third channel is carried and is nobody's measurement, and the borrowed instrument is up that coast and has not come down.
- **376 — Friday the thirtieth of July, the forty-sixth day of the ninety.** Nothing in, nothing out; the bag thirty-six pence, being three shillings. **A man of about fifty-one of the six comes and asks for a day, having asked on the fifteenth of July and not since.** There is no day's work, and the bag is thirty-six pence, and a second man in that boat could not be paid and could not be told he could not be paid. **And the second reason is not about money: one of six on a boat and five of six on a stone becomes a word and a figure in a month, and the figure will be in a return and nobody will be able to find out who made it.** The man says *ask me when you have nothing to spend and no boat, and I will take what there is, and if there is nothing there will be nothing and I will not have been promised it.* **He will be asked and is not asked on that day.** Afterwards the man takes the stone off the corner of his own page and puts it in his pocket, which he had not done before, and nobody on that crown asks him why. A boy of about seventeen brings a word in and is not paid and does not know what it is: a herring skipper of fifty-one wants a day of a man and a boat on Saturday at the slate's figure. No name and no age of the boy is written down in that yard.
- **377 — Saturday the thirty-first of July, the forty-seventh day of the ninety. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE COMES IN.** Nine hours of caulking and painting on a boat of about thirty-one tons at the third lay, by the holder and a man of about twenty-nine with a caulking iron who brought his own bread and his own water out of his own hand. **The herring skipper of fifty-one puts one hundred and sixty-eight pence on the bench stone at about four and the bag is two hundred and four pence again and the figure short of the wage is four hundred and thirty-six pence.** He says that if the yard is busy in the autumn he would send work to whoever is not looking for it and is not asking for anything to be held, and the holder says he will not be busy, and he says he will ask again in the spring. **At about eleven the chandler of about fifty says the price of a barrel of lamp oil out loud in the road to a man who does not buy — four hundred and fifty pence, being thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, quoted on the first of June, with February's three hundred and seventy-eight pence, being thirty-one shillings and sixpence, left visible above it, both dates on the board, and not to be taken off — and nobody in that yard says one word to that chandler and he is not asked a third time.** A lighter of about thirty tons is lying at the quay with a foot and four inches of water in her and two tons of wet flour in her bottom, in on the night of the twenty-seventh on her own account. **A man of about fifty-three in her says *that is what happened*, says he is not going to call it anything else, asks for nothing and is given nothing and is promised nothing, and is not comforted, not thanked and not forgiven, because there was nothing to ask for and nobody asked for anything.** About twenty-six tons of that flour is in seven boats lying off the point at about a mile and has not come in.
- **378 — Sunday the first of August, the forty-eighth day of the ninety.** Nothing in, nothing out; the bag two hundred and four pence. **A man of about thirty-four of the second lay, who is not Fisk and who keeps the whole fouling ladder of that harbor in his own book and has never been asked for a copy of it, sounds three places at the edge of the fairway with a hand lead at about seven: four foot and no more at the edge of the stone, six foot and three inches a boat's length inside that, eight foot and nine inches at the third place where the lighter went. THE FIRST AND THE THIRD ARE IN THE FIRST COLUMN BECAUSE A MAN WITH A LEAD CAN GO AND GET THEM AGAIN; THE SECOND IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN BECAUSE THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THE PLACES IS IN HIS OWN BOAT LENGTHS AND NOT IN FEET.** He has had eight foot and nine inches at that place in his book since a Tuesday in the fourth of March and has never had a reason to give it to anybody. **He says he will give the whole fairway and will not give the other thing and did not name it, and that if he were asked he would put his book in his pocket and go home, and that the day a harbour asks a man for that figure is the day somebody in an office has decided what the answer is for. HE IS NOT ASKED.** A man of about forty-four of the six, the top of his left hand out of the binding for the first time since the twelfth of July, **asks to have a name put on a leaf in a drawer so that he would be the first asked and not the last, and is refused with the same reason and the same words as the hose was refused on the twenty-sixth, against the yard's own interest**, the reason being that a list becomes the boat and everybody not on it is not asked and everybody on it has a figure, and the page of six names has said a boat and no figure since the eighth of July and a list would finish it. He says he had known the answer before he came. Two lights at about a mile where there were none on Wednesday, and nobody has hailed them.
- **379 — Monday the second of August, the forty-ninth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-FIFTH WIPE AND THE SIXTY-NINTH CHARGE.** **A man of about fifty says he is going to enter the twenty-seventh of July in the box on his table for days a boat of that harbor has gone out past the line without a declaration, a box empty since the fifth of July, and that he is going to put it there himself in his own hand and his own hour rather than have it written for him by somebody who was not in the fairway. HE WAS TELLING AND NOT ASKING, AND THE HOLDER ASKED HIM NOTHING, and gave the reason out loud: a question from this yard about a boat would be a request, a request is a claim, and this yard is not entitled to the answer.** The man says he will write what he knows and will not write who was in the boat because he does not know and has not asked, and says that a person in that town who is not asked anything is a person who cannot be got to answer anything, and that there is one box in that office he would rather be empty than full. **The fourth box on the other paper was not filled and is not filled now.** At about two Calder goes to the office on the west basin and stands at the counter and asks the clerk of about sixty nothing, and the clerk asks him nothing, and they stand there for a minute and a half saying nothing to each other, and the list on that board is a list and is not a schedule and binds nobody and the hose is not on it.
- **380 — Tuesday the third of August, the fiftieth day of the ninety. THE CLOSE.** **The forty-first wage Tuesday, the wage not paid, the column unmoved, forty-one weeks fallen due. READ-BACK at four: one hundred and twelve, four hundred and thirty-seven, none, one hundred and four; AT CLOSE: one hundred and thirteen, four hundred and thirty-nine, none, one hundred and five, the hundred and fifth the last line in that book and the column not closed.** The first column's one hundred and three at the close of the twenty-fourth plus ten is one hundred and thirteen, one entry against each of the ten days and not one day in two of them; the second column's run is three hundred and eighty-nine plus five a day, three before the reading and two after it, and the figure is that ledger's own and is not checkable from a mole; the first's one hundred and twelve and the fourth's one hundred and four at the hour **are** checkable by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil, and both definitions are on the face of the reading. **The third column is none on ten consecutive days, nobody appointed, the boy's hand at the head of it not scratched out, the name beside it said once on the thirteenth of May past, HIS SURNAME ON NO PAGE, and the three nots of the eighth of June past unasked and now unasked for a fourth week.** **Mara Venn asks the only question asked in that shed that day, being whether seven thousand is money; he says he does not know and that nobody on the water said and that he is not going to guess, and she says then it is not money in this shed and that is a decision and not a finding and it goes in the second column with the reason that nobody said.** At ten past five the mole head: the light out and its lens out since the seventh of May, the oil at four hundred and fifty pence with February's above it, the notice at seventy-eight days, the tender's seventeen days at the outer water and eight at the head of a line inside it, two lights at about a mile, the objects at four hundred and eighteen days, the bench bare for the hundred and eighty-fourth night, the second seam not looked at, and the bellwright not asked in eighty days with no digit printed.

### What the batch paid, in one line

**Movement 3 entire, the volume's midpoint: eight work boats in a line inside the line with a tender of about ninety tons at the head of them, a board with one word at the head of it in block capitals and eleven marks in a column and two impressions at the foot he did not read and the fourteenth of February cut into the timber, a fair copy of the same word in a room off that market where nobody in that harbor sent anything, a slip of paper with seven thousand on it and no name on it that is entered as a slip and not as a sum, the absence stated once and in a working man's mouth, being that no master in this country has ever been given a form saying what a man outside an officer's company may be asked for; the cost in flour, paid as a tow held eleven minutes and a painter parted and a lighter of about thirty tons on the ground in about six foot with two tons of wet flour in her bottom and seven boats that have not come in and no sack that has come ashore; the second cost, paid in a municipal office on a Monday morning by a man of about fifty who was not asked to and could not have been stopped; a man of about forty-one who refused him his boat and then put him to work; a man of about twenty-six who asked a question nobody had answered; a woman of fifty-eight with a slate and a figure that cannot come off; a chandler who said his own price out loud in the road; a fouling man with three soundings and one thing he kept; the wage of four marks not paid for the fortieth and the forty-first week; a hundred and five lines in a fourth column that is not closed; and a read-back of four columns with both definitions on its face.**
