NONE OF THE FOUR MOVEMENTS TOOK A STAGE, AND THE WORD *KEELWRIGHT* IS IN NO MOUTH ON ANY PAGE OF THE FORTY, AND THE FOURTH COLUMN HAS A HUNDRED AND FIFTEEN LINES IN IT AND IS NOT CLOSED, AND THE THIRD COLUMN IS EMPTY AND UNAPPOINTED, AND A HARBOR POORER AT THE FORTIETH CHAPTER THAN AT THE FIRST IS THE STANDING CONDITION OF THE WHOLE THING, AND THE CHEAPEST THING IN IT HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE FIRST OF JUNE.**


## Volume 08, Batch 0005 (Chapters 391–400), Movement 5, *he stopped it* — the climax and the volume's close — as written, 28 September 2026

### Chapter 391 — Saturday the Fourteenth of August, the Sixty-First Day of the Ninety. A sheet ruled in that shed, and four men who said no, and what a no costs

A single sheet folded once is ruled on the bench stone at about seven in the morning with a rule that has a nick in one edge everybody in that shed knows about: a line for a master and a line for every man under him, a ruled column at the right-hand edge for a master's hand and an hour, and a head at the top of the left side carrying one to eleven with nothing under it. **Eleven was the highest number written on it and it was written before anybody was asked anything.** The ship's hand says there is no wage on it and no price against a boat on it and no figure of any kind on it, that she has not put one there, and that if anybody puts one there she will take the sheet off the bench and will not be asked twice; and when he says she has just said that twice, she says she has said it once and will say it again if it happens and he can put that in whichever column he likes. **He did not write a name on that sheet before the man gave it to him, and that is the whole of the manner of it.** Four masters are asked in the same words and all four say no, each with a reason, and no master is asked twice and no name goes against any of them. A master of about forty-seven of the third lay has been in company with men off that coast three times and had it go wrong twice, and both times it was a Wednesday and a man was not there, and the boats did not know, and he will not put a Wednesday into a file with his name at the top of it: in his boat it is a Wednesday and a man who was not there, and in a room it is a Wednesday in a file, and then it is a fact about me and not about the Wednesday. A herring skipper of fifty-one who has papers of his own and has not shown them to anybody in four years says a paper with eleven masters' names on it is a thing that is in a room by Christmas, not because anybody is wicked but because that is what a paper is, and the room has a box in it and the box has a date in it, and on the date somebody in an office that has never met him will decide that a sheet of eleven names is a record of something and he will find out from a man on a quay. A master of about fifty-eight of the second lay with a boy of nine says his boat is his bread and his boy's bread after him, and that every man in that harbour will do it if a man asks him on a quay, and what is different on a paper is that a man in an office does not have to ask him — and keeps coming back to the eleven, and would rather somebody's list of eleven were a list of things a boat wants. Two say yes. A master of about twenty-nine of the second lay came up that hill on the sixth and again on the fourteenth on his own account and was not thanked either time, and says that a name on a sheet is worth a great deal more to him than a warp, because if anything is done on that water there will be seven men in it who were there and cannot be talked out of it. A master of about thirty-six of the second lay says **he cannot read** before he says yes, and says he signs a mark and has signed one on about four things in his life, and asks for the whole of the sheet to be read to him and for his own men read back to him, because he will know by Saturday whether Calder has got them right and Calder will not. And at about four on the second slip, in the tone he uses for a figure, the cost of the four: **four men gave a day apiece, a day is a mark and eightpence, four days of it is six hundred and seventy-two pence, being four marks two shillings and eightpence, and none of that goes against the four and none of it came out of the bag, because nobody was paid for being asked. It came out of nobody.** The master of about fifty-five, who came up about four and was not asked anything, says the four of them will be at their own benches tomorrow and this yard has not asked them to be anywhere else, and Calder says that is what it costs and he is not going to improve on it before supper. **The standing inventory is entered in full on this day, once, and carried by a short pointer on the nine that follow.** At ten past five the mole head, because that is where he goes, and there was nothing up there and nobody had sent him: the light out, the two objects of nobody's at four hundred and twenty-nine days, the bench under that pump bare for the hundred and ninety-fifth night, and two lights off the point unmoved in thirteen days.

### Chapter 392 — Sunday the Fifteenth of August, the Sixty-Second Day of the Ninety. A sheet carried round seven boats, and a man who would not have his name written

He goes round the seven berths on foot with the sheet flat on his own forearm and a pencil behind his ear and no slate and no second paper, and the order of the seven is the order of the sheet, being one to eleven, and the four blanks are the four men who said no and they stayed blank all day. Every name goes on as the man who owned the boat said it, and where a man said a name in a way that did not sit down on the page it is written as he said it and he is not asked a second time about the spelling, and one master of about thirty said a surname twice differently in two hours and both were written and left side by side without a mark between them and the master said that was right and went away. **A MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY READS HIS OWN MEN BACK IN ONE GO, ALL OF THEM, WITHOUT STOPPING, and says he has not had his own crew write themselves down in nine years and was not aware it could be done in an afternoon**, and says it is right and that you have got one of them wrong and it is the second one, who is on his after thwart and will tell you so, and he is not going to; the second one was corrected in front of the man himself, a man of about twenty-two who said his own name twice before Calder had it right and then said that was the one. **ONE MAN IN ONE OF THE SEVEN BOATS WOULD NOT HAVE HIS NAME WRITTEN DOWN, AND HIS MASTER WROTE IT WITH HIS OWN HAND BECAUSE THE MAN IS ABOARD, and the reason is that a line with nothing against it is a hole and a hole in a sheet like that is a question somebody will ask him in a room in a month and he has not got the answers to that room. The man himself was not asked anything and does not know that his name is on a sheet in a pocket in a boat of about twenty-six tons, and nobody in that shed is going to tell him.** The master of about thirty-six is read the whole sheet at about eleven and again at about half past three, and does not improve on the first reading, and says when it is done that you have said the same thing twice and that it is the first time anybody has read me the same thing twice; a third reading is coming on Friday and it will be the third and not a favour. **A SECOND WARP** comes out of the master of about fifty-five's fore hatch in a bundle with a piece of twine round it, bought off the west quay on Friday out of his own hand, and the figure is not written down anywhere and is not going on the sheet or the leaf, and if Calder puts it there the warp goes back aboard and the master is not in company on the Saturday; and the reason for the warp is that he has been in company three times and in two of them a man cut his warp and the company came down on him and he went round in a sea with nobody's hand on him. A master of about forty has a man in her who can read a clock and not a watch. A master of about forty-one has a hand lead and a line and somebody in her who can use one. A master of about thirty-eight has nobody awake ashore at the other end at the hour and has not had for two years, and that goes in the second column and not on the sheet and he is not thanked. **The man of about fifty-one with six names and a boat on a piece of paper on the crown of that mole and a stone in his own pocket was not asked for a line, nothing of his went on the sheet, and he was on that crown at about four and said nothing. The man of about thirty-one of the third lay came down the hill at half past four with his bag, went past the shed, and was not asked for anything and is not going to be cited anywhere by anybody in that harbor or any other, and he did not ask to be.**

### Chapter 393 — Monday the Sixteenth of August, the Sixty-Third Day of the Ninety. The sixty-seventh wipe, the seventy-third charge, and a paper that is a list

**A MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY OF THAT THIRD LAY IS AT THE SHED DOOR AT NINE IN THE MORNING AND IS NOT THE FIRST ONE THERE AND NOT THE LAST**, and he puts his hand flat on the bench stone about a foot from the sheet and asks for the words again so that he can say his and go and get his warp mended. He is given the words, and when he says that on the fourth the yard said that the day a yard writes down who turns up that yard has a list, and a list is the boat, he says that is what was said and he is not going to improve on it and is not going to say it a second time because the man is asking him to, which is a thing he has noticed men do. Then he says his own question, which is that sheet: he has a boat of thirty tons and about nine men in her and every one of their names is on it, and his own name at the foot of it in his own hand, and on Friday he is going to sail in company with six other boats out of that harbor on a flood because of a piece of paper; and what a piece of paper is, is a way of asking a man a question in three months in a town he has not been to. He puts his finger on a name and does not move it: **that is a list, and you have told me for twelve days that a list is the boat, and the thing you have just told me not to do you have done, and you have done it with a rule instead of a pen, and I did not come up here to be clever about it, I came up here because I am going to be in that water on Saturday and I would rather say it on a Monday.** And Calder says it is a list, and will not argue the word with him, and then gives the whole of what he has got against it, once: that paper says who is going and does not say who is going to be there, and that is the difference between those two and the whole of what a day out and a day back is, and that if he had a second sheet with the men who will be on the mole head at four in the morning in it, this one would be a hand's breadth wider and there would be two of them and the second would have a name against a man who cannot sleep and a name against a man who is owed forty marks in that harbor. The master says that does not make the paper clean, and he has not said it does; he has said it is the whole of what he has got against it, and that the thing he has not got is the thing the yard refused to write down on the fourth, and there is no way to get it onto paper without making the paper worse. **Nessa writes the man's words and her own reason against them and does not join them with a colon, and enters that he came up the hill on purpose and was not sent for and was not thanked and is not going to be.** At about four Calder goes down to the second lay and asks the caulker for the seventeenth by name, on the Monday, so that he can say no to it while there is still a Monday left, and the caulker says he did that on purpose.

### Chapter 394 — Tuesday the Seventeenth of August, the Sixty-Fourth Day of the Ninety. The forty-third wage Tuesday, and a Saturday eight pence beyond the bag

**THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, WAS NOT PAID, THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE, AND FORTY-THREE WEEKS STAND FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE AGAINST ANY OF THEM.** Isaac Fell is on the mole head at about four in the morning with a maul and a bucket of oakum and his own hands and has been there since about half past three, and he is not surprised to see anybody and does not say so. He works the day where he is told to work it, which is the whole of the day, going round the seven in the order of the sheet, and he does not do the big things and does not say that he has done the big things: he puts oakum in the seams that want oakum and drives it with his own maul and caulks about nine feet of a garboard on the second lay that has been open since June and that nobody wanted, and he says what he would do to the other seams and does not do them, and he is on the mole head at about four in the afternoon with his hands black to the wrist. **He says a day is a day and he has been paid for it at four o'clock and he is not going to be told at four o'clock that it was more than that, and is not going to be told at the end of a Saturday that it was less than that either.** Then the price, out loud, before anybody has agreed to anything, which is the only thing anybody in that yard is asked to do: **two days of that man is three hundred and thirty-six pence, being two marks one shilling and fourpence, and there are three hundred and twenty-eight pence in the bag, being two marks and eightpence, so the second day is eight pence more than the yard has got, and a yard that has not got a figure has not got a Saturday, and I am not going to write a Saturday in that column against a day it cannot pay for.** He says he will earn it before Friday, at a berth, out of that yard's own figures, and not one penny out of the man with two papers or out of the owner of any of those seven boats, and that the man on the stone is not to be paid by the person who wants the thing looked at, and that that is standing and is the reason the yard is short and the two are not to be added together. She prices the earning too, at the same figure, and says she has not got a figure for the man who does not sleep and is not going to invent one at half past ten in the morning on a Tuesday. **A MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE OF THAT THIRD LAY COMES UP THE HILL AT TWO AND SAYS HE HAS HEARD THERE IS A SATURDAY AND THAT HE IS NOT ON IT AND IS NOT ON THE PAPER AND HAS NOT BEEN ASKED AND IS NOT GOING TO BE, and that he has come up so that if a man in a room in a month asks whether he was in company on the twenty-first he can say he knew about it and was not in it, and that his papers are in a locker in a house in another street with three things in it that are not paper, and that he thought about the reason he gave on the eleventh and would not take it back.** Nothing is written on that sheet about him and he is not thanked and nobody has ever said he was right. At about half past four the caulker is paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence in coin on the flat of the stone, and when Calder asks him for the Saturday he says he has not said no, and that he will be at the stone at half past three on the Saturday either way, because that is where he is at half past three, and neither of them will be able to say he said yes to a thing he was not asked for — and asks to be asked again on Thursday. He is asked again on Thursday.

### Chapter 395 — Wednesday the Eighteenth of August, the Sixty-Fifth Day of the Ninety. One hundred and sixty-eight pence in, and a skipper who has been asked by somebody else

A boat of about nineteen tons belonging to a man of about forty of the second lay wanted a seam opened and caulked in one day at the price in chalk and got it. **They were on the berth two tides and not one**, and the tide gang's want of four men is on no board in that harbor and is in the first column of that leaf and in no return of any office, and there were three men on that work and the fourth thing was done by the man who owns the leaf, and he was slow at it and a man of about twenty-six said so once and then did not say it again. **The man of about nineteen had the tiller from half past six until about six and said the figure first, before anybody had said anything about money at all: one hundred and sixty-eight pence, that is what it is, I have not asked you what you would pay and I am not going to ask you, and I am not going to be paid twice for one day by anybody, and if anybody on that quay offers me a second mark and eightpence for this day for carrying a sheet of paper in my pocket I am going to hand it back and you can have your sheet.** And then he says he does not want it said out loud, he wants it not to happen, and those are two different things and the second one is the one he is paid for. At about two he says there is a boat going down the reach at a mile and a half with two boats in company and no lights showing and she is not one of that harbor's, and that he had seen her on the ninth at the other end of the tow of flour boats and had not written it down then and is not writing it down now: that is all she is and that is all he has got and he is not going to have anybody make a thing out of his having seen a boat. **A HERRING SKIPPER OF FIFTY-ONE COMES UP THE HILL AT FOUR AND SAYS HE HAS BEEN ASKED THIS WEEK BY SOMEBODY WHETHER HE WANTS TO TAKE HIS NO BACK, and will not say who and is not going to be asked, and will not say what he said either, and says that if he did it would be worth nothing because he has said the same words to about four men in eleven years and it has never once been taken off him.** Then the rest of it: he said no on the fourteenth with a reason about a room and a box and a date, and the yard wrote it on a leaf with the hour against it and no name against it and did not ask him twice, and that is the whole of what he has got out of this; and on Friday seven men are going to put their hands at the foot of a sheet in front of him and go out on a flood, and he is not going to do it, and he has thought about it for four days at sea and has a new reason and the new reason is worse than the old one, **because when it happens there will be a record that a man sailed and a record that a man did not, and both of them will be in the same room, and the one that says a man did not will be the one somebody asks about.** He says no more than that and Calder does not improve on it and does not say he is proud of him and does not put it in a return, and the skipper goes down the third lay under the sixth clause and was not thanked. At about half past five Calder goes up the mole and stops at the foot of it, and there are two men at the bottom of the steps and neither of them is waiting for him: the man of about fifty-one is on the crown with his own page and his own stone and has said nothing about it for thirty-five days and was not asked for a word, and **a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers stands four feet below him, looks up at the page for about as long as it takes to read a thing, does not go up, does not speak, and goes away down the slip with a fold of a notice of the seventeenth of May past in his own inside pocket which nobody in that harbor wrote and which he has had in that coat since before the spring, and he is not going out on the Saturday and nobody asked him whether he was and he did not offer.** Nothing came into that yard in the five days since the fourteenth except that one day at a berth, and nothing went out of it except that one Tuesday.

### Chapter 396 — Thursday the Nineteenth of August, the Sixty-Sixth Day of the Ninety. A route he can draw and cannot take anybody down, and a sheet nobody put up

The cistern is charged for the seventy-fourth time and walked on by none of it and the top name on the rota board is still off it. He does not go out on the Thursday. He sits in the shed from about nine until about one with the leaf open and a chart of the reach below the foul weighted at the corners, **and gets no further with it on the said day than he had got with it on the thirteenth.** The reach below the foul comes out a mile and a half inside the point, there is a channel in it he has never been down, he has three soundings off a hand lead on a leaf a stranger with a lead could go and take again, and the two places he put on it are in a man's own boat lengths and not in feet, because the man who gave them gave them that way and would not be asked to change them. **The third channel is three iron rings on a pinger on a buoy that came adrift on the twelfth of July and is nobody's measurement; nobody in that harbor put it there and nobody has been down it, and the pinger went back up that coast on the Tuesday of the thirteenth and has not come down and there is no hand on that coast that has it. So I have a route out and I cannot take anybody down it, and if I say it in one more breath as a route out then I will be saying a thing I cannot do, and I have been caught doing that once in a month already and I am not doing it twice.** And of the man of about thirty-four of the second lay: he keeps the whole fouling ladder in his own book and gave three soundings on the first of August and kept one back and told him plainly there is one thing in that book he will not give and did not name it, and that if he was asked he would put the book in his pocket and go home; he was not asked on the first and is not going to be asked by anybody in that crew before the Saturday or after it, and he is not going to be the man who teaches them that a thing can be asked for twice. **A thing you can draw is not a thing you have got.** Nessa enters it in the second column with the reason: no sounding was taken on that reach on that day by anybody, and a route nobody has been down is not a passage and is not being written down as one. He goes up to the mole head at about four in the morning because there is nothing else to do at that hour and because that is where he goes, **and there is nobody on the flat of the bench stone, and a maul on the step and a bucket with three inches of rainwater in it, and he stands there about two minutes and goes down and does not go back at four in the afternoon and does not look for the man and does not ask anybody where he was, and nobody in that harbor was told anything about it because there was nothing to tell, and it went in no column of any ledger and it is not an absence and it is not a fault and it is not a lesson.** The woman of about fifty-eight tells him at about half past two at the end stall, without being asked, that **there is a sheet up in the front street since Friday with a seal she cannot read and about nine lines in a small hand that her man cannot read either, and that there is a figure on the other side of the board where the other sheet was, so whoever put it there did not take the figure off first.** He reads it at a quarter to four, standing, with his hat in his hand, for about as long as it takes to read nine lines twice, and nobody in that street spoke to him and he spoke to nobody. It says that certain work is taken out of other men's hulls in this and in every other port by concerns that keep no account of it, and that a concern which takes work out of a hull and keeps no account of what it has taken is a concern whose accounts no man has ever seen, and that the Crown proposes that every such concern be entered in one register, and that a concern not entered in that register is a concern whose accounts are not to be produced to anybody. **It named no person, named no harbor, put no figure on it, has no price at the end, asks nothing of anybody standing in that street, does not say the work was stolen, does not say the men in it were paid, and does not say anything at all about a date.** He puts his hat back on and goes to the quay. At about half past four he asks the caulker for the Saturday for the third time and this time he has been asked, and gets yes, and is not thanked and is not put on a board, and the caulker says he said both of those once already on the tenth and has not forgotten it and does not have to be told again.

### Chapter 397 — Friday the Twentieth of August, the Sixty-Seventh Day of the Ninety. Seven hands, a mark made with a pencil, and a day named out loud

The sheet goes round the front room of the shed on the bench stone and nobody reads it out to anybody who can read it, because there is nothing on it that a man who could read wanted. **The master of about fifty-five puts his hand at the foot of it at about nine and gives the hour himself, a quarter to nine, and Calder writes the hour and not the name of the hour and the master reads it back and says it is right.** Then the master of about thirty at about half past nine, who gives the hour and does not read it back because he cannot read and had not offered to and nobody asked him to; then the masters of about forty of the second lay, about forty-one of that lay, about thirty-eight of that lay and about twenty-nine of that second lay, in that order, at eleven, twenty past eleven, twenty-five minutes to twelve and half past twelve. **That is seven hands and seven hours and the sheet does not say what any of them is paid and does not say what any of them owes and does not say what day it is.** The seventh is the master of about thirty-six of the second lay, who cannot read and never has been able to write his own name, and the whole of the sheet is read out to him a third time at about a quarter past one from the top without skipping a line and without reading the hours out of an order of his own choosing, and when Calder comes to the end of the left side the man puts his own thumb on the bench stone and stops him: read me the two at the top again, the first man in the first boat and the second man in the first boat, I have been sitting here for an hour and I want to hear those two and I am not going to tell you why. **They are read again and the man says that was right and nothing else and Calder does not ask him why, and the man then puts a mark at the foot of the sheet with the blunt end of a pencil that was not sharpened for it, being a cross with one arm longer than the other, and gives the hour, twenty-five minutes to two, and Calder writes the hour and writes the word *mark* against the hand and not the word *signature*.** Nobody was asked to sign anything in advance, every one of the seven came and put his own hand at the foot of it on the day, every one of them was told what was in it and what was not in it before he put anything at the foot of it, and the four blank lines are the four men who said no. **At about two the holder goes down to the head of the third lay and says the name of the day out loud in front of the boats, because he has said on the tenth and again on the thirteenth that he would say it on a quay and not in a shed: Saturday the twenty-first of August, out on the flood at about half past seven and in on the evening's flood at about half past five, seven of you and a sheet between you and a man on that mole head at four in the morning and at four in the afternoon, asked for that day by name, paid for it at four o'clock on the day and not before and not after, out of his own figures and not one penny out of the owner of any boat on that quay.** About nine men are on the quay or the steps and nobody says anything. **The reason is the tide: a flood is the only water that harbor can make and the only hour a loaded transport can come down that reach going that way, and that is the reason and that reason is true. It is not the whole of the reason.** The master of about thirty says then say the rest of it, and he says no, and says he has said a quarter of it and the quarter he has said is true and the three quarters he has not said are his and he is not going to lay them on a quay in front of nine men on a Friday afternoon, because if he says them now then in a week somebody will quote him and he will have said it in the wrong order to the wrong men, and that he will hear the rest of it from him and not to a man on a quay asking him a question, and that he is telling them now that he is not going to pretend otherwise and he would rather a man be angry with him on a Friday than disappointed on a Monday. The master of about thirty says he is not angry, he is going to be in that water in a day and has a right to know what the rest of it is, and that he has been told twice now that he will not say it and that is a thing at least. **The tender of about ninety tons was at the head of eight boats inside the line on the said day, being her twenty-fifth day, counting the twenty-five days from the morning of the twenty-seventh of July past and the seventeen days she lay at that outer water before that, and was not there on the Saturday morning, and this yard did not see her go and has not asked anybody where she went and is not going to, and nobody has written a day against either of those two facts and neither is in any return.** And a woman of about fifty-eight comes down the front street at about four with her slate under her arm and puts it on the bench stone face up, which she does not do, and says that on Saturday morning, when those boats are on the water and she has not got a thing to sell anybody who is not going out, there will be nine men in that market who have not got a boat and who will ask her what a mark and eightpence buys, and that she will tell them what it buys, and that she is telling this yard on a Friday that she is not going to tell them one word about a sheet in a boat or a man on a stone, and would rather this yard knew that before Saturday than after it. She has done it for the nine.

### Chapter 398 — Saturday the Twenty-First of August, the Sixty-Eighth Day of the Ninety. The sending, the attack, the work stopping at eleven, and the man who walked away

The seven lie off the point at about a mile at half past six, and the master of about fifty-five has the sheet folded in his own inside pocket with the seven hands and the seven hours on the outside of the fold where any man in any of the seven boats could put his thumb and feel them. **Calder goes out in his own boat of about nineteen tons with the man of about nineteen, past the outer marks at about half past seven, on a breach of the first clause of a notice of the seventeenth of May past, which is the way it is done; no declaration went with her, no paper of that yard's went in her, nobody hailed them going out and nobody hailed them coming in, no man of that yard was put aboard any of the seven, and not one penny of any of that came out of the owner of any boat. They do nothing for the first two hours, and that is the work.** At about ten he goes alongside the second of the seven and puts himself where the seven can hear one voice, and says out loud, once, in a boat, on the water, that he is going to say the same thing in seven boats and it takes about nine minutes in each and they have all heard it in the shed and he is saying it now because **a thing said in a shed in a town is a thing a man in a room can write down as a thing somebody said in a shed, and this is not that**; and each of them will say what their boat has and has not got and the hour, and it goes on a leaf in the wet in his own pocket and back in the shed tonight and nowhere near any office; and then the four things and the fifth thing, being a man on a mole head at four in the morning and at four in the afternoon who is not on that sheet and not on that leaf and not on a board and not on a list, and is on a day and a wage and an hour, and whose wage is a mark and eightpence out of the holder's own figures and not one penny out of the owner of any of their boats, **said on the water so that there is a man on this water who has heard it said.** They say it. Seven boats and about thirty men, two of them with nothing and saying so, and one of the seven saying he has a spare warp and a second one he bought out of his own pocket on the fifteenth, the figure for which is not on any paper in that harbor and was not said out loud on the water and was not asked for. Then, at about twenty past ten, a boat of about thirty tons came down the reach. **She was a transport of about a hundred and forty tons with a merchant's company aboard and about sixty tons of flour in her and three boats of her own in tow, coming down that reach on the flood going the way a loaded transport comes down that reach going that way, which is the only way she can come, and which is the reason that harbor can make.** At about half past ten the small boat of about twelve tons, with a boat's boat in her and a lever of about nineteen at her tiller, came out from the deep water with two of hers, and a boat's boat went along the transport's port side. **They cut her fore cable with a wire and stove her fore hatch with a maul and put a hole in her garboard with a boat's hook, and the three of her own boats in tow cut their own painters and went their own ways, and the transport came on down the reach with her fore hatch open and about half of what she had in her in the water by the time she was inside the point, at about one in the afternoon. Nobody was hurt. Nobody was named. Nobody was counted, and no figure of anybody came ashore with her, and nobody in that harbor has laid a claim for anything and nobody has asked for a thing. The flour of that transport did not all come ashore and did not come ashore at all into that harbor, and nobody has been made whole, and the paper of her own company says nothing about the four hours between the half past ten and the one o'clock and nobody has asked for a copy of it. ALL SEVEN BOATS SAW IT, EVERY ONE OF THEM AND EVERY MAN IN THEM, AND THE ONLY THING THAT ANY OF THEM HAD TO MAKE IT A RECORD WAS A SHEET OF PAPER WITH THEIR OWN NAMES ON IT IN A MASTER'S POCKET, AND THE MASTER OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE PUT HIS THUMB ON THE FOLD AND SAID ONE WORD OUT LOUD, AND NOBODY TOOK IT DOWN.** The nine boats of the closed-sea squadron were in company inside the line at about a mile and a half at the same hour, working from civilian hulls the way they had been working since the eighth of May. **Calder saw them first and said nothing about them for about twenty minutes, and what he did at about eleven was put his own boat across the reach into the middle of the seven and say, in the same voice he used for nine minutes in seven boats, one more thing, and that he is not going to say it in a room tonight either so that nobody in that harbor can tell him he said it in a room first and then in a boat: on the twenty-seventh of July past he lay alongside a boat in a line inside the line and read a board off an after thwart under a sloping canvas and did not get it and did not get near it and did not ask.** It is about a yard wide; there is one word at the head of it in block capitals and the word is *UNSEALED*; there are two ruled columns under it; in the right-hand one there are eleven marks against dates and the first of the dates is the eighth of May and the last of them is the twenty-second of July; at the foot of it there are two impressions struck side by side and he read neither of them and does not know whose they are and is not going to find out this morning; and above the head of the board there is a date cut into the timber, and the date is the fourteenth of February. Nobody in the seven boats said anything and the water did not say anything. **And then: that is a shape and it is not a sheet, and he has not got the sheet and there is no copy of it in that shed and no document of yours has changed hands with me at any hour since the spring and nothing in my pocket is yours, and he is not going to stand in that boat and say a word about what was in any of those eleven hulls, because he does not know and is not going to guess, and is not going to say a word about any man who was aboard any of them, because he does not know that either and a man in a room will ask him for it and he will not have it.** The work on that reach stopped at about eleven and did not start again that day, **and it stopped the way work stops, which is that a man put a maul down and then eleven other men put theirs down over about a quarter of an hour, and not one of them was brave.** It stopped because a thing done in front of about thirty men in seven boats with a sheet of paper naming every one of them in a master's pocket is a thing somebody will write down, and because the word at the head of the board is a word about what the work is, and thirty men on that water had that word in their ears at the same minute and in the same words from one mouth. **The man with the board under his arm was in the third of the nine boats, and he had a satchel across him and he was about thirty-one and he was not an officer and nobody in that harbor had ever seen his face before. He stepped from the third boat into the boat's boat of the second of the nine at about twenty past eleven and the boat's boat went away up the reach at ten knots or thereabouts, and the master of about forty-one of that third lay had a boat at the quarter of his own with the man of about twenty-two in her, and a boat at the quarter is forty minutes behind a boat's boat and is a great deal more than forty minutes ahead of a man in another man's hull with a lead line and no water in his own boat. Calder did not ask him. The master of about forty-one looked at him. Calder did not ask him and the master of about forty-one did not go, and his man of about twenty-two did not take the painter out, and the boat's boat was inside the point at about noon and was not seen again that day by anybody in that harbor, and nobody stopped the man who was in it and nobody asked him where he was going and nobody thanked him for anything and he is not mentioned again in a room by anybody in this series.** "You had him." "I had him." And nothing else is said about it, and Calder did not improve on it and did not explain it and did not say what the other thing was, and it is one line in the second column and it is not in the first column and it is in no return and it is in no office and it was not entered in the wage column and it cost nothing and it is not nothing. **AND THE MAN WITH THE BOARD UNDER HIS ARM WALKED AWAY FROM IT, AND HE WAS NOT STOPPED, AND HE WAS NOT ASKED WHERE HE WAS GOING, AND HE WAS NOT THANKED, AND HE WAS NOT MENTIONED AGAIN IN A ROOM, AND THE COST OF THAT IS A SHEET THAT STILL EXISTS SOMEWHERE AND IS NOT IN THAT HARBOR AND IS NOT IN THAT SHED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THIS VOLUME COST AND IT IS NOT A WOUND AND IT IS NOT A DEATH.** Fell is paid at about four, in coin, out of the bag, and says he was on the stone at half past three and all day at both ends of it, and that he was not asked for the Sunday and will not be on here on the Sunday, and he is telling you that now so that you do not come up on the Sunday and find nobody and stand there and make something of it; and Calder says he was up there on the Thursday morning at four and there was nobody on it and he did not stand there and make something of it and has not said one word to anybody about it and is not going to, and that there were two of those now and Fell is not going to charge for the two. The seven come in at about half past five on the sixth clause, which is free, and the sheet goes back into a man's own pocket on the mole and no man of that yard said a word about it at any time. **A tender of about ninety tons that had been at the head of eight boats inside the line for twenty-five days, being that the twentieth of August is her twenty-fifth day from the morning of the twenty-seventh of July past, was not there on the said morning and was not seen again on that reach, and the work of a squadron on that reach stopped at about eleven and did not start again that day, and a ship of about sixty tons with the squadron's own boats in company with her went up-coast in the night, and the small boat of about twelve tons went up-coast in front of her and did not come back down.** A man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait is on the quay at about ten past six with his own painter over his shoulder, and says what he saw, and that she was not a man-of-war and she had a company aboard and a master's company, and that he has been up and down that reach for eleven years and knows what a man-of-war's lights look like and that was not one, and that the little one went up-coast and is not on that reach and he has been past that reach twice since; and that their work on that reach stopped at about eleven and there was nothing on the water at all after about twelve; and that is what he saw and he is not here to tell you what it means and he has not come up here to be thanked and you are not going to thank me. In that shed at about half past nine that night, in one sentence, and not improved on by anybody afterwards, Calder said that the squadron had lost the ship and that the man who had it had gone up-coast, and that not one penny of it had come into that yard and there was nothing in that yard's leaf that came of it, and that it was not a victory and there was nobody in that harbor to whom it was one.

### Chapter 399 — Sunday the Twenty-Second of August, the Sixty-Ninth Day of the Ninety. The eleven weeks in a room, the admission on a mole, the question, and a thing said once

The room is over the fish market and is let out on a Sunday to anybody who wants it, and the man who lets it takes the money in a bowl on the step and does not ask who is going in. **There is no clerk in that room and no board on the wall of it and no list and no name over the door.** He goes up at about eleven with a leaf and nothing else, and he said four things before he read it and was not going to say them again that month: he has not got the sheet and there is no copy of it in that shed and nothing in his pocket is anybody's; he is reading dates off a leaf in his own hand and has not moved one of them to make it come out even; anybody who wants to write any of it down may write it down and it is theirs and he is not going to know their names; and he is going to read the shape of a thing after the eleven and not before them, and say why afterwards and not now. **He read the eleven dates: the eighth of May, the fifteenth, the twenty-second, the twenty-ninth, the fifth of June, the twelfth, the nineteenth, the twenty-sixth, the third of July, the tenth, and the twenty-second of July.** Ten of those are a week apart and the last one is twelve days after the one before it, and that is what the board says and he has not tidied it. A man at the back says eleven boats, and Calder says eleven hulls, not eleven men, not eleven families, and that he does not know who was aboard any of those eleven and has not asked and is not going to ask, and that if a man in a room in a month asks him who was in any of them he is going to tell him he does not know, and that is going to be the answer whatever is in the room. About forty people in a room will say something at some point, and nothing was said. A man near the middle says a hand lead and a line would be worth putting in a column, and Calder says it would and he is glad he said it and is not going to use it. **Then he read the shape, flat and without stopping: one word at the head of it in block capitals and the word is *UNSEALED*; two ruled columns under it; the eleven marks he has just read against the eleven dates; at the foot of it two impressions struck side by side and he read neither and does not know whose they are and is not going to find out; and above the head of the board a date cut into the timber, being the fourteenth of February, and that is ninety-two days before the notice went up on a wall in a street two doors from where he is standing.** Then the fourth thing, afterwards, as promised: he read it after the eleven and not before them because he has not got it, and if he had said the word at the top first then forty people in that room would be thinking about a word, and in a year the word would be what happened and the eleven hulls would be what was said about it, and they are not — eleven hulls is what happened, a word is what somebody wrote at the top of a board, and he cannot read the two impressions and the man who can is not in that room and may never be in that room. The woman of about fifty-eight asks the room whether the flour is coming back, and he says no, and that he is not going to tell her a figure for it because he has not got one, and that there is no flour in that market and there is not going to be any this month. **THE SLIP OF PAPER DID NOT COME UP THAT STAIR.** At about four in the afternoon he is on the flat of the bench stone with about sixty people on that mole, and the master of about fifty-five is against the parapet with his arms on it and has not said anything for ten minutes, the master of about thirty is beside him, the master of about thirty-six is on the third step, the man of about thirty-four of the packet is on the ground with his own painter across his knees and his own painter had been across his knees all day and he had not asked anybody for anything, and the man of about thirty-eight with no papers is at the head of the steps and came on his own account and is not thanked. He says he has got about four minutes and is going to use them, and is going to say it once, and is not going to say it a second time this month and is not going to have anybody say it for him, and that if you want to say something to me you can say it down at the shed and not up here. **And he said it, in his own voice, at the speed of a man reading a figure: Saturday the twenty-first of August; he named the day on a quay on the Friday and said the reason was the tide, and the tide was the reason and it was about a quarter of the reason; he chose that day; he knew it was the flood when he chose it; nobody made him name it and nobody put it in his mouth; and he did not ask what else goes down that reach on the flood, and did not ask because he did not want the answer, and that is the whole of it and it is not going to get better by me saying it slower. A transport of about a hundred and forty tons with a merchant's company aboard and about sixty tons of flour and three of her own boats in tow came down that reach at about half past ten; they cut her fore cable with a wire and stove her fore hatch with a maul and put a hole in her garboard with a boat's hook; about half of what she had was in the water by the time she was inside the point at one o'clock; none of that flour is in this harbor; nobody has laid a claim for a pound of it; nobody has been made whole; nobody was hurt; nobody has been counted and he is not going to count anybody and is not going to say one word about a man who was aboard that transport or a man who was in the water this morning, because he does not know and will not guess. And then the three things people are going to reach for, which he reaches for first so that nobody else has to: two foot of water on a line made by a man who is dead is nobody's arithmetic and he is not putting it against the flour because it is not his to put anywhere, and if it had been his he would be standing here just the same and he wants that said in that order and not in the other order; that mole is four thousand seven hundred yards of second seam off a board in the office on the west basin and there is not one man in this harbor keeping it and there never has been one, and he is not going to stand up there and tell sixty people that a mole is long, because a mole being long is a thing you all know and is not an answer to a boat's fore hatch, and he has watched a man get ready to say it and has said it first; and this harbor is poorer tonight than it was in May and will be poorer in September, and that is not what the flour was and he is putting the two side by side because both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other.** Then he stopped, and about four seconds passed on that mole, and then he said: that is all of it, I am not going to say it again and I am not going to have anybody in this harbor say it for me, and I am not going to be told up here that I did my best, and if anybody wants to tell me that they can tell me down at the shed and I will not thank them for it. **Nobody said anything. Nobody put a hand on him. Nobody stood at his shoulder. Nobody said that he was brave and nobody said that he had done his best and nobody said that it was not his fault and nobody said the patrol was going down that reach anyway. The master of about fifty-five took his arms off the parapet and said nothing, and the master of about thirty said nothing, and the master of about thirty-six said one thing and only one thing, to the water: she was not there to be caught, she was there because that is the water.** "That is right," Calder said, "and I have not got one word to add to that, and I am not going to." At about half past five he goes down to the office on the west basin, and a man of about fifty is at his table with his two papers and the fourth box on the other one still empty, and says he has read a paper and is not going to give it to him and is not going to ask for it back and is not here about a boat. **When Calder asks him to read the clause, he says that is a request, and he is not going to be asked for it and is not going to give it, and what he will do is say there is a clause and what shape it is: it gives two named people a look at one thing out of three in that office's custody room, somebody of that office stands in the room the whole time, an hour is named on it and that hour is the end of it and not the middle, and nothing goes out of that room in any hand, in those words, and it is a clause about a door and a man standing at the door and not about an opening.** And the third of the three is not on it and is not named on it, and there is a claim on it in a book in that office that has been there since the December before last and he has never seen anybody come in to take it back, and he is not going to be the one who starts that this month. He goes back to his table and does not look up again. **And at about ten to six, with the clerk of about sixty in the room — twenty-two years in it, owed a quarter, no book and no power — Calder asked him one question, out loud, once: *If the Navy cannot own the sea by force, is the Crown going to try to own history by making it legally singular?*** The clerk put his thumb down on the edge of the board on that wall, which is a list and is not a schedule and binds nobody, and looked at the list for a while, and said: I have not got a book for that, and he wanted to say that straight because it had been asked in a room and there was a man in it, and he has been in that room twenty-two years and has never once been asked a question he could answer and is not going to start on a Sunday; and he is not going to say yes and is not going to say no, and is not going to tell him what the Crown is going to do, because he has not got a book for that either. **NOBODY HAS ANSWERED IT SINCE AND IT IS NOT ANSWERED NOWHERE ELSE EITHER.** At about six she is on the crown of that mole with the market gone off it and the light out and the flat of the bench stone bare, with a maul on the step and a bucket with an inch of rain in it, and Calder does not stand on it and does not look at it for longer than a man looks at a step, and she does not look at it either, and neither of them says one word about it and it is not going into any column of any ledger and it is not a fault and it is not going to be turned into anything today. And she says: say the rest of it as a thing and not as a reason; I have had a reason off you on a mole an hour and a half ago and I am not going to have it twice, and I am not going to thank you for having it, and I am not going to forgive you for it, and the forty marks is not what I am standing here for and it is not going to be reduced by anything that happened on this mole this afternoon. He said nothing. **Then: you are going to do it again, not this, something with a day named on a quay in it, and the day after you name it you are going to come up that hill and tell me what it is, and I am not going to ask you for it, and if you come and tell me and I do not like it then that is what happens and I will not make a scene about it and I will not stand in that shed and make a scene about it either.** "That is standing," Calder said, "and I am not going to put it in a column and I am not going to put it in a return and I am not going to say it out loud in front of anybody else." And she said: you are not going to put it anywhere and I am going to be the one holding it, and that is the whole of what there is; and it is not a rescue and it is not a reward for a mole and it is not the apology either; she has the apology given on the water on the twenty-first of July and has not forgiven it and is not going to forgive it tonight, and a second one is not coming on that mole, and if he tried to give her one on this mole she would go down that slip and he would not see her for a fortnight; and it is not a rescue will go down that slip and you will not see me for a fortnight; and I am not going into that shed's book and you are not going into my hand, and the two of us are not going to be a thing that a man in a room can put in one line with a figure under it, and if anybody in this harbor or any other asks me what you are to me I am going to tell them the truth, which is that you tell me before and I do not agree and neither of us is paid for the other. "That is the whole of it." "That is the whole of it, and it is not a good thing, and it is not going to be a good thing, and nobody in this harbor is going to be told about it, and I am not going to be thanked for it and you are not going to be thanked for it and if either of us starts thanking the other for it I will stop coming up that hill." **THE COMMITTED RELATIONSHIP BEGINS ON THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE AT ABOUT SIX IN THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-SECOND, IN A FEW SENTENCES, AND IT IS NOT A MARRIAGE, AND IT IS NOT SEALED, AND THE WORK IS NOT MERGED, AND SHE IS NOT RESTORED, AND FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD IS NEITHER REDUCED NOR PAID AND IS NOT GOING TO BE, AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR WAS TOLD ANYTHING ABOUT IT AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR IS GOING TO BE TOLD ANYTHING ABOUT IT.**

### Chapter 400 — Monday the Twenty-Third of August, the Seventieth Day of the Ninety. The last page: the mole head at ten past five, the read-back, three statements, the inventory once, and a door in a corridor

**The wall came down bare for the sixty-eighth time at about eight and went up at the angle it has been at since the twelfth with nobody putting it back, and the cistern was charged for the seventy-fifth time at about eight and walked on by none of it at about half past nine, and the top name on the rota board is still off it. Nothing came into that yard and nothing went out of it, and the whole of what came into it in the ten days ended on the said day is one hundred and sixty-eight pence on one day, being the eighteenth, at a berth, and the whole of what went out is three hundred and thirty-six pence on two days, being a Tuesday and a Saturday of a man of about twenty-three, out of that yard's own money, and three hundred and twenty-eight plus one hundred and sixty-eight minus three hundred and thirty-six is one hundred and sixty pence, and the two sums are not the same figure and neither of them is the wage of four marks.** Forty-three weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them, and the forty-fourth falls on Tuesday the twenty-fourth, which is outside these ten days. Nothing happened on the said Monday, and that is the whole of the last working day of that yard in that month and it is said as a fact and not as a fault. **The caulker of about twenty-three was at his own bench on the second lay and caulked the rest of the nine feet of garboard he opened in June that nobody wanted, and nobody asked him for that day and he has not been paid since the Saturday and will not be paid again until somebody asks him for a day by name on a day.** The man of about fifty-one is up on the crown with his six names and his boat and no figure in his own hand and his own stone in his own pocket, and has said nothing to anybody about that page for forty days and was not asked for a word about it, and no boat was promised to him and no wage and no figure and nothing of his is in anything, and his page is not in any return and is not going to be taken down by anybody. At about half past five he goes up the mole. **There is no light in it.** The lens has been out of that lamp since the seventh of May past and it was dark on the twenty-third of August as it was dark on the twenty-third of May before it, and the board in the front street carries the last figure anybody in that harbor has for a barrel of lamp oil with February's above it and both dates on the board, and a figure put on a board cannot be taken off again, and nobody in that street said a figure of oil out loud in this month and no man went to that counter. **THE SHIP'S HAND READ THE LEAF BACK ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING, IN THE OPEN, IN HER OWN LEFT HAND, ALL FOUR COLUMNS INCLUDING THE EMPTY ONE, and the holder stood on the other side of it and did not touch it: the first column has one hundred and thirty-two entries at this hour and one hundred and thirty-three at the close, there were one hundred and twenty-three at the close of Friday the thirteenth and ten have gone in since, one against each of the ten days from Saturday the fourteenth to this day, not one day in two of them, and this evening's own is the tenth; the second column has five hundred and thirty-seven at this hour and five hundred and thirty-nine at the close, four hundred and eighty-nine of them at the close of the thirteenth and five a day since, three before the hour of that day's reading and two after it, three of this day's before this reading and two this afternoon after it, and that figure is that book of that yard's own and is not a count of anything anybody can check from a mole, while the first column's one hundred and thirty-two and the fourth column's one hundred and twenty-four at this hour are a count of entries and of lines, and a day of the first column carries one entry against it whatever else that day printed, so that a stranger with a leaf and a pencil can count both of them, and those are the two definitions and they are printed here so that a later writer with a pencil knows which of them they are counting and at which of the two moments; the third column is empty and nobody has been appointed to it, and the hand of a boy of twenty-two is at the head of it with a name beside it that is not that boy's and is not the holder's, said out loud once in a boat on the thirteenth of May past and not said since, the four lines above his named line are four and nameless and not struck out and are in about sixty boats on that coast, he was not on the stone on any of these ten days and was put on nothing and nobody asked him one word about the three nots standing against the eighth of June past, and no day of any week before the first of July was entered against that line and none is going to be; and the fourth column has one hundred and twenty-four at this hour and one hundred and twenty-five at the close, and the hundred and twenty-fifth is the last thing in that book, and the column is not closed, and nobody has closed it, and nobody in this yard is going to.** She shut it and put it under her own coat and neither of them said one word about the figure it gave. **Then three things were said on that mole head after the reading and nobody asked for any of them.** The first was about the water, and the ship's hand said it: the mark on the face of that mole's second seam is fouled about a foot and seven inches on the weather side and nothing at all on the other side, where it was on the nineteenth of May past, and it was not looked at on any day of this month by anybody; the mark four hundred yards off it is of a make nobody in that harbor makes; the season of both of them is nine marks and neither has been paid and neither is going to be; the whole of the fouling ladder is in another man's own book and nobody has explained it and he is not going to be asked; and no person of that yard was in any stone on any day of this month and none has been in one since the eighteenth of June past. The second was about the harbor, and the woman of no office said it, standing four feet off the stone, and she was not asked for it: there is no flour in that market and there is not going to be any this month, and the cheapest thing in that harbor went up on the first of June and has not come down, and the light is out, and the north berth is out, and the tide gang is four men short, and the hose is dead until the spring, and a cistern is charged on a Monday and a Thursday and walked on by nobody, and a hard at Ashtide is unanswered, and the third lay fills on the first of April and one berth is short and it has been short for four months, and that harbor is poorer tonight than it was in May and it is going to be poorer in September, and nobody in it is going to be told that anybody stopped anything. The third was about that yard, and the holder said it, and he did not look at anybody while he said it: three hundred and twenty-eight pence on the thirteenth and one hundred and sixty tonight, and one hundred and sixty-eight pence is a day at a berth and a day of the man on that stone, and this bag buys one of the two and not the other and not both; the wage of four marks, being six hundred and forty pence, has not been paid for forty-three weeks and not one of the forty-three of them has an envelope against it, the column is at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks with twenty envelopes on a bench in a chest, it does not move tomorrow either and nobody is going to write one word under any of that saying anybody is going to pay it; and the hundred and twenty-fifth line of that fourth column is the last line in that book and the column is not closed and it is not going to be closed by me. **Then he came down the mole at about twenty past five and went up the hill and across to the circuit office, which is a building in that town and is not the office on the west basin and is not the harbor authority, and went into a corridor and stood in it. The corridor was empty. There is a bench at the end of it and a table against the wall and three doors on that corridor and two of them are open and the third one is shut.** The shut one has a paper on it, pinned at the corner, not new, on that door a day or two, not taken down by anybody in that building, and the holder of that writ did not take it down and did not touch it. **It named three people. It said, in three lines, that at the hour named Calder Marr and Mara Venn were permitted in that room, and that at the hour named and for the whole of it Saul Drury, copying clerk of that office, would be present in that room. Under those three lines it said that it was a look at one thing out of three and not a taking, and that nothing was to go out of that room in any hand, and that the hour named on it was the end of it and not the middle of it. The figure on it was a time and a place and an arrival, and it said that the hour was ten in the morning on Tuesday the twenty-fourth day of August, and that the place was this door, and it is the only figure in fifty chapters of that yard that is not a price anybody paid.** The third of the three is not on that paper and is not named on it, and there is a claim against the third in a book in that office that has been there since the December before last, and it has not been withdrawn and nobody in that harbor has asked for it to be withdrawn and nobody is going to. **At the foot of that paper there is a seal line, and the seal line is not the shape of any other seal line the holder of that writ has seen on the face of a paper in that harbor, because the office at the end of it is not one that has ever sent this yard anything. It reads, and it is read out here once and by nobody in that building and by nobody in that harbor: *Sealed and entered at the Morrow circuit office by order of Magister Ilya Serr, Registrar of Recovered Accounts.*** **Nobody was in that room. He did not knock, and he did not open the door, and he did not go in, and he stood in that corridor for about as long as it takes to read nine lines twice and then he went back down the hill and went to his own bench and put the leaf under his own coat where the ship's hand had left it.** Then the whole standing inventory, entered once and nowhere else in that chapter: the oil figure that did not come back down and the light out; the slate and its rule; the bench under that pump at the two hundred and fourth night; the two objects of nobody's at four hundred and thirty-eight days; three marks to a man of Ashtide since the eighth of August past, unmoved and unsent for; seven pence to that yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, the chest not opened, the bellwright not asked in one hundred days, no digit of anything he ever said printed; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure; forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid, not reduced by oil and not paid by a question and not reduced on a mole; forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots of the eighth of June standing unasked for a sixth week, the third column unfilled and unappointed, and a hand at the head of it that is not scratched out; the second seam and its mark four hundred yards off it and the two seasons of nine marks neither paid and the use closed at four figures with no fifth; a page of six names on the crown with a boat as a price and no figure and a stone in one man's own pocket and no boat and no wage and no figure gone to him; six men ashore with no boat and one of them back on the water at a tiller and not at a caulking iron with the top of two fingers of his left hand gone, not paid and not asked to pay; the slip of paper in a drawer, not looked at, not priced, not headed; the two boxes in the office on the west basin; the municipal paper of the eighteenth of July with its door open four days up that coast and nobody at it; **the nine-line sheet with a seal on it in the front street since the fourteenth of August, which nobody there put up and nobody has taken down and nobody there has answered, and which names no person and no harbor and puts no figure on it and has no price at the end of it, and which is true enough on the face of it that nobody who reads it can go up the street and say it is a lie; the custody room with three things in it under three numbers whose digits are on no page, none returned and none asked for, a look at one of the three named on a paper on a door for tomorrow morning at ten o'clock with a man of that office standing in the room the whole time, the room not entered and nothing going out of it; nine communities and six centuries and three hundred years that was not handed to the communities; the notice of the seventeenth of May at ninety-eight days untouched, the fifth clause a breach and the sixth clause free and the sixth clause never once having asked anybody anything; the chandler's note at thirty-one with its three counts and its holder not asked a third time; the delayed note at eleven and two; the four returns and no fifth; the first echo's witness; the day of the first of July past lost with its reason and no name and no figure and no second day entered against that line; the plate in eleven feet with its note open and the only mechanism anybody has named for reaching it a change of politics in an office and not a better letter out of a shed; the case of five bells not raised; the lead plug and the chest and the undertaking not touched; the can upon a stake not on a chart of about nine years and not a route; and the far bench with one shoe beside it that is not his and that has been there since the third of May past, and the holder did not go over to him on any hour of any of the ten days and the yard entered that he did not and that neither brother has said why.** And then the seven boats, and the sheet, and the four refusals with their reasons, and the master of about thirty-three with no papers who came up a hill to say he knew about a day he was not on and was not thanked, and the herring skipper of fifty-one who said no on the fourteenth and again on the eighteenth and was not thanked either time, and about eleven men of a master of about thirty who cannot read the notice and nobody in that harbor has told any of them anything and nobody was sent and nothing was written. **Five of the seven of that Saturday are five boats and a foot. And nobody was hurt on that reach and nobody was named and nobody was counted and no figure of anybody came ashore with that transport and no figure of anybody is on any page of that month, and what is on that reach is a loss of flour and a loss of time and a thing done to a hull, and a squadron that was on that reach has not been seen on it since the twenty-first and has lost a ship out of it, which is not a thing that yard won and did not come into that yard and is not in any return and is not a thing anybody in that harbor is to be pleased about. And the ninety, taken on the fifteenth of June, being the day six men were told to stand by, is at seventy days on the twenty-third of August, and there is no seventy-first day, and this is the last page of that leaf and the column is not closed.**

**THE SHAPE OF VOLUME 08 AFTER FIFTY CHAPTERS OF IT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF IT: FIVE MOVEMENTS ARE PAID AND THE VOLUME IS AT ITS LAST PAGE AND ITS LAST LINE. MOVEMENT 1 PAID AN INSTRUMENT WITH FOUR PRICES ON IT, NINE REFUSALS OUT OF ELEVEN HELD BY THE PEOPLE WHO OWNED THE FOUR THINGS, AND A SQUADRON AT THE OUTER WATER ON THE DAY THE ANSWER WENT. MOVEMENT 2 PAID A ROOM IN WHICH NOBODY WITH A TITLE IS, A CLAUSE THAT HAS NEVER BEEN TESTED AND A DOOR THAT BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT USE IT, A MAN SAYING OUT LOUD WHAT A REFUSAL COSTS, AND AN APOLOGY THAT WAS NOT FORGIVEN AND NOT THANKED AND WAS PAID ONCE. MOVEMENT 3 PAID THE MIDPOINT: ELEVEN WEEKS OF LIFTING UNSEALED TESTIMONY OUT OF CIVILIAN HULLS UNDER A FORM WHOSE OWN WORD FOR IT IS *UNSEALED*, A STANDING INSTRUCTION DATED THE FOURTEENTH OF FEBRUARY, NINETY-TWO DAYS BEFORE THE NOTICE, A BOARD AND A FAIR COPY AND A SLIP OF PAPER WITH A FIGURE AND NO NAME ON IT, AND A COST IN FLOUR. MOVEMENT 4 PAID THE CONDITION AS A BEGINNING AND NOT A STAGE, FOUR THINGS ON A LEAF AND A FIFTH THING THAT IS A PERSON AND IS NOT ON IT, A WAGE AND A DAY AND A MAN WHO IS THERE ON A TUESDAY, SIX MASTERS TAKEN IN ON A PAPERS QUESTION AND ANSWERED ON A LINE THAT ASKED THEM NOTHING, A PAGE ON A MOLE SAID BY THREE MEN OF A LAY, A MUNICIPAL BOX THAT IS NO LONGER EMPTY, AND A PATROL SENT DOWN-COAST BECAUSE OF A TIDE HE CHOSE AND KNEW HE WAS NAMING. AND MOVEMENT 5 PAID THE VOLUME'S WHOLE ARGUMENT IN FOUR MOVES AND IN THIS ORDER: THE CONVOY, being about eleven masters asked one at a time in the same words with a paper between them that names each of them and each of the men aboard, four of whom said no with a reason and a man's day as the cost and no name and no figure against any of them; THE PATROL, being a real attack on a civilian transport carrying flour on the flood he chose, with nobody hurt, nobody named and nobody counted; HIM STOPPING IT, being the work on that reach stopping at about eleven because thirty men had heard a word at the same minute from one mouth, and the man with the board under his arm walking away from it, which is the cost and is not a wound and is not a death; AND THE ADMISSION, said once, in his own voice, on a mole, in about sixty people's hearing, naming the cost, the timing, the two foot that is nobody's arithmetic, the four thousand seven hundred yards that are not an answer, and the harbor that is poorer, and not improved on and not comforted and not thanked. AND THE VOLUME'S LAST PAGE IS NOT A VICTORY AND NOT A DEFEAT: A HARBOR WITH NO FLOUR AND A LIGHT OUT AND A BAG OF ONE MARK AND A WAGE COLUMN FORTY-THREE WEEKS SHORT, A FOURTH COLUMN WITH A HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE LINES IN IT THAT IS NOT CLOSED, A THIRD COLUMN EMPTY AND UNAPPOINTED, A DOOR WITH A MAN STANDING AT IT, A SEAL LINE NAMING AN OFFICE THAT IS IN NO MOUTH, A QUESTION THAT WAS ASKED ONCE AND IS ANSWERED NOWHERE, AND A COAST ROAD THAT IS NOT LOOKED AT. NONE OF THE FIVE MOVEMENTS TOOK A STAGE, THE WORD *KEELWRIGHT* IS IN NO MOUTH ON ANY PAGE OF THE FIFTY, AND A HARBOR POORER ON THE FIFTIETH CHAPTER THAN ON THE FIRST IS THE STANDING CONDITION OF THE WHOLE THING, AND THE CHEAPEST THING IN IT HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE FIRST OF JUNE. THE VOLUME'S NEW SEAL LINE, ITS QUESTION, ITS COST, ITS NEW OFFICE AND ITS LAST LINE ALL STAND WHERE THEY STAND AND NONE OF THEM IS ANSWERED BY ANYTHING THAT HAPPENED ON THAT REACH.**
